member of the commission. - madam president, i am very glad to be here today. it has been a long road – close to five years – but we are almost at the end of our journey. some time ago i could not have imagined i would be standing here at the end of a successful second reading. i want to thank the rapporteur, ms frédérique ries, for her efficient steering. i also thank the shadow rapporteurs for their support during the discussions. these collective efforts helped us to reach the agreement with the council and to complete this task successfully. allow me to recall some facts about gmo cultivation in the european union. currently there is only one gmo authorised for cultivation in the eu. it is cultivated in five member states. nine member states have taken measures to prevent its cultivation in their territory, but these measures have not been considered scientifically justified by efsa. as a result, they are regularly annulled by national judges. this means that the countries wishing to ban gmo cultivation in their territory cannot do so. this is because the current legislation does not allow member states to take into account their national contexts and the views of their citizens. this creates extreme tensions between law, politics and public expectations. eu citizens, farmers and the biotech industry may feel that we do not address their interests. it also weakens the credibility of everyone involved in the process of gmo risk assessment at european level – namely efsa, the member states and the commission. this is why, in 2009, 13 member states asked for a solution. the commission proposed a legally sound and pragmatic response to this call in 2010. it had a dual objective: firstly to maintain a strong science-based eu authorisation system for gmos, securing uniform safety across the european union, and secondly to recognise – in full respect of the treaty – the freedom of each member state to decide whether to allow gmo cultivation in its territory. i am pleased that the text in front of you fully meets these two objectives. member states will have the final say on gmo cultivation, depending on their national situation. the member states that already cultivate gmos will be able to continue. those opposed will be able to restrict or prohibit cultivation in their territory. freedom of choice will be secured. the eu countries that cultivate gmos will have to implement measures to avoid cross-border contamination in neighbouring member states. the criteria used to assess the risk to the environment will be updated shortly. this will reflect the latest scientific and technical progress. let me stress that member states will still be able to adopt measures to address unforeseen risks that may be detected after a gmo is authorised. if you vote in favour of the legislative proposal on gmo cultivation, you will provide the member states with legally-sound tools to decide on gmo cultivation in their territory starting in spring 2015. the eu has repeatedly been asked to do more to live up to citizens’ expectations. i would like to believe this eu legislation is responding to the call. in this context, i would like to make the following declaration: when proceeding with the authorisation of gmos for cultivation, the commission will – in full respect of its obligations – take account of elements at its disposal, including the possibility for the member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos in their territory as provided for by this directive.

madam president! today, there's a very important vote on genetically modified crops. the proposed draft directive allows member states to retain their competence to prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. this is of particular importance for my country, poland, because the great diversity, the biodiversity of agricultural soils in poland and the absence of gmos are a great asset for the promotion of healthy nutrition and the export of very high quality polish agricultural products. our soils are capable of producing natural food, and the use of gmos would inevitably degrade them. fortunately, gmo crops are now banned in poland. poland is and must remain free from the cultivation of genetically modified food. member states have different attitudes towards gmos and the arrangements should be subject to their sovereign decisions.
madam president! the compromise reached on gmo crops allows member states to decide in accordance with their own interests, their specific situation and the opinion of their citizens. it is important to inform the public about what gmos really are and what effects they can have on agriculture, the environment and health. this issue should not be ideologised and politicized, but presented in accordance with the facts, available knowledge and research. the substantive discussion should allow the assessment of the real risks and possible benefits of gmo cultivation. it is a difficult debate and one that is stirring up great emotions in every member state. so, i think that supporting compromise is a way to facilitate internal dialogue and not to create a backlash in the community against a decision that's been imposed from the top down. it is important to emphasise that this compromise makes it easier for member states to ban gmo crops. further research is important as there is no consensus amongst scientists on the benefits and risks. the gmo crops must be completely safe and guarantee that the country where the genetically modified plants are grown will not infect the territories of neighbouring countries, organic and traditional crops. i hope that this approach will allow the politicized discussion to end and the government to make a rational, responsible decision that is best for the people.
madam president! genetically modified crops pose a risk to the environment and to human and animal health. in countries where gm crops have been grown for years, we can see how harmful these crops are, as confirmed by independent scientific studies. nevertheless, companies producing gmo seeds and plant protection chemicals are aggressively lobbying for gmos, seeking new markets, including in europe. the only effective solution is a total ban on gmos throughout the european union. i regret that instead of a ban, they have only worked out an agreement that is far from ideal. on the one hand, it gives member states the theoretical possibility of banning gmos, and i hope that my country, poland, that the government of this country, will take advantage of this possibility. but on the other hand, it opens the door to easy legalization of gmos in the future. the subject of genetically modified organisms should have been the subject of a thorough study by the committee on agriculture, and it was not. people don't want gm food on their plates, so politicians should listen to the public and ban gm food.
in writing. on 13 january 2015, a vote was held on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of seychelles on access for fishing vessels flying the flag of seychelles to waters and marine biological resources of mayotte, subject to the jurisdiction of the european union. given the migratory nature of tuna stocks, this agreement is of strategic importance and will allow the european union to maintain the privileged relationship it has with the republic of seychelles. it is mutually beneficial for the economic development of mayotte and seychelles and respects the principles of the common fisheries policy and the iotc in the area of conservation of resources. i voted in favor of the resolution.

in writing. - the 2011 transport white paper is a very ambitious document focusing on future challenges and initiatives that need to be taken immediately to effectively carry out a deep transformation of the transport system, to create a modern infrastructure and multimodal mobility supported by intelligent management and information systems. the book also sets out the objective of creating a system that is the foundation of economic progress in europe, characterised by a high level of competitiveness and savings. the committee on transport and tourism will shortly be examining the implementation of its objectives. however, it is clear to us today that the old challenges of european transport policy are still relevant and new ones are constantly emerging. the huge delays in the development of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe are keeping europe far from the objectives of the book. only by concentrating investment in the poorest regions will it be possible to build an effective single european transport area. in the hope of obtaining a complete picture of the state of infrastructure and its implications for citizens, i also supported today the request to consult the european economic and social committee on the implementation of the white paper.
in writing. genetically modified crops pose a threat to the environment and to human and animal health. in countries where gm crops have been grown for years, the harmful effects of these crops are already evident, as is also confirmed by scientific studies. people don't want genetically modified food on their plates, so politicians should listen to the public and ban these crops. the only effective solution is a total ban on gmos throughout the eu. i regret that the union has not introduced such a ban. the agreement reached between the european parliament and the council is far from ideal. on the one hand, it gives member states the possibility of banning gmos and i hope that the polish government will use this right. on the other hand, it should be noted that this agreement does not open the door to easier legalization of gmos in the future. i voted in favour of the agreement because it improves the current legal order, which did not allow member states to prohibit these crops on their territory.
in writing. i support the decision of the european parliament to transfer all prerogatives concerning the authorisation of the prohibition of genetically modified crops to the member states. this is the way. it is for the member states alone to decide what is best for them. no more decisions being imposed by the brussels administrative machine. its previous decisions have already led to a crisis in europe. genetically modified crops are still an area of great uncertainty. therefore, member states are best placed to read the minds of citizens and decide whether to admit them. i also oppose all attempts by the european commission to punish countries where uncontrolled dissemination takes place. in conclusion, the less power the european commission has, the better the law in europe.
in writing. allowing member states to decide individually whether to grow gm crops is a wash of hands for the eu institutions and a discharge of responsibility. the european union imports crops, grains and feed from countries where gmos are allowed. the introduction of a ban on gmos in european crops would distort competition between eu growers and those from countries where they are authorised. the free hand of member states in deciding on gmos also distorts competition, including in the internal market. in some countries, gm crops will be grown, increasing yields and reducing costs, while in others, where they are banned, farmers will be less competitive with their neighbours who can use gmos. ordinary farmers will be burdened with the costs of political decisions that are not always backed by science.
in writing. the new gmo rules address member states that have banned or plan to ban the cultivation of genetically modified plants on their territory by providing a proper legal basis and facilitating the decision to restrict or ban gmo cultivation. however, this prohibition shall not apply to scientific research and the marketing of modified seeds. this is important in light of the fact that technologies using genetic engineering are widely used in medicine, in the production of medicines, including insulin, in the study of disease mechanisms, such as cancer, in transplantation and in many other fields. the new rules do not restrict countries that have been and are planning to grow gmos on a large scale. the ban on gmo crops remains a choice, depending on the local environmental situation and social attitudes. gmos are a great hope for humanity, but they also pose certain risks. therefore, the current regulations must be supplemented by national rules that ensure adequate control and safety of production using gmos and guarantee protection against contamination of other products and infection of the territories of neighbouring countries. the new rules will allow countries such as poland, where agriculture is based on traditional, organic farming methods, to exploit the full ecological and health potential of crops. the key is to ensure that healthy food is competitively priced so that it is not a luxury item only available to the richest.
in writing. - the compromise provides that member states may prohibit the cultivation of 'gmos' or groups of gmos on specific grounds. the agreement also introduces mandatory measures for those countries that allow gmo cultivation to protect the border areas of neighbouring countries, unless such measures are not necessary due to geographical conditions. that is why i supported the compromise proposed, which, although far from ideal, provides that member states may decide not to allow the cultivation of gmos in all or part of their territory. member states should be free to decide whether or not to promote agricultural products based on organic farming. for my country - poland - this is a particularly important advantage, as agricultural production can boast healthy, natural food.

in writing. the gfcm's mission is to promote and recommend measures to develop and conserve living marine resources and to promote their wise management in the mediterranean, the black sea and the waters adjacent to these waters. the gfcm recommendations adopted in 2011 and 2012 go beyond the protection already granted to these species at eu level under the habitats directive and other union acts and provide for specific obligations with regard to registration and reporting, so their incorporation into community law will contribute to the sustainable development of the marine environment and fish stocks. however, we must not forget that the interests of fishermen, the fishing industry and coastal communities also need to be taken into account. therefore, i support the rapporteur's proposal to reject those standards in the commission proposal which are more stringent than the gfcm recommendations.

mr. chairman, please! in modern society, the pursuit of full gender equality in the public sector is something that is absolutely natural and necessary. but as far as the private sector is concerned, it is very important to take the specific measures necessary to achieve this noble objective, especially when it comes to doing business. it consists in undertakings acting in their own name, for their own benefit and at their own risk, on the basis of the principles of economy and mutual trust alone. the sacred right of property should be under special protection, the owners must have a decisive influence on the fate of their property and therefore on the way it is managed. i believe that states have the right to establish rules on governance, including the establishment of gender parities, but only in the case of public property. the desire to impose the same rules on the owners of private sector companies must be questionable. i therefore believe that the proposals we are discussing today should be re-evaluated.

in writing. the directive on gender balance among non-executive directors of listed companies, which aims to increase the participation of women in decision-making positions, has been opposed by some countries. the official argument is that the principle of subsidiarity is not applicable and that the legitimate demands for equality between women and men should be implemented at the level of national law. this argument can only be accepted if countries actually have or are preparing their own national solutions and the participation of women in decision-making positions is adequate and proportionate to their qualifications. not all opponents of the directive meet this condition, which calls into question the intentions of the opponents. meanwhile, the waste of women's knowledge and talents is reducing the competitiveness of the european economy. women make up over 60% of master's degrees and 35% of employers, but only a few dozen of them participate in decision-making processes in governments and large companies, and their share of the labour market is much lower than that of men. removing barriers such as gender stereotypes and the shortage of child and dependent care facilities can increase employment rates and improve governance in politics and business, and above all, make full use of the skills and talents of citizens. given the shrinking labour market caused by ageing societies, gender balance is the most important challenge for the modern economy and the key to solving economic and social problems.
the next item on the agenda is the statement by the council and the commission on european measures to combat organised crime and corruption (2015/2510 ((rsp)).
on behalf of the ecr group. - madam president! - i have to go. we're kind of artificially conflating the discussion of corruption with the discussion of organized crime or crime in general. corruption is a separate phenomenon. corruption is a disease and a pathology of power, and we should treat it that way. if the state works properly, if the state institutions work properly, there are no conditions for corruption. there's a saying, "doctor, heal yourself". and when we in the european union talk about corruption, we should look at how our actions work, which take place in the member states, and unfortunately there is often a lack of transparency. transparency is one of the key anti-corruption mechanisms. i myself in poland have a problem with getting information about who used the money from the european union to fight the e. coli bacteria (there used to be such a problem and large compensation). it turns out that eu regulations don't allow that. it's not supposed to be like this! transparency is the most important tool against corruption.
in writing. the european union is increasingly engaged in the fight against corruption, including by implementing the first eu anti-corruption report of 3 february 2014. it would be appropriate to establish definitions of corruption at european and international level, as well as definitions and a system of protection for whistleblowers. these are people who expose to the public the illegal practices of governments, administrations, companies or private associations. we are talking about a passive and active instrument in the fight against corruption. given that reporting of breaches is hampered by a reluctance to report illegal activities within one's own organisation and by the fear of retaliation, i believe that a whistleblower protection scheme (e.g. on the model of the us sarbanes-oxley scheme of 2002) should be established in the eu with a requirement to apply it. an organization to protect these people should also be established. the need for an effective whistleblower protection system has been highlighted by transparency international for years. the european ombudsman also points to the need for a comprehensive and effective system of whistleblower protection in his 2014 publication 'good administration in practice'. this instrument would help to increase the security of potential whistleblowers, raise awareness, and build a culture of integrity in organisations. it would undoubtedly be useful in the fight against corruption in all eu member states.
in writing. the threat of organised crime and corruption are real threats to eu society and the economy. in addition to traditional types of crime, such as money laundering, trafficking in human beings and drug trafficking, new challenges are emerging. the biggest of these are terrorism and the proliferation of cybercrime. the discussions traditionally focus on improvements in crime prevention and law enforcement. this is justified, as there are still considerable reservations in areas of cooperation between the authorities, such as the exchange of information and the transfer of detainees. however, two other areas should be considered. first, cooperation is necessary in the area of confiscation of criminal assets. the point is that criminals cannot profit from their nefarious activities anywhere in any european country. the second problem is to increase the role of europol. there is a debate in the eu about the need to create new institutions to fight organised crime. in my view, it would be simpler and more effective to provide europol with staff, operational and financial support rather than multiplying the number of entities.

the next item is the debate on the question for oral answer addressed to the commission by ms marita ulvskog, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the promotion of financial participation by employees (o-000002/2015 - b8-0103/2015) (2014/2987 (rsp)).
mr. chairman, please! it is becoming increasingly clear that the union has abandoned the idea of its founding fathers of building a social market economy, where not only the costs of the crisis but also the benefits of prosperity are shared by all social groups. today, corporate profits - especially those of multinational corporations - are increasing, and real wages for workers are decreasing. employee financial participation mechanisms or the institution of employee ownership of the enterprise are important ways of tackling this problem. if properly implemented, they can help to address the problem of dramatically increasing social inequalities, while strengthening the links between workers and their workplace. an analysis co-authored by an expert in the field, professor lowitzsch, commissioned by the european commission, found that after 30 years of research into examples of employee financial participation, companies that are partly or wholly owned by their employees generate higher revenues, are more efficient, generate more jobs and pay more taxes than their competitors without this type of financial participation. at the macroeconomic level, these companies achieve higher productivity levels, which also leads to greater competitiveness and growth. at the regional level, they make employee-owned companies more attached to their place of origin, more resistant to external or foreign takeovers. however, we must remember that they also carry significant risks. first, the implementation of these mechanisms in small and micro enterprises needs to be very careful, in writing. ladies and gentlemen! the hague convention on the civil aspects of child abduction has 93 signatory states, including all eu states. i therefore welcomed the accession of russia. the vote was over 90% in favour, which shows the weight of the situation regardless of political views. the convention is the fundamental instrument for ensuring respect for the rights of a child who has been abducted by one of his or her parents. child abduction is a crime, a violation of human rights, guaranteed by the charter of fundamental rights, among others. every year in the european union, we have an average of 3,000 child abductions between eu countries, kidnappings without the consent of the other parent. at the petitions committee, of which i am a member, we receive many reports of child abductions. these cases are among the most emotional. it shows how significant and how common this problem is. the accession of new countries to the convention is good news, and it will lead to more effective investigations of child abduction in the future. finally, i would like to thank the rapporteur for her excellent work.
in writing. the accession of new countries to the hague convention should be welcomed as it increases the emotional security of children and both parents. the hague convention regulates so-called parental kidnapping, where one parent, without the consent and knowledge of the other, takes a child to another country. the convention restores the situation to the state it was in before the abduction, unless it is contrary to the best interests of the child (the child has been adopted into a new environment). the convention also facilitates the establishment of contact between both parents and the child, which is extremely important in view of the child's universal right to contact and education by both parents. the accession of new countries to the convention raised the issue of revising eu rules governing custody and parental responsibility for parents from different eu countries. it is also important to have national legislation recognising parental kidnapping as a crime and ensuring fair child custody processes, allowing for in-depth examination of the child's situation and review of decisions taken in lower courts. in this context, it is worth highlighting the importance of mediation institutions and information campaigns for parents to be aware of the symmetry of their rights and obligations related to the upbringing and care of the child, including the prohibition of leaving the country with the child without the consent and agreement of the other parent.

in writing. the verification of members' seats, which the legal affairs committee is required to carry out under the rules of procedure of parliament, is a formality, a normal administrative procedure of this house, and an opportunity to look in detail at the elections to the european parliament and, drawing attention to the most important problems, to put forward proposals that could contribute to the implementation of the methods of holding them. the communications published by the member states after the elections held in may 2014 included annotations on cases of disenfranchisement of certain citizens. this applies to irish, danish, cypriot, maltese and british nationals living outside their own country. this is a clear violation of the rights of eu citizens (the right to free movement of persons and the right to vote), and it is also completely incomprehensible when we consider the technological possibilities available to almost every european. i subscribe to the rapporteur's call on the commission to eliminate such cases in future and to oblige member states to develop effective voting systems for their citizens abroad.
in writing. the report concerns voting irregularities in european elections in some eu countries. the report calls for the european elections not to be used to disenfranchise citizens who are not in their country of residence at the time of the elections. in this context, it calls on the commission to ensure that no member state allows such a possibility. the report calls on the member states to ensure that registration formalities for citizens of other member states participating in european elections, both as voters and as candidates, are simplified, in particular by removing unnecessary administrative barriers. i voted to accept the report.
in writing. the european system for the exchange of driving data for vehicles with foreign registration plates is a key instrument in the fight against road traffic offences and crimes in the eu. it is primarily aimed at ending the impunity of drivers who break the law outside their own country. the european data exchange system will contribute to improving road safety and will be much more effective than bilateral agreements between member states. this is a major step towards achieving the eu's target of halving the number of road deaths and reducing road injuries by 40% by 2020. progress in this area is particularly important in the face of the effects of the financial crisis in the form of an increase in the number of obsolete vehicles, drastic cuts in infrastructure maintenance expenditure and a lack of funds to finance new facilities. given the seriousness of the subject, we cannot allow a legal loophole to be created in this area, and i therefore support the decision to base the act on the provisions on transport safety rather than on the provisions on police cooperation in criminal matters, because the aim of the directive is road safety and the exchange of information is only a means of action. the extension of the territorial scope of the new law to denmark, the united kingdom and ireland resulting from these changes is also highly desirable as it will ensure the harmonisation of the rules throughout the eu.
in writing. the exchange of information on road safety offences is the culmination of many years of efforts to reduce the number of road accidents, road deaths and injuries and their consequences. the offences are usually cumulative in the individual countries, but without taking into account offences committed on the roads of other countries. in the age of the open and freely accessible road network, this had to change. this report is leading us in that direction. it's in our mutual interest.
in writing. i supported the report on a directive to facilitate the cross-border exchange of information on road safety related offences or offences. in my view, the adoption of this act will effectively reduce the number of offences committed by reckless drivers from other member states. the only reason why they have so far avoided liability is that the law enforcement authorities did not have the data of the owners of cars registered in other eu countries and therefore the proceedings could not be effectively initiated. although attempts have been made to resolve the problem through bilateral agreements, experience has shown that such approaches have caused a great deal of conflict and dissatisfaction between the various traffic control authorities. now, this situation will be resolved by the coming into force of the legislation in question. i am also convinced that they will be effective in improving road safety in the eu and reducing road fatalities.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the exchange of information on road traffic offenders because i believe that transport safety is one of the most important issues that we should address at european level. freedom of movement, which is now a cornerstone of european integration, should also guarantee the possibility of punishing those who break the rules of the road and pose a real threat to the health and life of eu citizens. member states should have effective tools to enforce penalties against non-residents who break national road rules. however, it should be noted that such an act of providing the driver with address and other personal data should take into account all the restrictions related to the exchange and protection of personal data. european regulations should pay particular attention to the confidentiality of the information exchanged in the procedures for the transfer of personal data between the competent authorities of the member states. i'm glad the solution we've adopted provides such protection. at the same time, i would like to express my satisfaction that the member states denmark, ireland and the united kingdom which have so far remained outside the system will become part of it after the transitional periods. i think that's the best indication of how effective this mechanism is. i think it is also worth considering extending these regulations to eu-associated countries, in particular those countries that belong to the eastern partnership.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft agreement and protocol on a partnership on sustainable fisheries between the european union and the republic of senegal. the european union established relations with the republic of senegal in the fisheries area on 1 june 1981 and the renewed protocols concluded in 2002 expired in 2006. the commission has therefore initiated the renewal of the agreement between the republic of senegal and the european union, which has resulted in the proposal for the conclusion of a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement. the appropriate management of the protocol will undoubtedly require clarity and commitment from the parties concerned throughout its life. given the opportunities for senegal's economy to develop through the rational use of available resources, in line with the principles of sustainable fisheries and best industry practices, the new agreement and protocol are mutually beneficial based on available fish stocks and future opportunities for cooperation on other species, and taking into account the opportunity to develop the local fishing industry in partnership with eu vessels, while providing the eu market with high quality fishery products. in addition, the satellite vessel monitoring system and the cooperation between the eu and the republic of senegal on vessel monitoring and tracking in senegalese waters will help the local authorities to step up the fight against illegal and unregulated fishing.
in writing. this fisheries partnership agreement will allow eu vessels to fish in the waters of the republic of senegal. the agreement, which will be concluded for a period of five years, allows the fishing of 14 000 tonnes of tuna and 2 000 tonnes of hake. as with all other fisheries partnership agreements, the agreement includes a commitment to increase local knowledge of fish stocks and to develop strategies for fisheries and the development of the local fishing fleet. i voted for the resolution.
mr. chairman, please! torture is unacceptable and there is no discussion, no debate, no difference of opinion. let no one say we disagree on this, for we do not. i would like to say, as the polish proverb says, not to throw out the baby with the bath, that is, that the justified condemnation of torture and the use of illicit means should not be a pretext for abandoning the fight against islamic terrorists, for abandoning the fight against any kind of terrorism. i want to say this very clearly and very clearly, we condemn torture, but at the same time we must continue to support those who are fighting against a threat that affects our parliament, our citizens, our taxpayers and our voters.
in writing. from its inception, the union was supposed to stand guard over democracy and respect for human rights, freedom and security. and she's always been an ally of the united states in the fight against terrorism. it also reaffirms its commitment to close cooperation in order to prevent acts of terrorism, while respecting the common values. these two facts are not in conflict, but on the contrary, respect for human rights allows us to fight terrorism effectively. the union cannot therefore accept the toleration of methods which are contrary to international law and cannot allow interrogation methods which violate human dignity to be used. support and use of existing tools and organisations that combat breaches of the peace and terrorism should be encouraged.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution because it highlights one of the most important issues facing the world today. terrorism in all its forms and manifestations is one of the most serious threats to peace and security in the world, and the rise of racism is further increasing the sense of insecurity among eu citizens. a comprehensive approach to countering radicalisation and terrorism is therefore necessary. to this end, member states should, in addition to cooperating with each other, cooperate closely with the specialised agencies (eurojust, europol, cepol), making full use of existing capacities and legal and judicial instruments available. the common foreign policy should focus on cooperation with third countries, as these can become important partners in the fight against terrorism. external action to build capacity to counter terrorism and radical propaganda on the internet and other media should be stepped up. the possibility of imposing sanctions on states and governments responsible for the financing of terrorists or terrorist organisations should also be seriously considered.
in writing. i strongly condemn all acts of terrorism, both within europe and beyond. but to counter such acts of violence by force, by retaliating by attacking the countries where terrorists are trained, and by harassing the followers of religions that encourage murder in the name of higher values, is the wrong way to go. the european union is based on democracy and dialogue, and its main idea was to prevent armed conflict. so, remembering why we are united and why we are working together for the freedom and security of europe, let us not encourage violence and discrimination. solidarity and coordination are the basis for effective counter-terrorism. strengthening internal security in the member states will result in a strengthening of internal security in the eu. we must not forget that terrorism is a global threat and that international cooperation is essential to ensure that responses to threats are swift and effective. we as members of the european parliament have a duty to promote the idea of dialogue and equality, while at the same time discouraging radical attitudes and criticising extremist behaviour. very often it is the lack of understanding and mutual respect that leads to acts of violence. let us do everything in our power to counter terrorism with common sense and calm.
in writing. in discussing terrorism and counter-terrorism, i wanted to highlight the huge role of education, which is not adequately highlighted in counter-terrorism strategy and measures. the protection of external borders, the exchange of data, cooperation between countries and the safeguarding of internal security are undoubtedly key elements in the fight against terrorism. we must remember, however, that the threat of terrorism is not limited to the middle east. more and more young europeans are embracing very radical views and are willing to kill to defend their values. that is why it is so important that we focus on working with young people, on teaching tolerance, respect for other cultures and religions, a culture of discussion and communication. schools are a key element in preventing and countering radicalisation. it's supposed to be a double feature. on the one hand, to instill in young people the ideas of tolerance, integration, dialogue, respect and cultural diversity, and on the other to be sensitive to the emergence of very radical attitudes among young people. good communication between school, pupil and parent, taking into account the cultural specificities of young people, is a key prerequisite for countering their radicalisation. it should be emphasised, of course, that this challenge of indirectly combating extremism does not lie solely with teachers. on the contrary, it requires the involvement of the media, ngos and experts from the local communities to be effective.
in writing. i welcome the vote to extend the mandate of the internet governance forum for another five years. the forum's mission is not yet complete and i am glad that most of the members are aware of this. the internet is a public space, by its very nature free and open to all. it's good for democracy, good for cultural diversity, good for the economy. it's the impetus for innovation and all kinds of exchanges. it is intended to serve the eu's digital single market. the internet is a collaborative, trust-based system, and it needs clear rules. the growth of the internet economy is forecast to be almost 11% in the eu. in turn, the share of this economy in gdp is expected to increase from 3,8% in 2010 to 5,7% in 2016. the resolution stresses that 2015 will therefore be a pivotal year for internet governance. the internet is a global resource and should never be monopolized by any single group. it cannot be held hostage by particular economic or political interests. its enormous potential must be harnessed to ensure the trust of its users by processing their personal data in a secure manner. the internet governance forum, which is a continuation of the mandate of the world summit on the information society, is designed to serve the network security.
in writing. eu citizens want and have a right to know where their meat and processed products come from. consumers don't want to have horses on their plates instead of beef, genetically modified meat or meat from cloned animals. therefore, the voice of the public should be heard and the mandatory indication of the origin of meat should be introduced in order to restore consumer confidence in the sector. systematic food quality control is also essential for the rights and health of eu citizens. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the commission should make a new legislative proposal on this matter. the solution proposed by the commission must also take into account the need to minimise the additional financial burden on producers and consumers.
in writing. i do not support the text of the resolution drafted by the envi committee, which calls on the european commission to adopt legislation introducing the obligation to indicate the origin of meat contained in processed food. the new act would significantly increase the cost of producing meat products, as labelling would have to include both the place of birth of the animal, its rearing and its slaughter. as 90% of refineries are small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), the new rules would have a negative impact on the generation of growth, the creation of jobs and the competitiveness of the european economy. it is estimated that administrative costs would increase by 30% and products containing processed meat would increase by 5-9%. contrary to the assumptions of the rapporteurs, the introduction of the mandatory labelling will not solve the problems of food adulteration, such as the recently revealed practices of replacing beef with horse meat. the appropriate action is to increase the frequency and intensity of checks. in those circumstances, the commission should not submit legislative proposals in this area. i believe that the existing voluntary labelling system is sufficient and that the possibility of introducing such an obligation should be left to the member states. although i am a strong advocate of a culture of conscious food choice, the costs of the proposed changes seem to far outweigh the potential benefits. however, for the avoidance of doubt, i support the rapporteur's call on the european commission to resolve as soon as possible the discrepancies in the results of the study on the price effects of the introduction of this act.
in writing. opponents of the introduction of the indication of the origin of meat argue that this will increase the costs for businesses that produce processed food, which is linked to a number of different costs arising from the need to include and update information on the origin of the meat ingredients in processed products on food labels. research shows that the vast majority of consumers are interested in information about the place of origin and even the 'journey' the meat has taken from the place of farming through the place of slaughter and processing. proponents of labeling argue that the cost will not increase as the studies show. it is worth considering whether the place of origin clause will eliminate the occasional scandal and misuse in the food industry - probably not, but there is a chance that it will reduce them, introduce greater transparency and a sense of security, which is what consumers expect. we also do not know exactly what the 'country of origin' of the meat is. is it the country where the animal was born, or is it the place where it was slaughtered? in conclusion, consumer opinion surveys are insufficient in this respect. the preparation of appropriate solutions before legislative work requires further analysis and research, both on the part of the processing industry and on the part of the consumer.
in writing. the problem of food labelling fraud, exemplified by the recent horse affair, has led to increased consumer awareness and interest in the origin of meat and meat products. therefore, the mandatory indication of the country of origin of meat is a good step towards restoring consumer confidence in the sector and may meet their expectations to choose better labelled products. the obligation to label processed meat applies both to the country of origin of the animals and to the country where the meat was last processed. the obligation applies to all types of meat except beef which is already covered by such a scheme. i voted in favour of the resolution calling on the commission to put forward its own proposals on this matter.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr goerens. i am convinced that an open, structured dialogue between the european union and the acp states is urgently needed today and that the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly is the perfect forum for this. i also agree with the rapporteur, mr goerens, who stresses, among other things, the key role of local authorities in the preparation and monitoring of national and regional strategy papers and in the implementation of the european development fund. i believe that regional authorities should be one of the key partners in the drive to reduce poverty and achieve sustainable development. after all, they are the ones who are leading the way in solving local problems, such as food security, social exclusion, infrastructure, rapid urbanization and many others. in my work in the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly, i would like to pay particular attention to this issue.

first vice-president of the commission. - mr president, this debate is about the way forward for frontex and the european asylum support office – at least that is what i thought it was, but it has become a debate about much more than that. it has become a debate about what is arguably one of the biggest challenges european societies have faced, and will face, for perhaps a generation. migration is an issue with daunting complexity – all sides of the migration issue – and therefore i would warn against politicians who have very simple, one-dimensional solutions to such a daunting challenge. frontex is not going to solve this; the office is not going to solve this; just building ever-stronger borders is not going to solve this; putting an end to free movement is not going to solve this. if i were a father with children in homs or in damascus and i wanted my children to survive a terrible war and therefore i would try and flee to europe, do you think that, for one second, i would ask myself, ‘is there free movement in europe or is there not?’ no! i would look for a way to save my children, and i think that is completely justified. we would kill the fundamental values we share as europeans if we would deny people the right – if they have to flee – to flee to a safe haven. but that is not the only dimension of this issue. the other dimension is that this is also an economic activity exploited by very dangerous criminals. so you cannot have the naive answer of saying: just let everybody in. just imagine what would happen to our inner cities if we were to have a completely open-door policy in terms of migration. just look what would happen to the fabric of our societies if we were to do that. so there is no room for being naive. this is not a conspiracy of big corporations in a capitalist world to create migration flows. come on, let us not try and sell people this sort of nonsense. this is a consequence of the world as it is today, with many facets. that is why the commission will present a holistic approach to the migration issue, because at the same time europe is struggling with illegal immigration, it is struggling with the need for solidarity between european nations in tackling the issue of illegal migration and asylum seekers. but at the same time, europe will need migration for our economy, for our sciences, for the structure of our societies. europe is in a demographic place where we will have fewer people in europe without immigration over a longer period of time, and our economy will ask for people to come for a while and work here and then go back or not, etc. so we need to have a clever policy that addresses all these issues, and that is why the commission will come up with a holistic migration policy. it is part of our working programme. it is one of our absolute priorities. as part of that, we will have to look at the way forward with frontex and the european asylum support office. these two organisations are part of the solution, but not the only part. frontex needs to be strengthened. i do not think at this stage that the finances are the most acute problem but, if they are, on a year-to-year basis the commission has always made sure that we had enough financing for frontex. i do think that; but if you were to ask me what i am going to do to ensure more solidarity between member states, this, to a large extent, is a matter for discussion between the member states. this is not a competence of the commission or even of the european union. you know, if you have seen the reports of the informal measures to fight these phenomena. we should all continue this work. the union has numerous tools that should be more intensively applied and, where necessary, adapted to new realities. for example, frontex could make use of the common application tools offered by the european border surveillance system (eurosur) to enable selected monitoring of designated pre-frontier areas at the external borders, which have been identified through risk analysis and information as being potential departure or transit areas for illegal immigration or cross-border crime. there is also potential for more intensive inter-agency cooperation – for example, ensuring that europol is made aware swiftly of all information useful in the fight against smugglers that is gathered at the eu borders by member states’ surveillance services. cooperation is also working well under the recently concluded service-level agreement between frontex and the european maritime safety agency. i would also like to mention the actions included in the operational action plan on illegal immigration of the eu policy cycle, which aim to combat criminal groups organising the smuggling of immigrants. the european asylum support office (easo) can cooperate with frontex in relation to reinforced management of the eu’s external borders. easo could coordinate the screening of immigrants in mixed flows by identifying those in need of international protection and those who have special needs, including vulnerable persons; and by providing information, easo could contribute to catering for their needs upon disembarkation. furthermore, enhanced inter-agency cooperation between easo, frontex and europol could be important in the fight against smuggling and in the identification of facilitators. easo could also, for instance, contribute by gathering information on facilitation during the asylum decision process. we might also ask what easo can do in relation to unaccompanied minors. easo already takes action to support member states in the implementation of the common european asylum system in relation to children, including unaccompanied minors. these actions take into account the general work on child protection and the protection of the rights of children carried out inter alia by the commission and the fundamental rights agency. concrete easo deliverables so far include the publication of a report on age assessment and the organisation of a meeting of experts on family tracing. in the coming years, easo should continue to provide support and develop practical cooperation tools on issues relating to children and unaccompanied minors. further to remarks made in the discussion, i have a few points. first, on budget resources: easo and frontex operate within the new multiannual financial framework, including within the bounds of the new asylum, migration and integration fund and the internal security fund. for the period 2014-2020 this financial framework provides the basis for eu financial support on asylum, migration and borders, including allocations to eu agencies. as a consequence, any choice to have easo and frontex intensify their existing tasks or taking up new tasks will require either the allocation of additional means to these agencies within the financial framework or prioritisation in the agencies’ work plans. both in the council and in the european parliament, the executive directors of easo and frontex have highlighted the need to match expectations with funds. secondly, at the moment external evaluations of both easo and frontex are being conducted. when ready, the evaluations should provide important input for discussion on the role and tasks of these agencies in the coming years. honourable members, several remarks have been made about the efficiency of the european asylum system. in this regard, i must note that the new legislative instruments of the common european asylum system will come into force this summer. this means that we will first have to assess the impact of these instruments. only then, in the light of the results of that assessment, could the issue of mutual recognition be discussed. we will have to see if sufficient mutual trust exists among member states to introduce a mutually recognised eu protection status. easo could provide important input for that discussion. as co-legislators we will be called on to agree how easo and frontex should further contribute to successful eu migration and asylum policies. today’s debate provides important input for mapping the way forward. in doing so, it is our common responsibility to match means and expectations and to continue giving both agencies our full support.

in writing. the union needs instruments to stimulate long-term investment, including for large infrastructure projects. however, from the outset, the commission's legislative proposal on european long-term investment funds raised legitimate doubts. first of all, the commission was accused of having conducted a cursory public consultation and of not having taken into account all stakeholders. the main complaint was that the draft regulation submitted was imprecise and confusing. the proposed changes seem to have removed these doubts. another important complaint was that the prohibition on the pre-mortem disposition of shares could have reduced the attractiveness of the funds, especially among retail investors. the proposed changes seem to be moving in the right direction. on the one hand, the prohibition remains in force ensuring the stability of financing and planning with these funds and on the other hand, the possibility of the withdrawal of shares is allowed if the fund manager establishes a specific withdrawal policy that takes into account the interests of all parties. unfortunately, another major problem concerning the maturity adjustment principle introduced by the regulation has not been resolved. many experts point out that this may reduce profitability and thus the attractiveness of the funds, primarily because of the risk of reaching prices that are unsatisfactory to investors. it is highly likely that they will compensate themselves with the expected interest on the loans granted, thus increasing the cost of the investment.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it will harmonise the rules on the limitation of transaction fees. currently, interchange fees for processing card-based transactions vary between eu countries, where they are subject to legislation in some cases and administrative decisions in others. the fees are levied by banks belonging to so-called 'quadrilateral' systems, in which the card-issuing bank, the merchant-handling bank, the merchant and the card user are involved and together control a significant part of the market. merchants pay for each transaction with a card and add these costs to the prices of goods and services offered. in supporting the adoption of this report, i believe that the fees charged by banks for handling card payments made at points of sale will be reduced throughout the eu. the cap on fees applies to both domestic and cross-border payments, which should result in lower costs for payment card users. the new legislation should improve the transparency of charges, increase competition and allow not only traders but also customers to choose the system offering the best conditions.

the rapporteur. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. europe needs growth. without a return to sustainable growth, we will not be able to cope with the debt burden, reduce unemployment, finance important social needs and, above all, restore our people's faith in the sense of a united europe. we're not gonna restore hope for a better future. we're all tired of the long crisis. production in the european union only last year reached its pre-crisis level of 2008. so, we can talk about six years wasted. there are different opinions on the causes of this long-term stagnation. we often hear, even in this chamber, that the main cause of the economic collapse is budgetary austerity, that it has led to mass unemployment and falling incomes. we don't share those views. the budget cuts were a necessary response to the excessive spending before the crisis, spending that led to uncontrolled debt growth. the fundamental cause of the current difficulties has been the irresponsible fiscal policies of governments and the equally irresponsible credit policies of banks in some countries. it could have been avoided, because there was no obligation to go into debt. however, in 2014 there were signs of economic recovery. after a two-year period of decline, the gross domestic product of the european union rose by 1.6% and is forecast by the european commission to accelerate to 2.1% next year. these data confirm that the difficult fiscal consolidation and structural reforms undertaken in many member states are delivering the desired results. countries under adjustment programmes, such as ireland and portugal, have been able to rebuild their financial credibility, and ireland is the fastest growing economy in the union. however, the foundations of economic growth remain fragile. further action is urgently needed to strengthen macroeconomic stability, create jobs, accelerate investment and improve the competitiveness of european economies. the european commission's annual growth survey is a document that proposes such actions. the commission proposes an integrated approach to growth based on three pillars. these are the investment support programme of the european fund for strategic investments, growth-friendly fiscal consolidation and the necessary structural reforms. the investment pillar aims not only to create a fund with an investment potential of over eur 300 billion, but also to be a confidence-building instrument for private investors. growth-friendly fiscal consolidation aims to strengthen public finances and restore the ability of indebted countries to raise funds on the market. it also aims to protect public investment, especially in areas such as infrastructure, education and healthcare. finally, structural reforms are aimed at modernising european economies: improving competitiveness through labour market reform, removing barriers in product and service markets and creating favourable conditions for business, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises. however, not all agree with these proposals. there are ideas to get out of the crisis by going into debt. in this context, it is proposed to relax the eu's fiscal rules and to suspend structural reforms. mr. chairman, please! we don't agree with those ideas. we consider them frivolous and irresponsible. their implementation would deepen the crisis and threaten the integrity of the euro area. the obvious question is, where will the money come from to finance the next debt? we therefore support the commission's position that these three areas of action should be among the priorities of the economic policy of the member states for the coming years in the next cycle of country-specific recommendations. we also stress the need for the member states to be fully involved in these priorities. it cannot be that when it comes to difficult decisions, difficult reforms, individual governments shift the responsibility onto brussels. we expect national authorities, governments and parliaments in the member states to fully identify with the reforms and take responsibility for their implementation. the european union cannot be treated like a bad cop. we all have a responsibility for europe.
mr. chairman, please! both mr rosati and mr prieto have pointed out in their reports to the democratic deficit. in his report, mr rosati calls on the commission to make the necessary proposals to tackle the problem of democratic accountability in the application and accountability of the institutions in economic governance. i do not know how the commission would do that. the governance of the single market in the european semester necessarily limits the role of national parliaments in shaping member states' budgets. this is particularly the case for euro area debtor countries and non-euro area countries that are dependent on the inflow of union funds. it puts decisions in the hands of anonymous officials or experts, and it undermines democracy, which is only alive at the level of nation states. so democracy is replaced by technocracy. i think we need to move away from the idea that centralization, that putting decisions in the hands of officials, even competent officials, is a guarantee of economic rationality, and democracy is a disruption.

rapporteur.– mr president, let me first express my thanks for the debate we have had in this house: i would like to express my thanks to all the colleagues who participated in the debate and especially to the shadow rapporteurs, with whom i had very fruitful cooperation throughout the whole period of preparing the report. of course, we did not agree on everything, but i appreciated their readiness to find reasonable compromises. now, on the debate, i would like to refer briefly to three points. the first is the recurring theme of austerity. many colleagues complained that austerity is creating ruin in their countries’ social models. well, let me remind you once again that austerity measures were simply a necessary reaction, a necessary adjustment to the excessive spending in the period before the crisis. all those countries which had irresponsible budget policies had, of course, to make some cuts, and that is nothing to complain about. those countries which were prudent in their budgetary policies have not had to resort to austerity. the second point i would like to refer to is the social cost involved in these structural reforms. i very much share the view that there have been social costs involved with fiscal consolidation and reforms. nevertheless, we have to remember that if wages were growing at a pace much higher than productivity before the crisis, then there is a need for those wages to come down. so we should not be surprised that, in some countries, wages and incomes have had to come down, simply in order to stay in line with productivity. lastly, as to the point about bureaucrats in brussels who allegedly imposed restrictions on our countries: this is simply not true. all the member states agreed on the fiscal rules, and the bureaucrats in brussels are merely responsible for enforcing them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean. the amendment of the gfcm agreement was initiated in 2013. following the review of the results of the action, completed in 2011, it was concluded that the agreement should be amended to clarify its objectives and functions and to enhance its effectiveness. the overall objective of the present agreement is the biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources. the main tasks of the commission will be to promote the development, conservation, rational management and optimum use of living marine resources, as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and the black sea. the document also sets out clear rules governing the dispute settlement mechanism in case of disputes between the parties to the contract. the new agreement integrates the key elements of the common strategy on maximising sustainable fishing, protecting the ecosystem, reducing discards and combating illegal and unregulated fishing, which will help to make the common fisheries policy more effective.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission / high representative.– mr president, you held a very fruitful and comprehensive debate on the panzeri report yesterday. i am honoured to present to you now the eu priorities for the un human rights council in geneva, which resumed its work last week. this debate gives us the opportunity to publicly renew our commitment to a strong multilateral human rights system. the european union has been a staunch supporter of the human rights council from the very beginning, and over the years we have contributed to strengthening its capacity to address violations and to promote greater respect for human rights all over the world. for this reason, it was particularly important for the vice—president / high representative to participate in this high level segment last week. her presence in geneva, together with the eu special representative stavros lambrinidis, was meant to remind the world, but also ourselves, of the great importance which is accorded to human rights in eu foreign policy. she also wanted to give voice to the work that the eu does and which this house does to uphold human rights worldwide. the council is the place where the gravest human rights violations are publicly condemned and where new partnerships can be forged with countries from all regions to take resolute action to prevent and respond to human rights violations and abuses, and to fight discrimination and violence. unavoidably, the debate in geneva is very much focused on the many human rights crises resulting from ongoing conflict or fragility. your resolution refers to a number of them, and they correspond to the situations that the vice—president/high representative highlighted at the council last week. firstly, the eu condemns the serious deterioration of the human rights situation in ukraine, where the price paid by the civilian population is simply appalling – almost 6 000 people have been killed and twice as many have been injured – and where the tatar community in crimea is persecuted and journalists and the media are intimidated. together with partners, the eu strongly calls for an end to violations and abuses, for respecting international human rights and human rights law, for granting safe passage and for allowing the release of hostages and detained persons. the eu supports the work done by the un human rights monitoring mission in ukraine, which is documenting violations and will guarantee the accountability of those who have perpetrated them, and calls for unimpeded access to the mission to crimea. secondly, in syria, entire communities, women and children, are taken hostage both by a brutal regime and by ruthless terrorist groups who wage a war under the false pretence of protecting their religion. the eu supports the work of the commission of inquiry set up by the human rights council since we know from experience that restoring justice to the victims of atrocities is crucial to achieving sustainable peace and reconciliation. moreover, where impunity prevails, there we find disaffection and alienation – feelings which are exploited by extremists. the result is a spiral of violence and destruction which is difficult to control. this is why, when the time comes, we will support also the role of the icc in addressing these violations. third, finally let me mention south sudan, a country we will discuss afterwards and where the conflict spares no one, not even young children. here the eu urges the african union peace and security council to consider the report of the african union commission of inquiry. again, justice and accountability are vital elements in the reconciliation process for the country. human rights are not only violated in situations of conflict. the eu also deems it important to shed light on long—standing and grave human rights violations or accompany countries in transition to democracy. therefore, we again are a partner with japan to bring international attention to human rights in the democratic people’s republic of korea – a situation which the general assembly last december, on our initiative, recommended to the attention of the un security council with the request that it should consider a referral to the international criminal court. like you, we have not forgotten the situation in myanmar/burma where progress has been made indeed but where, at the same time, we continue to be concerned about the inter—communal violence towards the roghingya and by the situation in conflict-affected areas and by the possible adoption of legislation on the protection of race and religion. moreover, the european union continues to work to bring attention to the rights of children, who are our future but who are all too often the first victims of conflict or crisis. we are the long-standing sponsor of resolutions on the rights of the child, both in geneva and new york, and support in particular the protection of children from war, violence and abuse. last, but not least, let me mention the eu’s commitment to freedom of religion or belief on which we are going to table a resolution at this session. we have also just hosted, on tuesday 10 march 2015, a successful event with un special rapporteur bielefeldt on the timely subject of speaking out against acts of intolerance, discrimination and violence allegedly committed in the name of religion or belief. this is a complex phenomenon which requires a firm response by states, regional organisations, religious or belief communities, ngos and by media representatives. let me say in this respect that realising all human rights for all and fighting marginalisation, discrimination and intolerance is the european answer to radicalisation, violence and abuse. before closing let me mention three issues of particular importance to this house. firstly, as you rightly point out in your resolution, civil society representatives and human rights defenders experience harassment and imprisonment, threats and violence as well as restrictions on their activities in many countries around the world. the eu defends their space at the united nations and raises their plight in bilateral dialogues. we now go beyond traditional diplomatic or political tools, together with the high commissioner for human rights and the brazilian permanent mission to the united nations, the republic of korea and tunisia. in geneva we have just launched an innovative social media campaign called ‘#i defend’ making sure civil society has its voice. with this initiative we want to express support to, and solidarity with, human rights defenders and civil society representatives. secondly, we must lead by example. our collective commitment to the universal peer review or principal decision to cooperate with all special procedures of the united nations are extremely important for our credibility and for the credibility of the human rights council. this also means bringing human rights back home and vigorously working on our own shortcomings. in her speech in geneva the high representative has openly spoken about the challenge of migration and the eu’s commitment to better protect the human rights of migrants in the future through deeper cooperation among the eu member states and support for the work of the unhcr. third and finally, let me recall that the credibility of the un human rights systems rests primarily on the independence and integrity of the office of the high commissioner. we must defend this independence by supporting the office financially and by staving off attempts to place its activities under the scrutiny of member states. i would like to thank you for this debate and for the recommendations regarding the eu priorities.

on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the displacement of people, environmental migration is taking on a massive character in tanzania. most of the displacement observed affects the poorest and most marginalized members of the population. communities particularly affected by the consequences of illegal displacement are those without formal land rights. the lack of these rights is often the reason for the denial of compensation related to resettlement, which violates human rights standards. tanzania's weakness is that it lacks many legal acts. i condemn the illegal evictions of people, discrimination in property rights and violation of fundamental human rights related to the illegal land grabbing of the local community. the lack of transparent information on the number of investments in tanzania is a concern. i call on the tanzanian authorities to promote an agricultural policy that benefits the local population and to implement land ownership laws to protect this community. i stress the importance of adequate compensation in accordance with the real value of previously occupied or used land.
mr. chairman, please! land grabbing is a serious problem in many african countries, including tanzania. it is primarily about the loss of the rights of the local community to land, water and other natural resources. in recent years, there has been a new wave of large-scale land acquisitions, driven by the growing global demand for raw materials, agricultural products, biofuels and tourism. however, land acquisition does not guarantee development, for example most of the investments in biofuels between 2003 and 2008, for which 640 hectares were allocated, failed. in tanzania, 75% of the population are farmers, but only 10% of them have formal certificates of ownership of the land they cultivate. widespread corruption and abuse of power by politicians and government officials have resulted in the seizure of local farmland by foreign investors, and the forced migration of people who lack access to natural resources in search of food and water. the tanzanian government should support investments that benefit the local community, and we as the european union should pursue a policy of dialogue, trade and monitoring of european companies' operations in this part of the world, with a view to addressing local woes.

mr. chairman, please! today, instead of discussing rational solutions in accordance with the overriding provisions of the treaties, we are basing our debate on the undefined concept of social dumping, which is the pretext for introducing protectionist legislation that violates the fundamental principle of freedom to provide services and provides for disproportionately high penalties and administrative burdens for carriers from other countries in any situation: transit, international transport or cabotage. i would point out that a competitive advantage based on lower labour costs, organisational efficiency and labour productivity cannot be equated with social dumping. we know that lower labour costs are due, among other things, to differences in the level of economic development of individual countries, but also to differences in social security systems, in the level of contributions paid by companies. therefore, there is no social dumping, as no company can afford to operate below cost. today, none of us is questioning the right of any member state to introduce a minimum wage in its own country. however, the problem is the scope of application of the rules on that salary to persons employed in other member states and its compatibility with the freedom to provide services in the internal market. in view of the chaos and legal uncertainty created by the recent german legislation, we are today asking the european commission for a clear and unambiguous answer: to what extent should the german national law on minimum wages be applied to foreign transport operators, while not conflicting with european union law and the national law of the other member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the annual report on taxation. tax policy, by safeguarding our revenue base, is an essential part of fiscal stability. urgent, coordinated and coherent action is needed to eliminate tax evasion, tax fraud and tax avoidance, and to combat aggressive tax planning and tax havens, using a common approach that should be implemented not only at european but also at global level. the promotion of effective tax coordination should be the main instrument for shaping tax policies that stimulate growth, employment and investment. this is important to maintain transparent and fair tax competition between member states, which is favourable to growth and employment. effective, efficient and sound national tax policies require the proper functioning of national tax authorities. it is also important to exchange information between national tax authorities on best practices in order to learn from each other. tax policy is essential not only for the social security of families and households, but also for competitiveness and job creation.
