rapporteur.– madam president, this multi-species plan has been long awaited. i believe this approach is much more effective than management based on a single species. it aims to take account of interspecies interactions, such as the influence of the cod stock on herring and sprat stocks, and the other way around. the plan should provide for a balanced, sustainable exploitation of these stocks and for the stability of fishing opportunities and thereby the livelihoods of fishers. at the same time, it should guarantee that management is based on the most up-to-date scientific advice regarding the status of the stocks covered, interactions between species and other aspects related to the ecosystem and fisheries. the most controversial part of this dossier concerns the scientific advice, namely target fishing mortality ranges as set out in article 4 and article 5. to explain to our non-fisheries members, those ranges will indicate how much fish fishermen will be allowed to fish. obviously the smaller the range of values, the smaller the amount of fish; and the broader the range, the more flexibility for the sector from one year to another. values in the commission’s proposals are provided by the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices) which is the scientific advisory body of the commission. these figures are advised after careful analysis of all available data and applying scientifically reviewed and tested models. some may say that the values of those ranges provided by the commission were not in line with the reformed common fisheries policy (cfp). frankly, that is partly true. they are not yet in line, but only because we have until 2020 to reach the targets set out in the reform. the basic regulation says: ‘in order to reach the objective of [...] restoring and maintaining populations of fish stocks above biomass levels capable of producing maximum sustainable yield, the maximum sustainable yield exploitation rate shall be achieved by 2015 where possible and, on a progressive, incremental basis at the latest by 2020 for all stocks.’ so we have five years to fulfil the obligation of the reform of the cfp. while setting fishing mortality targets, we should also take into account the most recent scientific advice. let us not forget that we are politicians; we are not scientists. we should not play around with arbitrary formulas. we should listen to the scientists and wisely use their advice. at the same time, i want to dispel some doubts. it is probable that future plans will be modelled on the baltic plan, but only in terms of structure. in terms of content, the principle of regionalisation will be applied. therefore what we adopt for the baltic cannot be copied for the mediterranean or the north sea. this also includes the targets. however, on the contrary, accepting arbitrary formulas would create a very dangerous precedent. this means that such an approach would also be used in other future plans for the north sea or the mediterranean sea. how are we going to explain this to the fishermen? many amendments have been tabled asking to follow the most scientific advice and this is exactly what i try to do. i want to use the fmsy (fishing mortality consistent with maximum sustainable yield) figures advised by the scientific body, ices, wisely. finally, i would also like to underline that i am against including seabirds and sea mammals in the text of the fisheries management plan because we have different legislation for that. let us not experiment with the baltic. let us follow science. let us not mix the legislation and let us not confuse politics with science.
on behalf of the ecr group. i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur on his hard work in preparing this report. it offers a last chance to restore the baltic's resources and ensure proper conservation. it should be recalled that, until now, sprat, for example, has been treated as a pest, adversely affecting the cod population by feeding on its eggs. it was fished uncontrollably for industrial purposes. this has disrupted the food chain and led to a collapse in the cod and pelagic stocks. the only way to restore the baltic's resources is to temporarily stop all fishing and introduce protection and compensation schemes for fishermen. this is the only way to guarantee and preserve fisheries, especially family-owned fisheries, while at the same time guaranteeing their development. in the light of the disastrous policy pursued so far, the european union has a responsibility to protect the environment and to support fisheries, especially family-owned fisheries.
rapporteur.– madam president, i would like to thank everyone for their contribution throughout the process of our work and in today’s debate, even those with whom i strongly disagree. i would like to remind you of a very important point. i believe we have to stay true to our word, the word we gave last year when we voted in the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). in it we understood and we agreed that we should reach certain levels, levels of fmsy (fishing mortality consistent with maximum sustainable yield), levels above msy, and those levels should be reached by the year 2020. starting from this year, we should do our best to work in a correct manner in a steady process of ensuring that those levels are reached. i believe that by tabling certain amendments we are trying to achieve something right now – this year – which is going against the word we have given to the fishermen. please remember that the common fisheries policy and this multiannual plan and all other multiannual plans are there to create a more stable framework for the future of the fishermen. when we pass certain legislation in this house they have to believe that we want to do everything in our power to ensure that there is plenty of fish in the sea and there remains plenty of work for them to do. and as such i would like to ask you to support my amendment tomorrow on the ranges from 0 to fmsy, with the note that we will do everything in our power to reach levels below fmsy as soon as possible. please remember also that this dossier contains a revision clause which is supposed to be applied in three years’ time, so even if we reach the levels by then we still have two more years to reach the levels that are in agreement with the basic regulations. please support me tomorrow and once again thank you very much for your help.
ladies and gentlemen! eliminating discards is a pillar of the reform of the common fisheries policy. it is estimated that this practice accounts for 23% of the total catch. the fight against discards is a priority for us and fishermen will have to land all commercially valuable species caught. it is good that this obligation applies both to fish below the minimum conservation reference size and to fish caught after or without fishing quotas. this will result in more reliable stock data, better management and more efficient resource management, and above all, end unnecessary waste. i congratulate the rapporteur. you have my full support.

and the european commission for the effective work they have done together on this report. the bologna process is an attempt to organise the higher education system in europe in such a way that it becomes universally understood, accessible, trustworthy, and at the same time remains diverse or even proud of its diversity. our report focuses on the evaluation of this process, the issues that need to be improved and the new challenges that this process faces, such as youth unemployment, the economic crisis and demographic change. although the bologna process has achieved a great deal over the past 15 years in terms of quality of education, mobility, recognition of academic diplomas, there are still many areas where urgent action is needed. we believe that it is necessary to consistently implement the jointly agreed reforms in the countries of the european higher education area and to strengthen the bottom-up approach. it also requires a greater focus on the student. the learning outcomes are what the graduate knows and can do, not necessarily how they learned it. we also need clear and transparent communication on the bologna process to raise awareness and support for higher education reforms among citizens. there is no doubt that the recognition of qualifications acquired abroad, periods of study abroad and prior education should be improved. this would directly benefit the students. it should be possible for any student studying in any country of the european higher education area to have his or her qualifications recognised throughout the european union. to achieve implementation of national qualifications frameworks. improving the quality of higher education and establishing quality assurance systems is a major priority for many countries. the challenge for the bologna process remains to further enhance social inclusion and equal opportunities in access to education and international mobility of under-represented and disadvantaged groups. it is also important to strengthen the links between higher education and scientific research by facilitating dialogue between academia and society and promoting the beneficial application of technological innovation in teaching and learning. continuous investment, more efficient use of available funds and the development of new financing models are needed. the objectives of the process cannot be achieved without adequate funding for higher education. the bologna process is not just a 3+2+3 system, but a series of parities that must lead to the creation of a european higher education system. in writing. ‒ it is estimated that the introduction of e-call will reduce the number of deaths by around 2500 each year. the system will automatically connect to the nearest emergency call centre via the mobile phone network, even when passengers are unable to speak. the most controversial issue is the protection of personal data, but it should be remembered that this is not a permanent connection to the network and the system is only active when an accident occurs. the introduction of e-call is an important step towards improving road safety in the european union.
in writing. ‒ in my view, a regulation requiring new car models to have an automatic accident notification system (the so-called ecall system) must be controversial and give rise to ambiguous assessments. on the one hand, this is to protect the health and life of road users, but on the other hand, it is not to interfere with the privacy of eu citizens. the ecall system, on the other hand, collects data relevant to citizens' privacy, such as the make of the vehicle, the type of fuel used, the direction and exact location of the vehicle, and the number of seat belts fastened. experience has shown that there are no safeguards that would completely prevent access to this type of data, even if its acquisition remained illegal. therefore, i believe that ecall could perhaps be implemented, but only on a voluntary basis, i.e. the installation of the ecall system should be at the discretion of the owner or user of the vehicle. however, the regulation does not provide for this possibility and i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ tackling high road fatality rates is one of the eu's top transport policy priorities, which is why i voted in favour of this report. to do this, we need to use modern communication technologies. a quick response by emergency services is often crucial to preventing fatalities. the ecall system seems to be the solution to reduce as much as possible the time between the event and the information transmitted from the vehicle to the emergency services using the 112 emergency number. i believe that the european union should take action to ensure that manufacturers introduce this solution into vehicle design. of course, all aspects of the operation of this system, especially those related to the protection of sensitive data, and in particular vehicle location information, should be subject to special protection. the implementation of this system should not in any way infringe the right to privacy. we should monitor the implementation of this system carefully at every step so that, while protecting human life, we do not open the door to abuse.
in writing. ‒ proposals to amend directives 98/70/ec on fuel quality and 2009/28/ec on the promotion of energy from renewable sources were put forward by the european commission in october 2012. from the outset, they have generated heated debate, with both ardent supporters of the proposed changes and staunch opponents of the project in the member states. according to (not entirely reliable) scientific data, the indirect land use change effect (iluc) is expected to substantially offset the greenhouse gas emission reductions achieved through the use of biofuels. the commission therefore proposed to reduce the 10% target (set in directive 2009/28/ec, which was originally to be achieved by 2020) for conventional biofuels in transport to a maximum of 10%. in many member states, however, the investments made by producers have not yet begun to yield income, since the directive has only been in force for a few years. this change would also hit hard at farmers who have prepared for the near future. after two and a half years of negotiations, an agreement was reached to limit the use of first generation biofuels in transport to 7% and to introduce an additional cap for advanced biofuels of 0.5%. this is a compromise, but changing the rules in the middle of the game is a fatal move by the commission and will certainly have a negative impact on both agriculture and the eu economy.
in writing. ‒ it is in the interest not only of european agriculture but also of consumers above all that arable land is used mainly for the production of agricultural products for the consumer market or for the production of feed for farmed animals. in addition to fossil fuels, we should also seek to produce energy from genuinely renewable sources such as solar, wind and water, and thus avoid using plants, especially those grown for the human food market. instead of raising the share of such plants in the overall energy balance, more resources should be allocated to research and development of new energy generation technologies, which will make it possible to increase the availability of energy and at the same time reduce its price. i therefore voted in favour of amending the fuel quality and renewable energy directives, but i believe that a policy of encouraging innovation and developing new technologies for the clean use of fossil fuels and natural renewable sources should be pursued in parallel.
in writing. ‒ in view of the ongoing environmental degradation and disruption of ecosystems, any action to limit these destructive processes is highly desirable. the initiative to reduce the use of plastic bags is therefore strongly supported. reducing waste is something we can do ourselves as concerned citizens of our future. each of us, if we look around us and examine our daily habits, can take small steps to improve our environmental performance, whether by saving energy or by reducing the use of single-use plastic bags. charging for them in supermarkets is one of the most effective tools to reduce their production and consumption. we must constantly work to ensure that civilization does not destroy our most precious resource, nature. monitoring of the strategy and environmental education from an early age are necessary. it's very easy to destroy, but what's destroyed is not always easy to rebuild.
in writing. ‒ used plastic bags cause serious damage to the environment. the commission proposal aims to significantly reduce the use of lightweight plastic shopping bags in the eu. this problem can be solved easily and effectively, as has already been proven in many eu countries. charging for plastic shopping bags is a quick and lasting way to reduce their consumption. it is also important to set clear targets such as reducing the number of bags to 40 per person per year by 2025 and introducing mandatory bag fees from 31 december 2018. the commission has also proposed to set targets for the recycling of plastic bags, which is a significant step forward.
in writing. ‒ for environmental protection measures to have the desired effect, they must be practicable. the idea of radically reducing the use of lightweight plastic shopping bags is a good one. however, i think it would be even more important to support research into new technologies for the production of environmentally neutral packaging. otherwise, consumer societies, by accepting higher costs, will not reduce the amount of plastic they use significantly. therefore, although i voted in favour of adopting the packaging and packaging waste directive as proposed, i would like to see support for research into new packaging technologies on the one hand and more innovative and, in particular, more efficient ways of recycling plastic packaging on the other. nor can it be used to promote the use of paper, which is often done. this increases the need for, for example, tree pruning. i believe that action to reduce plastic use and promote other packaging should be carried out in parallel, otherwise we will not achieve the globally desired environmental effect.
in writing. ‒ in 2010, an estimated 98.6 billion plastic bags were placed on the eu market. most of these are lightweight plastic bags, which are usually disposable. although i am in favour of limiting the use of lightweight plastic bags and introducing charges for their use, for example, i abstained in the vote because the proposed rules are too restrictive.
in writing. ‒ environmental protection is important, but there are limits to the interference of public institutions in the area of economic freedom. restricting the use of plastic shopping bags per person is an extreme solution, but it is certainly justified. the commission has also identified a number of other measures that could be considered as part of the 'safety and environmental impact assessment' of the european union. that would be a more rational solution. as history has shown, the use of a system of commands and prohibitions does not always have the desired effect and often causes the opposite reaction instead of encouraging society to act in an environmentally friendly way. the obligation on member states to reduce the consumption of lightweight plastic shopping bags will also hit their manufacturers. while it is difficult to assess all the negative effects of these regulations on the labour market and the economies of the member states, they cannot be underestimated. therefore, in view of all the above arguments, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ in the second half of the 20th century, fishing in the baltic sea has been greatly intensified. by the end of the century, this had led to overfishing, as the cod fishery illustrates: from over 400 000 tonnes a year in the early 1980s to around 40 000 tonnes a decade later. in recent decades, studies have shown that over-fishing affects dozens of baltic fish species, threatening their extinction and the biological balance of the waters. the common fisheries policy (which was established in the 1970s as part of the common agricultural policy and has been formally operational since 1983) is therefore designed to manage eu fish stocks and to ensure fair income and a level playing field for fishermen in the member states. since herring, cod and sprat are the main fish species caught in the baltic sea, the proposed multiannual plan for these stocks is multi-species. this will allow a broader approach to fisheries control to be developed, taking into account the interdependencies between these species. this is certainly a good strategy, allowing for efficient management of fishing quotas and guaranteeing a balanced approach based on the most up-to-date scientific data on the stocks and the baltic ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ regulating fisheries in the baltic sea is of paramount importance. this is a small body of water with relatively limited natural resources. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the proposed draft regulation. however, i believe that it is not just the rules themselves that are important, but also the adoption of fair standards and their distribution among the countries benefiting from the baltic sea. the implementation of new standards also requires effective fisheries controls, so that the adoption of rules at eu level has a measurable impact on businesses and consumers, as well as on the environment.
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to create a multi-species management framework for the baltic cod, herring and sprat stocks, which have accounted for nearly 94% of all catches in the baltic in recent years. the plan should help to ensure the sustainable exploitation of those resources and the stability of fishing opportunities and thus the sustainability of the livelihood of fishermen. experts and fishermen in poland are sounding the alarm about the dramatic situation in the baltic and the disruption of the marine ecosystem, which is why i voted in favour of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of full, full membership of croatia in the european union. it would appear that the extension of the eu-russian federation partnership and cooperation agreement to croatia is only a minor procedural adjustment. however, it sends an undesirable political signal, signifying acceptance of russia's status as a partner country. in the meantime, it is responsible for the illegal annexation of crimea, the armed aggression against eastern ukraine and the use of hybrid warfare against its neighbours, including eu members. the partnership and cooperation agreement with the russian federation, which is attempting to rebuild its soviet or russian empire sphere of influence by force, should be suspended and, if aggression continues, dissolved.
in writing. ‒ russia is not a party with which the eu should in any way move to normal diplomatic relations at this time. although this amendment concerns only technical aspects and is not intended to modify the substance of this agreement, until russia's illegal activities in ukraine cease, crimea is returned and russian troops are withdrawn from the territory of the eu-associated state, we should freeze all such activities. even if it is a small gesture, it is necessary to demonstrate our outrage at moscow's violation of international law. that is why i voted against this recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process is an intergovernmental initiative designed to enable the sustainable development of higher education in the european union. it aims to standardise the quality of education, to promote student mobility and to give students a wider choice of educational pathways. quality higher education is essential for cultural, economic and social development and for providing young people with an education that will enable them to succeed. much remains to be done, but i believe that the implementation of the bologna reforms will enable european higher education to meet the challenges of an ever-changing labour market.
in writing. ‒ the objectives of the bologna process have been achieved by member states to a very uneven degree. the priority is to implement the reforms agreed jointly. achieving this requires political commitment and cooperation, and an important element should be the development of additional tools and methods to help countries facing challenges make greater progress. it also requires greater focus on the student, his needs, and what he should learn. the social aspects of the bologna process are considered to be among the most neglected. most students participate in programmes that follow the three-stage structure of the bologna process. the creation of such a study structure is a way of better preparing graduates for the demands of the labour market and social challenges. the proper implementation of the european credit transfer and accumulation system (ects) is necessary to achieve the objectives of the bologna process. the recognition of qualifications acquired abroad should be improved, which would bring more direct benefits to students. another important aspect is the joint programmes, which are also a key aspect of the internationalisation of higher education. work should be done to develop mobility in the bologna system, both for students and for teachers and education staff.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that the potential of the european cultural and creative industries is not being fully exploited. europe, which until recently was an inspiration for other countries and continents, is losing its position more and more clearly not only to america but also to asian countries. the example of south korea, india and, closer to home, turkey, shows that, with the right mechanisms, regional works can be turned into a leading export product. tv series and films from these countries are conquering the world, including europe. that is why i was pleased to support the report. the rapporteur rightly points out that the problem is not the quality of european production or its tightness, but above all the lack of effective promotion. europe, which produces 1,500 films a year in dozens of languages, is unable to encourage or even provide its citizens with the opportunity to watch them. if we are now asking ourselves how to create new jobs in the union, the cultural sector is the place to be. by changing the funding model for film production and channelling part of the funding to broad promotion - including language translation - we can increase the potential of this industry and create new jobs in a very short time.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the new eu forest strategy for forests and the forestry sector because i believe that it does not present the concept of sustainable development. the new eu strategy cannot serve the interests of private forest owners alone, bypassing state forests. the commission notes that the forestry sector is not a single sector, but is rather a group of sectors, which are linked by a common economic interest. the rapporteur, mrs köstinger, has not taken into account the important amendments concerning, among other things, the carbon capture mechanism which i tabled with my colleagues from the polish delegation in the ecr group. as a member of the european parliament from poland, where forests are the wealth of all citizens, i cannot agree to such a strategy. that's why i voted against this resolution.
in writing. ‒ forests are one of europe's greatest assets. in many countries, they make up more than half the land area. they are a part of the landscape, a home and a shelter for animals, a 'green lung' for urban centres and a source of employment for over 3.5 million europeans. so i agree that we should be more careful and precise in our approach to planning and managing this natural resource. the most important aspect of this strategy is the sustainable development of forestry and the timber industry so that present and future generations can both benefit from and enjoy it. i agree with the rapporteur that the strategy should not impose additional bureaucratic guidelines on forest owners and foresters, but rather, because of their heterogeneity, should set out individual criteria for each area. it is also necessary to take advantage of innovative research and ideas that will enable the timber industry to develop in innovative ways and provide even more jobs to the economy.
in writing. ‒ this report covers all aspects of forestry, with emphasis on more sustainable long-term development, resource efficiency, multi-functional forest management, future challenges related to wood scarcity and threats from climate change, and most importantly, calling for an action plan with specified resources and funding. better and more efficient use of forest resources and the maintenance of employment in the sector will help europeans to better understand the importance of forests for the environment and the eu economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the new eu forest strategy for forests and the forestry sector. the european union should play its part in supporting national policies to achieve active and sustainable forest management. it is essential to promote the management of different types of forests and to strengthen cooperation in the face of cross-border threats. it is important to remember that forestry is the responsibility of the member states, so the subsidiarity principle must be respected and differences in preferences between countries, regional conditions and ownership models must be respected. the european union should stop imposing new market restrictions on forestry and wood products and, through these measures, ensure the application of the principles of market freedom. the european forest information system will be an additional valuable asset, to support the exchange of data, best practices and up-to-date knowledge on forests in the member states, thus contributing to the active development of this sector of the economy.
in writing. ‒ the report on the new forest strategy aims to update the european framework for forestry activities that support sustainable forest management. in reality, however, it represents the interests of private forest owners, bypassing the interests of state forests. meanwhile, polish forestry is a model for the concept of sustainable development, a concept that the eu refers to in almost every document. the unesco award given to polish state forests in 2013 proves that this is the case. moreover, the assumptions of the strategy do not take into account the relevant objectives. it is important to remember that carbon dioxide is the gas of life and that managing it is the basis of ecological engineering to regenerate agricultural and forest soils, produce a renewable energy source such as biomass and shape the desired biodiversity. the rapporteur also did not include in the compromise text amendments that were important for state forests, which were tabled by pis mps at the meeting of the agriculture committee. i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ wood is a strategic national asset which like other natural resources should be protected and treated with special care. the fact that this is a renewable resource should not lead to its exploitation in an irrational way, putting current economic interests above a rational approach to the use of resources. the state forestry enterprises play an important role in protecting against deforestation. compared to private companies, they are the model for the concept of sustainable development, which is widely present in the environmental policy of the european union. the polish state forests in my country are the best example of this, as evidenced by the award of the unesco prize in 2013. for this reason, i cannot support a report which puts the interests of private forest owners ahead of the interests of the state forests.

mr president, we need a comprehensive action plan that covers the internal and external dimension of security and horizontally connects various sectors under clear rules as described in the document. fighting against cybercrime is a key challenge; with the loss of more than eur 300 billion every year, each of us can become a victim of cybercrime. i am pleased to see that cybercrime is one of the top three priorities in the european agenda on security. very often now, cyberspace creates the framework for organised crime and terrorism. we need to set the rules, use modern technologies to find appropriate tools and build public-private cooperation. there are new technological possibilities which allow for processing the data – not personal data: frequencies of data set transfers, photos by spectrum of colour analysis – and preventing crimes. research and innovation can be a successful source for new forms of security. this is the new concept of data-driven security. the fight against organised crime remains high on the agenda, but we need to make the anti-terrorism policy more effective by adoption of the pnr directive, by more resources dedicated to fighting radicalisation, and by better use of algorithms supporting the early warning system. we need the synergy of cooperating eu institutions to be able to gather enough resources and to efficiently exchange information under clear rules of privacy protection. i believe that the european cybercrime and counter-terrorism centres in europol should be further strengthened.
in writing. i welcome the fact that the european commission is increasingly concerned with the internal security of the union. the fight against crime requires better cooperation between all the countries of the union. we are facing increasing challenges such as terrorism, organised crime and cybercrime. they are increasingly threatening societies across europe. the fight against crime must be primarily carried out by the member states. however, cooperation within the union brings tangible added value. in this area, two actions are particularly important. first, to facilitate the exchange of information between law enforcement authorities and union agencies, such as information on stolen documents or vehicles. second, we need to change the rules on the transfer of information from criminal records. currently, 26 eu member states exchange more than 100,000 messages each month on punished eu citizens. however, this system does not cover punished non-eu nationals. this is a serious problem, for they are increasingly forming international criminal groups that engage in human smuggling and drug trafficking. it is worthwhile that information about these criminals is made known to law enforcement authorities in all countries of the union.

in writing. criticism of eu immigration policy is growing after another tragedy in the mediterranean, where more than 900 migrants drowned trying to reach europe. in 2014, about 3,500 people died on similar desperate voyages. the number of lucky people who managed to get into the union officially exceeded 207 thousand in the same year. according to the european agency frontex, the number of illegal immigrants has increased dramatically in recent years. a few years ago, the number of cases was around 70,000 to 100,000 a year, but now it has doubled. according to the united nations high commissioner for refugees, some 4 million undocumented immigrants from africa and asia are currently living in europe. along with the illegal voyages, there is also the threat of the islamic state, which has wreaked havoc in iraq and syria, causing an exodus of people from those areas, mainly towards europe. without a genuine community foreign policy, the migration of mediterranean refugees cannot be effectively counteracted or the conflicts that cause it resolved. in this context, we call for increased cooperation between the european commission and the countries of origin and transit of migrants. increased vessel and air patrols for the eu's 'triton' operation in the mediterranean and the frontex budget will be necessary to enable the union to effectively protect its borders and address the hundreds of thousands of migrants in refugee camps on its territory.

in writing. ‒ i voted to increase the amount of initial advance payments paid to operational programmes under the youth employment initiative. the budgetary constraints currently faced by member states, as well as the lack of funds available at the beginning of the programming period, have caused delays in the implementation of projects at national and regional level. most member states do not have sufficient funds in their budgets to make advance payments for projects aimed at young people. in general, countries pre-finance projects at national level and then receive reimbursement from european union funds. however, the rate of the initial advance payments, which amounted to 1 to 1,5% of the total allocation, proved to be insufficient to implement these programmes. therefore, increasing the amount of the advance payments for the youth employment initiative is crucial as it will allow the funds to be mobilised quickly and efficiently for the implementation of subsequent projects. the increased advance payments will amount to over eur 1 billion (30%) and will help over 7 million young europeans who are not in employment, education or training to integrate into the labour market. any further delays in the implementation of the initiative could undermine the efforts made by member states to combat youth unemployment.
in writing. ‒ i support the way europol has implemented the 2013 budget. the analysis shows that europol has expanded the scope of its collection of crime information and is increasingly transferring this information to individual countries. but i would like to draw attention to what i believe is a very important problem. under the aegis of europol, joint investigation teams are set up, which are composed of police officers from several member states for a fixed period of time. they investigate specific cross-border cases. it seems that we need to move towards the creation of such teams more regularly so that they can be permanently engaged in combating crimes with an international dimension, such as illegal smuggling and trafficking of human beings, drug trafficking, trafficking in stolen vehicles, cyber attacks on banking systems. this would require more money to train police officers for continuous, effective cooperation, i.e. more funding next year for the european police college, which is run by europol.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council regulation establishing the european public prosecutor's office for the following reasons. firstly, i believe that the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office is an important step towards the creation of an effective system for detecting cross-border crime. the creation of a single body dealing with similar cases, but with jurisdiction over the whole of the european union, would streamline the procedure and at the same time reduce the time it takes for union citizens to recover their money. secondly, the establishment of a policy-independent institution that supports the prosecution of financial crime offers hope for effectiveness at all levels. thirdly, although i personally object to excessive bureaucracy, i believe that this is an institution that is needed to help citizens to assert their rights.

mr. chairman, please! development aid is both an expression of solidarity and an investment in a safer and more sustainable world. the union and its member states are the largest donors in the world. the union's contribution to official development assistance is more than half of the total global contribution. some eu countries have cut aid spending during the crisis. now the total seems to be increasing. but it is not as high as europe had hoped. the millennium development goals will be phased out in 2015. these goals, which have been the basis of development cooperation for the past 15 years, will be replaced in september at the un in new york by a framework for poverty eradication and sustainable development. therefore, 2015 as the european year for development is crucial for sustainable development. official development assistance must continue and we must strive to reach the target of 0.7%, but i think it is also very important to introduce other forms of innovative development aid financing.

member of the commission.– madam president, i have listened with attention to honourable members’ interventions, concerns, warnings and proposals on this delicate subject. they will be fully taken on board when elaborating further response measures. i share your views that we need measures, such as the ones presented by the commission and endorsed by the member states, which are based on scientific and technical bases. their implementation should not be delayed. furthermore, a new set of measures will be examined with a sense of urgency. movements of plants out of the demarcated area in italy and imports from third countries have to be subject to very strict conditions. at the same time, eradication measures have to be taken in the infected area in italy to reduce the presence of the bacterium and prevent its spread in the union. the commission is determined to further intensify scientific research for xylella treatment, involving the horizon 2020 programme. honourable members, let me express my deepest understanding of how difficult it is for a farmer to remove a tree, especially when it has not yet been proven to be infected. it is our common responsibility to convince all actors of the benefits of such measures to prevent the spread of the disease in italy and beyond. in conclusion, let me assure you that the commission is ready to explore all possible tools available to support financially the implementation of the compensation measures provided in our legislation.
in writing. xylella fastidiosa is not only a threat to olive cultivation in southern european countries. the bacteria can attack several hundred different plant species, including vines, fruit trees, grasses, and grains. it has already destroyed crops in several countries in north and south america and in october 2013 the italian authorities reported its presence in the eu. no effective drug has yet been found to help the infected plants, and removing the infected organisms does not stop the disease from progressing. the potential damage that xylella fastidiosa may cause will have very serious consequences for the economy and the environment of our continent. in addition, according to the european food safety authority (efsa), the costs of combating the disease in the event of a spread of the pathogen will be extremely high. the european commission must take immediate action to curb the spread of the bacteria, focusing on strengthening controls on imported goods. however, it is also important to compensate farmers who have lost their crops and incurred severe costs as a result of the epidemic.
in writing. - i voted for the alcohol strategy. developing a single, coherent strategy for alcohol consumption is a challenge, as the problem has many facets. on the one hand, excessive drinking is a health hazard and can lead to many social problems. on the other hand, i agree with the arguments put forward by colleagues during the debate, who point to the positive cultural dimension of moderate alcohol consumption. one thing is certain, however: excessive alcohol consumption is particularly harmful to children and young people. sadly, statistics in many lands indicate that alcohol consumption among youths is increasing and the age of initiation is decreasing. i believe that education is the key to this problem, and i am glad that this has been highlighted in the draft resolution. but i think that it's not just the young people who need to be educated in this area, but the whole of society. too often adults still allow youths to drink. in many countries, it is being sold recklessly to minors in shops and bars, with no adult to intervene. i would like the commission to take this problem into account in its draft alcohol strategy and to develop guidelines to combat it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because it draws attention to the tragedy of people trying to cross the mediterranean, fleeing war or persecution in syria, iraq, eritrea, somalia and libya. more than 1,500 people have died in the mediterranean since january. our resolution calls on the commission to develop a european agenda on migration that takes into account all aspects of migration and to propose urgent action to prevent further deaths at sea, and calls for closer coordination of eu and member states' policies to eliminate the causes of migration. at the same time, close cooperation with europol, fronteks, easo and eurojust should be undertaken to combat traffickers in human beings and criminal networks of smugglers linked to drug, arms and terrorism trafficking. action should be taken to identify and trace their financing and to identify their methods of operation in order to prevent them from making profits at the expense of the lives of migrants. close cooperation and compliance by third countries with international law on the rescue of life at sea are necessary, as well as ensuring the protection of refugees and respect for fundamental rights. member states should make full use of the possibilities for issuing humanitarian visas at their diplomatic missions. a solidarity mechanism must be in place in the event of a mass or sudden influx of migrants. the common european asylum system needs to be implemented quickly and effectively by all participating member states, which will ensure common european standards.
in writing. ‒ the tragic events in the mediterranean are primarily the result of irresponsible geopolitics by the great powers, which have led to the destabilisation of some north african states. but trying to solve this situation - by burdening european countries with millions of refugees - is probably the worst possible solution. first of all, this will not solve the complex situation in the north african states, nor will it guarantee a peaceful and stable life for refugees and will significantly worsen the economic situation of the countries hosting refugees. the solution to the plight of refugees must be sought in their homeland.
in writing. ‒ the european council's report on the recent tragedies in the mediterranean and on migration and asylum policy in the eu has generated a heated debate. the deaths of refugees, the tragedies and the abuses that take place in their countries are shocking and unacceptable. we cannot be indifferent to these injuries. but it is clear that europe, an island of peace and prosperity in a war-torn world, has limited financial and territorial resources. our solidarity with the people of other parts of the world must be commensurate with our capacity. let's develop our immigration and asylum policies, our education systems and our social organization towards multiculturalism and multi-faith, but carefully, without losing our identity and our religion. it is essential, instead of moving the world to europe, to move europe - in the sense of institutions, organisations and ideas - to other continents, to provide assistance in situ, to curb the illegal trafficking of people. that is why i voted against mandatory quotas for member states, because these countries are economically diverse, often not yet adapted to multiculturalism, have different geopolitical situations. poland, for example, is already taking in many migrants from ukraine and other eastern european countries, and we expect more. we therefore need a non-fragmentary european policy that also takes into account these migration trends, as well as the different status of migrants in relation to the political and economic situation in their countries of origin.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the tragic events in the mediterranean and the union's asylum and migration policy. the lack of a common approach to migration policy weakens our ability to deal with these tragedies. unfortunately, despite many attempts, we have still not been able to develop a common approach to migration. today, none of us has any doubt that such a policy based on solidarity and respect for human rights is necessary. cooperation with the countries of origin and transit of migrants is key to combating illegal migration. cooperation in humanitarian, financial and political assistance, which should focus both on improving the living conditions of the local population and on combating smuggling and trafficking networks. further action must focus on the proper implementation of existing legal measures, including, inter alia, the effective implementation of the directive on sanctions against employers of illegal migrants. in the debate on the union's approach to migration, we must also address the issue of legal migration. with an ageing european population, migration can be an opportunity for us to fill labour shortages in certain sectors of the economy. we therefore need a clear european system to help bring different categories of workers to europe and to curb illegal migration.
in writing. ‒ immigration should be considered not only in the context of its current consequences, but also in the context of the future effects that can be expected not only in europe but also in the areas from which people emigrate. and that's the effect that's going to be felt for decades. there is no doubt that the hundreds of thousands of people from different cultural, religious and linguistic backgrounds who are admitted to the european union each year will have a huge impact on europe's socioeconomic relations. worse, however, the significant outflow of active people from the affected areas could lead to long-term development problems and major changes in the social fabric of these countries. this can be used by extremist groups, terrorists and dictatorial governments to pursue an uncompromising policy, not only towards their own communities and peoples, but also towards third countries, including european ones. the union should therefore not only pursue a humanitarian policy towards refugees, but above all be active in the refugee centres themselves. so it is not just the effects of immigration that need to be tackled, but also the causes. for these reasons, i abstained from voting on the resolution, which did not mention the union's strategy to combat the causes of the mass influx of people from africa and the middle east to europe.

member of the commission.– mr president, this is an important occasion to debate a very important issue, namely how to eliminate conflict minerals from our supply chains. by doing so, we will reduce the great hardship, endless wars and human rights abuses that have traditionally come with them. i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr winkler, the committee on international trade (inta), the other committees and all the members who have been active in working on this issue. one of the challenges in trade policy is to harness the potential of our economies while creating effective systems to avoid negative consequences, like the one we are discussing today. this challenge is particularly acute in developing countries, and the issue of conflict minerals is one of the most glaring examples. on the one hand, we do need a global market-based approach to raw materials that provides developing countries with a vital source of stable income through trade in natural resources. on the other hand, we need to break the link between minerals and conflict, the most obvious example of which is the conflict in the great lakes region in africa. the situation there is horrific. millions of people have been killed and millions more injured and traumatised since the outbreak of the first congo war in the mid-1990s. while congo is the most dramatic example of the phenomenon, it is not the only one. therefore, following calls for action by the united states, the g8 and this parliament, based on the work of the oecd, the commission developed, jointly with the high representative, an integrated approach. the draft regulation we are discussing here today is only one of its components. i insist on this integrated approach because it is crucial to understand – and i know you all do – that there is no silver bullet to deal with this problem. it is by nature multidimensional and extremely complicated. so we must look at it from different angles – development, political, the trade perspective – all at the same time. the size of europe’s trade footprint is such that businesses here must play their part. the eu is amongst the world’s largest importers of tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold ores and concentrates, with a share of almost 35% of global trade. the eu is also a relatively large importer of tin, tantalum and tungsten and gold metals which presently represent almost 25% and 15% of global trade respectively. but precisely because of our importance in trade, we can also make things worse if we do not approach it in the right way. if we impose a mandatory scheme without making sure that the conditions on the ground in the conflict regions are right in order to support the implementation of such a system, we do run a high risk of further disrupting global supply chains and driving them away from africa altogether. we also risk creating trade diversion, resulting in prejudice against individual countries, or even the whole continent, and that would lead to plummeting prices for minerals from certain origins. we can also risk continuing to have thriving underground markets in conflict and high-risk areas and a prosperous smuggling sector. we can also create a severe shortage in the eu for companies that are – most of the time – willing, but unable, to check their supply chains effectively, and we will have achieved nothing on the ground since we will have placed fragile mining areas and local communities under additional pressure from international markets. if you do not believe me, you can have a look at the situation in the great lakes region since the us mandatory scheme in the dodd-frank act came into effect. the difficulties there are described in united nations reports year after year. the commission proposal has taken these key considerations into account, following an in-depth impact assessment exercise. our plan is focused, proportionate and designed to complement the other components of the integrated approach. our proposal focuses on smelters and refiners. until they know where they source their minerals from, we cannot reasonably ask the majority of downstream companies to know. many of them might be tempted to lie. it will include responsible smelters and refiners in the eu and worldwide on a white list and consequently a ‘name and shame’ system for those that do not appear on it. there are no more than 40 smelters in the eu. how many of them do you think are able not to appear on that list? there will be a lot of pressure from you, from ngos and from other business. i would argue not a single one. moreover, the commission proposal sets up an enforcement structure to be deployed by member states’ competent authorities to ensure that operators claiming to be responsible are truly so. it also includes a strong review clause to open the possibility for switching – in a staged manner – to a mandatory approach in the event that the current proposal does not deliver. it operates in parallel to the eur 20 million package that the high representative and the commission have announced to further support capacity building in conflict regions. so i think this voluntary, incentives-based approach, integrated for responsible sourcing, is the most appropriate one to achieve the common goal that we have here. i thank you for this possibility to debate it and am looking forward to the debate.

in writing. ‒ i support the european parliament's legislative resolution on a regulation that would regulate the use of indicators in financial instruments and contracts. the financial crisis that europe found itself in after 2008 showed that one of its causes was the manipulation of exchange rates and libor rates. it was assumed that over time the financial market would correct these irregularities. it was deceptive, it led to market chaos and it encouraged speculation. and as a result, it hits the bank's customers. therefore, in my view, including indicators in the regulated business and not subjecting them to market manipulation alone is essential to restoring customer confidence in financial markets. the published indicators, which are so important for borrowers, for example, must be transparent. the point is not only to make these indicators known to the public but also to make the methods used to determine exchange rates and libor known to the public. this will promote predictability and build confidence in financial markets, which is crucial for investors and borrowers. that is why i support this resolution.

all member states of the union except denmark, governs the rules on the choice of law applicable to the proceedings and the recognition of judgments. since the regulation adopted so many years ago proved insufficient in the context of the economic crisis and the bankruptcy of many companies in the union, we started work in the european parliament during the last term of office to amend this regulation. the report was drawn up by our colleague klaus-heiner lehne and provided an excellent basis for the subsequent negotiations with the council already underway during this term. the positions of our two institutions were close to each other and, most importantly, we shared a common objective: to create a legal framework for crossborder insolvency proceedings that would, on the one hand, give creditors a chance to be satisfied, but on the other hand, allow these honest entrepreneurs to undertake proper restructuring and thus prevent the bankruptcy of businesses and the loss of jobs. the main objective of the reform was to try to limit the so-called bankruptcy tourism. the european court of justice has pointed out that there are no adequate safeguards against this type of procedure under the insolvency regulation. the interpretation of the term 'principal place of business' (comi) is relevant here, since it is necessary to determine the jurisdiction of the court competent to open insolvency proceedings. a change of jurisdiction entails the need to pursue your claims in a court in another country. this in turn leads to proceedings in a different language and under different procedural rules, which in turn leads to a lengthier process, higher costs and less legal certainty. it seems that in the present situation legal certainty in the european union's trade is extremely important to us. in order to eliminate the possibility of forum shopping, parliament therefore proposed that the following solution be introduced into the definition of comi: a three-month transitional period during which the debtor company cannot open insolvency proceedings after it has moved its registered office to another country. the other deadline, namely six months, was adopted in the case of consumer bankruptcy. this difference is due to a very important fact. well, it's much easier to transfer to a natural person than a legal entity. in the case of a consumer bankruptcy within this six-month period, the debtor has the burden of proving that his principal place of residence is where he declared it. secondly, we have proposed a new system of coordination of insolvency for a group of companies, which will be an optional instrument, i.e. non-compulsory. within 30 days of receipt of the notification of the request to open the coordination procedure, the trustee of each of the companies may decide to exercise the opt-out and exit from coordination if he considers that it would be in the interest of the company he represents. the effectiveness and efficiency of this mechanism will be examined five years after the entry into force of the amendments to the regulation. and thirdly, there is the establishment - which i think is very important - of a european insolvency register, which will allow the monitoring of insolvency proceedings throughout the european union. i am convinced that this register will prove very useful for both citizens and in writing. this convention is an important step towards equal opportunities for people with disabilities. the document discusses the rights of disabled people, the role of their representatives and the structures involved. there are some 80 million disabled people in the eu and one in six europeans has a disability. the european barrier strategy of 2010 aims to make europe a continent without barriers by 2020. adopted in poland in 1997 the charter of the disabled identifies the key areas where intensive action is needed to ensure that people with disabilities do not feel discriminated against. the so-called 'black paper' describes, among other things, architectural, technical barriers in education and workplaces and transport barriers. in recent months, polish railways has introduced legislation to help disabled people board and disembark trains. however, there is concern about the lack of financial security for carers of disabled people, which is most often the case for women who give up their professional work to care for a disabled person. unfortunately, there are now efforts to reduce even more the low level of benefits. the junior programme, which has been positively evaluated, is a vocational activation programme for disabled graduates, enabling them to undertake work placements and subsequently to enter employment. the new version of the unesco information text, entitled 'you have rights', has been translated in a child-friendly way.
in writing. the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, drawn up in new york on 13 december 2006, is the first international legal instrument that comprehensively addresses the rights of persons with disabilities. it is about promoting, protecting and ensuring the full and equal enjoyment of all human rights and fundamental freedoms by all persons with disabilities and promoting respect for their inherent dignity. despite the growing educational and organisational activities in many eu countries, there are still many barriers that prevent the realisation of basic aspirations, such as the possibility of full participation in civic and social life. therefore, it is appropriate to introduce an obligation to remove all obstacles that hinder the full and effective participation of persons with disabilities in society on an equal basis with others. the implementation of such regulations should also be monitored and the adopted provisions should be made publicly available to all citizens.
in writing.– it is estimated that around 80 million people in the european union have a disability. it should be one of our top priorities as members of the european parliament to ensure that the equal rights, dignity, equal treatment and full participation of persons with disabilities in society is a fact and not a mere wish. as members of the committee on petitions, we receive plenty of cases dealing with discrimination on the grounds of disability in access to employment, self-employment, public services and education. according to the eu agency for fundamental rights, discrimination and barriers while exercising their rights are part of everyday life for persons with disabilities. it is essential to underline that this is not a homogeneous group and therefore the policies and actions should reflect the various needs of women, children or people who need more intense support. furthermore, i am hopeful that the commission is going to take this matter deeply into consideration and will come up with an ambitious proposal for a european accessibility act, ensuring the full involvement of persons with disabilities throughout the legislative cycle while having regard to the proper level of accessibility to goods and services for all european citizens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of approving, on behalf of the union and its member states, the additional protocol to the eu-south africa trade, development and cooperation agreement to take account of the accession of croatia to the eu. the trade, development and cooperation agreement between the eu member states and the republic of south africa was signed in pretoria on 11 october 1999 and entered into force on 1 may 2004. on 1 july 2013, the republic of croatia acceded to the eu and became the 28th member state. on 24 september 2012, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with south africa for the conclusion of an additional protocol. the negotiations on this matter were successfully concluded on 19 may 2014. the purpose of the additional protocol is only to introduce into the trade, development and cooperation agreement the few technical and linguistic changes necessary as a result of the accession of croatia to the eu. the signing of the additional protocol is necessary for the republic of croatia to become a party to the trade, development and cooperation agreement with south africa.
in writing. ‒ most mobile phones, tablets and computers are now made from valuable minerals whose extraction, processing and even marketing are sometimes highly controversial. it turns out that the minerals used are often extracted in violation of basic human rights, which can be called 21st century slavery. moreover, profits from the trade in or the processing of such minerals are often used for other illicit activities, including - worst of all - the financing of armed conflicts that claim tens or even hundreds of thousands of lives, especially in africa and latin america. there is also a real economic dimension to this problem. we cannot allow honest companies that comply with international standards for the extraction and marketing of minerals to be harmed by competition from those who break the basic rules. i therefore support the form of regulation that will best ensure that all companies in the mineral supply chain comply with the relevant standards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on maternity leave because i believe that the council should return to the negotiating table as soon as possible. instead of threatening to withdraw the project, the commission should make every effort to break the deadlock and work out a common position between parliament and the council. in the face of an ageing continent and low growth rates in most european countries, legislation to ensure a better balance between family and working life is of paramount importance. i also voted for the passage of paragraph 5 on the introduction of paid paternity leave. fathers, like mothers, should be guaranteed the right to reconcile their private and professional lives. member states should realise that it is in their interest to create legislation that does not deter young people from starting a family but encourages them to do so.
in writing. ‒ in supporting the parliament's resolution on the amendment of the maternity leave directive, i voted for equal rights for women across the european union to enjoy the same standards of maternity leave and to maintain a decent wage for young women. the maternity leave regulation is at odds with eu policies on reconciling work and life, tackling demographic change and protecting women's health. in addition, the recommendations contained in this regulation indirectly contribute to the implementation of the 2020 strategy and allow young mothers to lead a decent life while caring for young children. given that the project is aimed at improving the living conditions of women citizens of the union and is in line with the recommendations of the international labour organisation on maternity protection, it should not be withdrawn. i would also point out that the project also strengthens the protection of women against dismissal after the end of the maternity period, which allows women to maintain greater employment stability.
in writing. ‒ the demographic challenges facing the european union today require strong action to support fertility, as the rapid ageing of european societies could lead to the collapse or significant disruption of pension systems. although poland currently has one of the longest maternity leave periods in europe, at 12 months, i believe that the competence to determine the length of maternity leave should remain in the hands of the member states. only then will it be possible for the legislator to take account of a number of national and national factors relevant to this issue, such as the tradition or the level of socioeconomic development of individual countries. i therefore abstained on a resolution calling for the resumption of work on the amendments to the maternity leave directive.
in writing. ‒ the demographic crisis in europe is no longer a question of the near future, but a real problem that increasingly affects our ageing european society. the european union is not, of course, the panacea for all the problems involved. the member states have a leading role to play in this respect, and they should ensure that social policy is geared to supporting families, especially women who decide to take time off from work and have a baby. this boundary between the eu's and the member states' competences is very clear and no one disputes it. however, we cannot ignore the community's potential to create a family and motherhood-friendly environment. we have an opportunity at european level to combat the ageing trend and we should seize it. supporting women is crucial here, because they bear the biggest cost of the decision to have a child. the creation of solutions that allow men to participate more effectively in childcare will be a valuable incentive to decide on parenthood. i think it is worth supporting this resolution and encouraging the council to take more active action for our future.
in writing. ‒ one of the objectives of our work in the agri committee is to ensure that consumers have the highest quality food. we cannot foresee all the challenges, but we have the ability to prevent and respond to foodborne illness and contamination. and that's how it should be this time. we should have learned from experience (asf in poland, the cucumber crisis in germany) that we should have the tools to ensure that this problem, which is occurring in a specific area, does not lead to a health risk for consumers and a stalemate for producers in the sector and huge losses for their own businesses, and above all the loss of thousands of jobs. each case should be treated individually, as each area has its own characteristics and will respond differently to a crisis. since olive trees have been cultivated in apulia for several thousand years, the tools used here should be specifically adapted to the epidemic that is occurring there. first of all, a financial instrument should be launched to support farmers in the crisis and allow them to quickly recover and return to the market. i would like to emphasise that such an instrument should be available at all times so that it can be used immediately if necessary.

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– madam president, honourable members, allow me to start by thanking the european parliament for the opportunity to debate the eastern partnership just before the riga summit, which will gather the heads of state from the european union and the eastern partnership partner countries from 21 to 22 may in riga. almost six years ago in prague, we set out our vision of bringing the relationship between the eu and its eastern european partners to a new level by deepening our bilateral engagement and building a multilateral framework for cooperation and dialogue. since then, we have achieved good progress in our partnership. we have a better understanding of the different interests, needs and ambitions of our partner countries within the eastern partnership. in riga, we will take stock of the considerable achievements we have witnessed since vilnius and chart a positive agenda for the future. since the last eastern partnership summit in vilnius, the signing of association agreements and deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta) agreements brought to a new level our cooperation with georgia, moldova and ukraine. the association agreements, including dcftas, with georgia and the republic of moldova are already provisionally applied and the initial indications are very promising. trade is already increasing between the eu and the partners concerned. as regards ukraine, the recent eu summit with ukraine reconfirmed that the provisional application of the ukrainian dcfta will start on 1 january 2016. as you are aware, commissioner cecilia malmström, is holding trilateral talks with her ukrainian and russian counterparts to ensure that provisional application on 1 january takes place in the best possible environment. the riga summit will be an opportunity to review the early stages of the implementation of association agreements and dcftas and to demonstrate the eu’s strong commitment to deepening our cooperation. the summit will reaffirm the importance of reforms which consolidate the rule of law and a competitive market economy as the best prospect for guaranteeing a european future for our partners. we will highlight the eu’s commitment to supporting efforts devoted to advance cooperation in institution-building, mobility and people-to-people contacts, market opportunities and interconnections. therefore, i would like to stress that, on the margins of the riga summit, three large-scale side events will take place: the media conference on the role of the media in the eastern partnership, the civil society conference and the business forum. these events will emphasise the increasing role of civil society and business contacts as an integral part of the eastern partnership policy. let me stress that the eu values our relationship with all six of our eastern partners and we are ready to work for more tailor-made arrangements with them. for partners with association agreements, the path ahead is laid out in those agreements. for the other partners, there is work to be done. we have reached an understanding with armenia on the scope of our future relationship and we hope that the council allows negotiations to begin on a new contractual agreement with armenia. the relevant negotiating mandate is being prepared. we currently await azerbaijan’s ideas on how it sees its future relations with the european union. once we have received these, we will give serious consideration as to the kind of relationship that both sides need and expect. we are also exploring ways to further deepen our critical engagement with belarus. we are convinced that developing bilateral relations in this differentiated way is the best way to ensure that all six partners have a stake in the eastern partnership and therefore remain committed to this unique framework. we have moved forward in the area of mobility. since april last year, moldova has enjoyed a visa-free regime with the schengen area. nearly half a million people have been able to take advantage of it. both georgia and ukraine have made good progress in implementing the benchmarks of their visa liberalisation action plans. fulfilling the actions required in the recent commission progress reports would allow these countries to complete their respective implementation of all the visa liberalisation action plans’ second-phase benchmarks. the commission will continue to monitor and to do its utmost to support them and will report on progress by the end of 2015. the finalisation of the negotiations with belarus on the visa facilitation agreement and readmission agreement and the launch of the mobility partnership in june is foreseen. let me stress that the eastern partnership riga summit is taking place in a new geopolitical environment where borders have been changed by force and where partners (and indeed member states) have been subjected to considerable pressure. let me stress once again that we do not share the zero-sum thinking based on rival spheres of influence or the use of coercion. let me be absolutely clear: neither the eastern partnership nor the bilateral relations between the eu and any of its partners have ever, nor will they ever, be directed against anyone. but let me be equally clear, the eu will continue to stand up for our partners as they make free, sovereign choices about their foreign and trade policies. in addition to being a major opportunity to reconfirm our commitment to the eastern partnership, the summit in riga will also be a valuable occasion to get our partners’ views on the future of the european neighbourhood policy. we want to make sure that in redesigning our policy for the future we have listened to our partners and taken their views fully into account. let me re-state that we offer our eastern european partners a genuine partnership. we do not impose choices on our partners. differentiation in our bilateral relations will need to be further enhanced, taking account of each partner`s ambitions and needs. the full engagement of partners’ governments is crucial in bringing about the necessary reforms. nevertheless, no government is able to succeed in such an endeavour without the broad support of the people. successful transformation is only possible if it emerges as a result of joint efforts of society as a whole. the nurturing of constituencies for reform able to influence national decision-making is imperative. local authorities, parliamentarians (including this house), the business community and civil society have a very important role to play in the eastern partnership. we therefore count on this house to help us stand with our partners in delivering the chance their citizens desire.
