ladies and gentlemen! the current rules on corporate taxation in the european union are not adapted to the requirements of a modern economy. some companies take advantage of the fact that countries differ in their tax avoidance practices. this results in significant revenue losses for member states, higher tax burdens and distortions of competition in the markets. the action plan we are discussing today sets out the way forward for more effective tax enforcement in the union. according to this concept, companies should pay their fair share of taxes in the country where they generate profits. and that is the desired, the right direction of change. the action plan envisages increasing tax transparency both within the european union and vis-à-vis third countries. it is necessary to strengthen the common system of protection against external threats to the revenue of the member states. this will also be the right direction in tax policy, which we should develop and support with effective tools. that is the kind of action we should be calling for today.

mr. chairman, please! the proposal for a sustainable circular economy is perhaps one of the most far-reaching and important projects undertaken by the union. it can, and potentially should, rebuild the entire economy based on the principle of resource efficiency. it can be an opportunity for the union, for all the member states, an opportunity for growth and new jobs. however, we must take into account that the objectives set out in the directive must be chosen realistically, and in particular with regard to the principle of subsidiarity. i would like to thank sirpa petikaïnem for her efforts, who is the rapporteur for this report, the author of it. i have to admit that some of the objectives that have been set here are set in a specific time frame, because we will have a proposal from the european commission in a few months, and it will affect the shape of the european commission's proposal, so i think we are introducing objectives that are going to break down existing regulations, such as the issue of waste incineration; new installations built with national money and eu money, among other things, and they are supposed to have a reduced waste stream. we have to sort this out in some rational way. the requirements of the ecodesign directive are problematic, for example; it is not the ecodesign itself that is difficult, but the requirements that will be imposed on other small and mediumsized enterprises, and we want them to develop as well. i think what is perhaps the most important thing about this whole concept is what mr karl-heinz florenz said: we should appeal to the public's consciousness. if the citizens do not help us, we will not be able to introduce this concept of a circular economy in the european union.
mr. chairman, please! i agree that we should consider a circular economy where waste is recycled and reused. this is a great opportunity not only for the environment, but also for the economy. but i think we should set ambitious but achievable goals. i believe, for example, that increasing the recycling rate of municipal waste to 90% by 2030 will be very difficult for many member states to achieve. the current level is 27%. so i would urge caution against over-regulation: over-regulation is choking the economy, and i hope most of us are aware of that. it is also important to raise awareness among citizens and to support countries in this regard. and i ask that we make european law with caution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the crisis in the dairy sector requires decisive action by the commission. the current milk package does not improve the situation of milk producers and the mechanisms it contains are inefficient and too bureaucratic. in many eu countries, including my own, poland, the proposals for producer organisations have not worked. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the union industry is facing a significant increase in imports of dairy products from the prc, which is likely to lead to a significant increase in the union consumption of dairy products. i also supported this report because of the clause which drew the commission's attention to the problem of high fines for exceeding milk quotas in the last two quota years. this amendment was promoted by myself and my colleagues from the polish delegation of the ecr. the penalties, which particularly affected polish farmers, are not justified on economic grounds, as the limits throughout the eu have not been exceeded.
in writing. ‒ the end of the milk quota system is a major blow to the european dairy sector, which has long been facing difficulties due to the russian embargo. the average price of milk received by producers has fallen by more than 16% over the last year, and the same is true for dairy products, including skimmed milk powder, which has fallen by around 35%. in addition, supplies are continuing to increase, and dairies are struggling to find a large enough market for their products. if we add to this the penalties that member states will have to pay for exceeding the amounts (in some countries this will be hundreds of millions of euros), the crisis in the sector becomes extremely serious. the european commission's efforts to improve the situation on the eu milk market are still not enough. it is essential to put in place mechanisms to mitigate the severe impact of the russian embargo and the end of the quota system. the increase in intervention prices seems necessary in order to enable farmers to obtain compensation at least equal to their production costs. on the other hand, the spread of over-payment penalties over time will mitigate the financial consequences. i also call for the funds from these levies to be returned to the dairy sector, which is in a really difficult situation.
in writing. ‒ a public-private partnership, abbreviated as ppp, is a broadly defined cooperation between public and private sector entities to exploit common opportunities for the provision of public services. the public partner provides the services, while the private partner is responsible for the economic activity and the making of profits. therefore, ppp is not a form of privatisation but a substitute for it. the combination of public services with private capital often results in cost reductions and efficiency gains, as well as in the quality of the services provided. public-private partnerships are very important as they contribute to growth, innovation, competitiveness and job creation. they also affect the development and modernisation of infrastructure. this is a huge opportunity for smes to take advantage of the opportunities offered by the public sector. i believe that an innovative solution such as ppp is beneficial for both sectors, for the member states and for the eu as a whole, because it combines the most important advantages of both sectors without the need for a privatisation process.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the fruit and vegetables sector since the 2007 reform because i believe that the commission should take action to improve the functioning and attractiveness of producer organisations. the level of these organisations in the european union is undoubtedly varied, and in the new member states, including my country, poland, they are fewer and weaker than in the old union countries. i think that these organisations should focus on introducing solutions to increase competitiveness and adapt to consumer needs rather than stockpiling. in the light of the crisis caused by the russian embargo, which has caused the greatest losses to fruit and vegetable producers, it is necessary to simplify the union rules on aid to this sector and to improve the crisis prevention and management instruments linked to the programme. the measures taken by the commission so far have not covered the real losses of producers and therefore new instruments are necessary. i supported this report because it calls on the commission to re-examine the financing rules in the field of crisis prevention and market management.
in writing. ‒ in the fruit and vegetables sector, we have seen a strengthening of producer organisations in recent years, which enable farmers to obtain better prices for their products, to make effective use of eu support and to protect their own interests. this is particularly relevant today, when turbulence in the sector is often caused by factors beyond the farmer's control, such as the 2011 e. coli outbreak or the current russian embargo. in addition, we are increasingly hearing about unfair business practices by large retailers. therefore, initiatives to support the creation of producer organisations should be strengthened, projects to improve the professional qualifications of their workers should be co-financed and mechanisms should be introduced to ensure fair competition in the sector. i would also like to draw attention to another important point, namely the use of instruments to prevent crisis situations. as the rapporteur confirms, these tools have been used to a very limited extent so far. meanwhile, the fruit and vegetable sector is often faced with sudden problems requiring immediate intervention. extraordinary support mechanisms must therefore be available to ensure the stabilisation of the sector and to allow for the rapid compensation of losses suffered by farmers.
in writing. ‒ we adopted the report 'the fruit and vegetable sector since the 2007 reform', which analysed the 2007 reform of the eu fruit and vegetable market, which introduced significant marketing and provided for a support scheme for producer groups and organisations to strengthen the position of fruit and vegetable producers. the report by mrs melo points to major shortcomings in this area and suggests solutions for the future, perhaps the most important of which is to ensure that producers have a greater share in the processing of their products, i.e. that they benefit more from the added value that is created in the field-to-table chain. fruits and vegetables are an important part of every diet, yet their consumption is still too low in europe. the production of fruit and vegetables is largely carried out on smaller farms and requires a high labour input, which provides employment for many people. fruit and vegetables are a particularly significant export item for both the union and poland. in the context of this sector, the situation regarding the russian embargo, which has additionally been recently extended for another year, is particularly important. in this context, we have, together with other members of the committee on agriculture and rural development, written to the commissioner for agriculture, phil hogan, in recent days, calling for the extension of the support mechanisms for producers affected by the embargo.

madam president! the european creative and creative industries contribute to around 4,2% of the union's gdp annually, providing more than 7 million jobs in the member states, including many in the digital environment. unfortunately, current procedures for copyright enforcement on the internet are not working well, if at all, and this is also hindering the growth of innovation. the economic benefits of well-educated workers, innovative research and knowledge exchange between universities and businesses are clear. unfortunately, the european copyright directive, which only regulates non-commercial research purposes, virtually excludes the transfer of knowledge from universities to the private industry sector. european companies cannot compete with their american competitors, who benefit from more flexible regulations abroad. although i have not been able to convince meps of the need to fully harmonise copyright exceptions, i am pleased that they have been reduced to the level of education and libraries, as well as the cross-border access provisions. i hope that the members from the other political groups will keep their word about rejecting certain harmful amendments that restrict, among other things, freedom of panorama and freedom of linking. in its present form, the report is a compromise stretched to its limits between the copyright harmonizationists of which i am a member and the conservative community. as such, it is not fully satisfactory to either party. however, i must congratulate the rapporteur, julia red, on her enthusiasm and patience.
in writing. the report on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright is an own-initiative report, so it does not have legislative power, but is a kind of initiative, it aims to draw attention to certain problems. in general, the document supports the liberalisation of copyright, but an amendment has been proposed which requires the author's or the office's consent for the commercial use of photographs with paintings, works of art or monuments. currently, such photographs can also be published for commercial purposes (in book publishing, television publications or online materials) without the owner's consent and without any payment. if the report were a legally binding act, such an amendment would require the withdrawal of existing products from the market or the author's consent to use the 'panorama' in his publications, which would certainly require complex administrative and legal procedures and would entail the corresponding costs. i hope that in today's vote the european parliament will vote against the restriction of the freedom of the panorama, because there is no indication that the lack of harmonisation of the rules in this area will create any obstacles for creators.
in writing. the report on the implementation of directive 2001/29/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 22 may 2001 on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society is an own-initiative report. the text does not have legislative power, but it does give an idea of what changes in the protection of rights the european parliament believes should be made in the eu. the report emphasises the need to make copyrighted content accessible across borders. the report stresses the importance of territorial licensing, especially for the financing of film and audiovisual production. the report contained a controversial amendment that was supposed to limit the freedom of panoramas, but the final text of the report makes no reference to this issue. after months of negotiations, the legal affairs committee has proposed a common balanced text that, on the one hand, protects the rights of consumers to content acquired legally, and on the other, gives authors the opportunity to protect their rights. the report provides a good basis for the european commission's proposals on copyright reform, which will most likely be presented later this year.
in writing. free-range fishing should be particularly protected. the attempt to insert a clause on the restriction of the freedom of panorama in mrs julia reda's report under discussion today is unfortunately a repeated practice of undermining the legislative process, but also the opinion of parliament itself. i would remind you that most of the countries of the european community have implemented the infosoc directive with the exception of the 'freedom of panorama'. article 33 of the polish copyright act provides for the freedom to distribute works displayed in public collections on public roads, streets, squares, etc. i know that even if we adopted an unreasonable solution in this report, it would not change the law, but it would unfortunately undermine the credibility of ourselves and the stability of the solutions that constitute the basic canon of civil liberties. as you can see, the appeal for common sense is needed again.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - i have to go. i would like to thank very warmly all those who have been involved in the process of preparing this report on my own initiative. i would like to thank in particular my counter-rapporteurs, the secretariats that support us, the staff, including the executive director of the european endowment for democracy, the representatives of the european external action service and the european commission. first of all, i would like to thank the ngo sector, which has been very supportive in evaluating and commenting on the eed's work so far. what is the european fund? this is a foundation created in 2012 under belgian law by the union and the member states, also with the participation of other countries outside the european union. the initiative to establish the fund was taken by the polish presidency in 2011. it's been four years since then, and the fund itself has been running for two years. the initiative is based on the fact that the traditional instruments for promoting democracy have not worked, for example, during the arab spring or in the events that took place east of the european union, in the neighbouring countries. the provisions of the lisbon treaty and the experience of the peaceful transformation of the central and eastern european member states, including the experience of solidarity in poland, also help us in this respect. the fund's task is to respond more quickly, more flexibly than through traditional instruments. it is also intended to support those who have not been supported so far. the fund emphasises the involvement of actors on the ground in countries undergoing this process of change, transformation. it has so far supported over 186 initiatives in virtually all the eu's neighbouring countries, both in the eastern partnership and the union for the mediterranean. and it's worth quoting one of the beneficiaries who said this: after the revolution, after the financial aid was given, they all disappeared. the edf brings a breath of freshness and hope, providing political and moral support not only to old well-established organisations but also to new actors. the eed-supported parties also pass positive checks in democratic elections over time as happened with the euromaidan activists in ukraine. they are now deputies of the supreme council. the eed's ability to provide bridging funding, i.e. funding that persists between the end of one funding and the start of the next from the european union, for example from the edhr fund, is particularly noteworthy. these procedures are more complicated, longer, and therefore oftentimes this period of interruption of funding proves difficult for those who are supported. that's why bridging funding is so important in these cases. as part of the evaluation report, we held a number of debates and hearings to find out how the european endowment for democracy is assessed. among other things, we met with ngos, who told us how they had used the eed, what their experiences were. we also held a number of consultations, both with representatives of the edf and of the collaborating institutions, the european external action service and the commission. the report assessed the two-year action to date and made a number of recommendations. the key conclusions are that the eed fulfils the tasks set out in the statute and, which is particularly important in the european parliament's recommendation of 29 march 2012 on the establishment of the eed. it adds significant value to the european union's toolbox for democracy in the world. at the same time, we call for the edf to be guaranteed sufficient and stable funding in the long term, both from the member states of the union and from the commission itself. it took a positive decision, as the fund received another three-year funding.
in writing. ‒ the eu's trade agreement with the united states strengthens the defence alliance. american investments in poland are among the most desirable. they concern the production sector in innovative fields, which means the creation of high-skilled and well-paid jobs. however, i would like to stress that the ongoing negotiations must take into account the specific nature of polish industry and the sensitivity of certain sectors. it's also a chance to settle some visa issues. i was a professional analyst of international trade agreements. each of them contains some element of arbitration. the isds mechanism in the bilateral polish-us trade agreement, which is the subject of a european debate, has proved to be an acceptable solution. out of 6 arbitration cases, 3 were won by the polish party, 2 ended in a settlement and 1 was won by the investor. ttip also provides an opportunity to improve these conditions. i warn against replacing a well-functioning bilateral mechanism with a european arbitration court. paradoxically, the isds, which is part of bilateral agreements between the us and the countries of central and eastern europe, has not had any negative effects. its inclusion in the eu-us trade agreement enhances the competitive position of the countries in my region in the european union. i'm for a common market from california to the black sea, not from lisbon to vladivostok. our voice must be clear: we want american investment in europe, and in our region in particular. they are not only a guarantee of development, but also of security.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen! the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) aims to stimulate economic growth on both sides of the atlantic. such a unified market, covering one third of world trade, would be worth two trillion euros, which would also translate into a significant increase in employment. in order to benefit from such extensive cooperation, citizens, consumers and employees of companies should be adequately protected. that's why i supported the removal of the clause on the use of isds private arbitration in the contract. the reason why citizens are afraid of ttip is because of isds, with 97% of the nearly 150,000 respondents from the 28 member states opposed to isds in its current form. we cannot leave the fate of millions of citizens in the hands of private arbitration. the isds in the form originally proposed is not needed in eu-us relations and foreign investors should not enjoy more rights than domestic investors. potential disputes should be dealt with in a transparent manner and by independent judges in public hearings, where a review mechanism is in place, consistency of judicial decisions is ensured and the jurisdiction of the courts of the member states is respected. the referral of the amendments to the report to reconsideration by inta did little to change the situation beyond the 'compromise of the compromises' of its chairman, martin schulz. with the assurance that isds will disappear from ttip, i decided to support the entire resolution and i'm glad that most of us here felt the same way.
in writing. ‒ ttip is the world's largest free trade area project, and it is a landmark for both parties, the us and the eu. the question is: will the agreement give the same impetus to economic growth for the contracting parties and will the number of jobs in the countries of the union increase or decrease? there is no doubt that both sides can initially benefit from the use of all the reserves that are not yet used. however, over time, the dominant party may become the american side. this is due to its competitive advantage lower energy and labour costs, and the fact that it has a large number of raw materials at its disposal. looking at global markets in the long term, the eu can become a valuable partner for the us in far eastern markets, including china, the largest creditor of the us. does europe have any other directions for free trade? i'm not sure. it can improve its global competitiveness by opening a free trade area with the eurasian free trade area at the same time as ttip. unfortunately, this direction has been blocked quite effectively for the eu, which unwillingly raises the question of the relationship between ttip and the unrest in ukraine. the ttip should be analysed in a holistic way, including in terms of the shape of the future global market. that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report containing the european parliament's recommendations to the european commission on the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) because i believe that the conclusion of this agreement is important from a geopolitical point of view. the effects of the russian embargo, which are severe for polish farmers, have shown the importance of establishing permanent and solid trade partnerships. in this resolution, the european parliament gave a clear signal to the commission that agriculture should not be a bargaining chip in these negotiations. the report called for a balanced and mutually beneficial agreement to be negotiated, one that would not compromise the quality standards of european food products. i also supported this report because of the call for the identification of a list of sensitive products, although in my view this provision should not only call for the introduction of transitional periods but for the complete exclusion of these products rather than the use of this measure as a last resort. it is good that this report calls for a safeguard clause which can be applied if imports increase to the detriment of member states' economies. the resolution also included an important appeal from the polish citizens to the commission to put pressure on the us government on the visa issue.
in writing. ‒ i am opposed to the eu's continued negotiations with the us on ttip in its current form. the secrecy of the negotiations is the best fuel for the interests of the european citizens to be appropriated by lobbyists and multinationals. the isds mechanism, on the other hand, deprives states of their judicial sovereignty. the reduction of certain european standards, particularly in the field of food safety, is also unacceptable. i am convinced that negotiations should be resumed with the active participation of national parliaments.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the report by mr lange on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). the last-minute compromise on isds proposed by the rapporteur meant that i did not vote against this report. i still have many doubts about the issues of smes, gmos and access to the air and sea transport markets.
in writing. ‒ the fundamental question about ttip is whether it will improve our competitiveness, whether it will be an opportunity or a threat to businesses and consumers. looking at the various statistical analyses, we cannot formulate a definite answer to these questions. nevertheless, the agreement, which aims to liberalise trade between the union and the united states, will undoubtedly lead to increased competition from large us corporations, which most small and medium-sized enterprises may not be able to cope with. as a result, the beneficiaries of this agreement may be mainly large european corporations which are already preparing for its implementation. without sensible protection of our market and regulations to protect consumers and the public interest, we are doomed to domination by commercial and financial interests that are all about economic profit. the ttip agreement may also entail the risk of harmonising norms and standards, unfortunately by bringing them up to the lower, cheaper, us level. this poses a major threat to food safety, labour rights and the further relocation of production to lower cost countries. the mechanism for settling disputes between states and the investor is also highly questionable. in view of the above concerns, i abstained from voting on the resolution on the negotiation of the ttip.
in writing. ‒ the eu-us free trade agreement currently under negotiation, if well and effectively implemented, should bring benefits not only to the contracting parties but also to the global market. it is important that the provisions of this trade agreement support businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, in their equal access to the american and european markets. but i believe that ttip can be a game-changer for the globalisation of prosperity. it's not the united states that migrates to mexico or other latin american countries, and it's not the europeans that migrate to the middle east or africa, but the other way around. this process is proof that democracy and prosperous economic growth in europe and north america are for the people. if so, the leaders of the two contracting states should strive for the globalization of the market, a process that will not only standardize economies but also raise the living standards of people around the world. i therefore voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation to the european commission and hope that the negotiated agreement will not be hampered by obstacles to its implementation.
in writing. ‒ free trade without barriers and borders is a very important thing that can benefit all parties to trade. however, it is often the case that the negotiating partners approach the talks from different positions. the united states is still an economic powerhouse that is very good at identifying and protecting its interests. the european union is not always able to deal with this well enough to take account of the expectations and objections of all the member states. i believe that the negotiation of a trade agreement with the usa is an opportunity which the ec should seize to create conditions for economic cooperation which will give a chance to develop not only the large companies but also the small and medium-sized enterprises. in many cases we must be very vigilant, especially where sectors of the economy that are important to poland can be compromised, as is the case with the chemical industry. the final shape of the isds and the issue of geographical indications of origin of products are also of concern. in these areas, the european parliament must constantly look to the commission for guidance and remind it of the concerns of the citizens of the member states about this agreement. i voted in favour of this report because the eu needs new economic impetus to break the morass of the last decade. this is not unconditional consent, of course, but a negotiating mandate for the commission, which will be settled at the appropriate time.
in writing. ‒ the shareholder engagement directive and the corporate governance statement are another example of the ongoing process of administrative interference with the free market, competition and the freedom to conduct a business that is specific to the european union. i think that this kind of philosophy which is dominant in the community should be changed. fortunately, many of the very controversial provisions in the draft directive have been amended or corrected during the parliamentary work, which is why i did not vote against this proposal. but i would prefer in the future that the european parliament and the other institutions of the european union should deal with more important matters that require real intervention rather than interfering with the free movement of businesses in a competitive market.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report by mr beleta because its assumptions are contrary to the polish national interest. attempts to raise the price of emission allowances are a blow to polish industry and economy, which are characterized by a certain energy structure, strongly based on coal. 90% of poland's electricity production is based on this raw material. there is no doubt that this will result in a change in the choice of energy source on a country-wide scale and will deepen the economic collapse of polish mines. it should be noted that the emissions in poland are only slightly different from the eu average. the old member states, such as germany, luxembourg and belgium, have much higher emissions, but these economies will not experience the change in the price of allowances as strongly as poland. each member state has the right to shape its own energy basket according to its capabilities and needs. i think the eu's interference in this area is going too far.
in writing. ‒ the pursuit of environmental improvement is a necessity that humanity cannot afford to abandon, but it is not the process that should be the goal, but the human being. because in all the initiatives we take in europe and the world, we should remember the people. a clean environment is good for them, of course, but the pursuit of these goals should be a process, an evolution, not a revolution. the aim is to improve the quality of life while avoiding the negative consequences of current actions. radical changes, economic restrictions, including industrial ones, do not have immediate effects on the environment, but they do have a significant impact not only on the situation of companies and their competitiveness, but also on the quality of people's lives. i therefore voted against this decision, considering it to be too far-reaching, with no prospect of improving the environment in the short term, and at the same time posing a serious threat to the economic development of the european union and its individual member states.
in writing. ‒ i am opposed to this resolution because i believe that the decision on the conditions of employment of seafarers should be left to the member states. i also think that regulation of this sector is unnecessary because it creates excessive bureaucracy and administrative constraints. it is ridiculous to say the least that the union is engaging hundreds of mps and tens of thousands of officials to decree the right of seafarers to access the internet on board ship.
in writing. ‒ despite the application of eu labour law to all sectors and categories of workers, seafarers have so far been excluded from the scope of the following directives: 2008/94/ec, 2009/38/ec, 2002/14/ec, 98/59/ec and 2001/23/ec. depending on the situation at national level, this exemption may have a negative impact on the rights enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights, in particular with regard to the right to information and consultation and the right to decent working conditions. as only some member states made use of these exemptions, this led to a situation where the same categories of workers were treated differently in different member states. i voted for mrs morin-chartier's report because it is important to ensure equal treatment and equal rights for all workers.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the commission’s proposal to extend labour directives to seafarers. seafarers up until now have been excluded from several protective labour directives, including the insolvency directive, the collective redundancies directive and the transfer of undertakings directive. having a well-qualified and experienced staff is vital for the health and growth of the maritime industry throughout the union. as the number of seafarers is decreasing, ensuring that seafarers enjoy uniform rights across all member states is essential to ensuring that the european maritime industry is well staffed. extending the protection of these social policy directives to seafarers ensures their protection under the european charter of fundamental rights. this measure will hopefully ensure that all labourers are treated fairly across member states, leading to more interest in maritime careers, thus preserving the european maritime know-how for future generations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. the financial and economic crisis and its social consequences justify the need to reformulate the employment guidelines for member states' policies. one of them is to promote equal opportunities and to combat poverty and social exclusion, which affect 120 million europeans. the fight against poverty and exclusion must be based above all on growth and employment and on modern and effective social protection. to ensure such effective, efficient and simplified social protection, it should be combined with a broad set of social policies covering: targeted education, promotion and support of social justice, health, housing, anti-discrimination, reconciliation of private and professional life through the provision of high quality care for children and non-independent adults, and family policy. reforms of pension systems to ensure decent living conditions and equal opportunities for women and men are also important.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because job creation and the protection of workers' rights should be a priority of european policy. the job-friendly economic recovery in europe is still not there, which is a prerequisite for ensuring decent living standards for people and strengthening the economy. the review of the europe 2020 strategy provides an opportunity to make quality job creation and improving working conditions a pillar of eu policy.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the debate on european employment policy, i would like to draw attention to two issues: the way in which this policy is conducted and its monitoring. the european union is taking many actions and is presenting many guidelines for employment growth, which are mentioned in the reports adopted today, and which are unfortunately presented to europeans mostly as national actions. those considered less popular are presented as european recommendations. such rhetoric is wrongly increasing the dislike of the eu institutions among eu citizens. it is therefore important that citizens are properly informed about the actions and initiatives we are proposing for them. so that on the one hand they can engage with them effectively, and on the other hand to strengthen their trust in our work. in addition, it is important that the development and implementation of employment policies be consulted with local authorities and take account of local and regional disparities. in the context of monitoring the effects of this policy, we need to strengthen the ways in which we assess the actions taken. the monitoring and evaluation should be carried out with the involvement of the authorities at all levels, the social partners and civil society, as proposed by parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by laura agee because i think it is a good and substantive document. i fully agree with the rapporteur that member states' policies at central, regional and local level should promote job creation by removing bureaucratic barriers, promoting and training entrepreneurial skills among young people, developing micro and small enterprises and promoting employment in the white and green sectors and the blue economy. i am also convinced that the implementation of policies aimed at equalising the opportunities of disadvantaged groups, in particular children and young people from families affected by poverty, the unemployed, immigrants and people with disabilities, is socially beneficial and leads to an increase in the employment rate of these groups in society.
in writing. ‒ according to eurostat data for 2015, the number of unemployed in the eu stands at 23 815 000, of which over 18 million are from the euro area. efforts should be made to develop indicators of absolute poverty and to combat poverty and social exclusion. in this context, it is also important to take into account the role and problems of schooling. member states should take joint action to tackle the effects of unemployment, promote the training of science workers and the employment of lower-skilled workers, and open up the eu labour market. income protection, social guarantees and compliance with labour law should be taken into account when designing policies that affect the eu labour market. it is also important to work towards making the union labour market more attractive, with a view to stimulating the activity of citizens belonging to different age groups. there is also a need to tackle the social impact of unemployment by collecting reliable data on absolute poverty, welfare systems and removing administrative barriers. we should pay particular attention to measures to ensure access to quality education, to address weaknesses in education systems and to ensure that as many people as possible are properly trained. it is also essential to combat any discriminatory practices in the labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the green jobs initiative report because i believe it addresses important issues facing the eu economy today. the so-called green economy is a growing sector with huge potential for growth and job creation. however, the transition to green employment is not only an opportunity but also a challenge. i believe that the final version of the report, which was the result of negotiations between all the political groups, maintained the right balance between these two aspects and addressed many important issues. i am pleased that the role that smes can play in the green economy has been highlighted and that it has been stressed that any changes should not result in additional burdens for entrepreneurs. i also believe that the transition to a green economy must not be achieved simply by increasing investment in new technologies or introducing new regulations. first and foremost, we need to invest in social capital and equip workers with the right skills that employers are looking for in a changing labour market where some jobs will certainly be created, but others will inevitably be replaced.
in writing. - i voted against because i think the whole project is absurd and unnecessary. the whole climate package, green energy and green jobs is just an idealization of economic life. this green ideology translates into difficulties in business, many times more expensive than, for example, energy in the usa, additional fiscal and administrative burdens. it is the proposals for additional fiscal burdens that i consider particularly damaging.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on resource efficiency: moving towards a circular economy. i believe that moving towards a circular economy requires two basic criteria:the life (cycle) of the product;the ease of disassembly and the possibility of recycling. this first criterion depends on reliability, i.e. physical wear and tear and the loss of the use, aesthetic or other characteristics of so-called moral wear and tear. the latter depends on the design of the product which facilitates (allows) easy disassembly and is made of materials which are suitable for deliberate recycling rather than forced disposal. it is necessary to establish legislation to ensure that both these criteria are fully met when products are placed on the market. of course, the additional important criteria for the placing of products on the market should be the complete safety of the consumer as well as the safety and protection of the environment (climate). for this latter purpose, it is necessary to introduce a differentiated environmental tax and a corresponding scrap tax.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the implementation of the circular economy model is the answer to key challenges for european union policy, such as increasing employment and growth, promoting innovation, re-industrialisation and the smart use of resources. in a circular economy, existing materials and products are continuously reused and recycled, and thus waste is minimised. it is a model that is necessary to maximize the productivity of available natural resources, which will bring significant economic benefits.
in writing. ‒ the rational management of resources is particularly important for the eu, as resources are essential for the proper functioning of industry and many other sectors of the economy, which provide eu citizens with a variety of key products and services. we must not forget that europe remains one of the world's largest importers of raw materials, and that about 40% of the materials used in the eu come from outside. for some substances, such as phosphorus, which is important for agriculture, the dependence on imports is even greater. it is important to take a sensible approach to resource efficiency and savings, as we cannot allow these actions to lead to a lower security of supply of certain goods and services and a decrease in competitiveness. however, where possible and safe for the eu economy, new waste management solutions, the creation of a closed loop of non-renewable resources, greater use of renewable energy sources and water management actions should be promoted. in addition, available data indicate that water supply issues may soon become a major problem in some countries. better use of available resources would have a positive impact on both the economy and the environment and would support job creation.
in writing. ‒ i am a supporter of a rationally developed circular economy. the concept that we don't have to own everything, but we can borrow or repair things that are getting old, is a good idea. however, i believe that the european parliament's report, despite its proper purpose, contained many solutions that were impossible to implement for economic, political and social reasons. i also believe that this report, if it were to be implemented as it stands, could threaten some of the 350 000 jobs in european industry, with the result that our entrepreneurs would be replaced by companies from outside the european union. they are not burdened by the same environmental requirements as the european ones. i have therefore decided to vote against the report by sirpa pietikäinen.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the european security agenda. the effective implementation of this comprehensive agenda requires adequate financial resources. we therefore need clear declarations from the council of support for the actions being taken at different levels under this agenda. in this context, i would like to emphasise the role of education and integration programmes as tools to combat the causes of radicalisation. we also need new programmes that help to spread awareness of radicalisation and help to extend cooperation in this area to all stakeholders. new innovative tools to combat terrorist propaganda online and to develop critical thinking skills among young people are also important.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because it addresses all the key issues in the region and gives hope for a peaceful solution to the key security challenges in the middle east and north africa. the focus was primarily on the fight against isis and other extremist groups and support for political change in tunisia and the development of civil society. the report also addresses the issue of ending the civil war in syria and ensuring the peaceful nature of iran's nuclear programme in return for reintegration into the international community.
in writing. ‒ i fully support and expressed this in my vote on the report by mr eduard koukan the demands for a review, revision and change of the european neighbourhood policy. the objective of this policy to develop an area of common stability, security and prosperity remains as relevant as ever, as does the method of financing the neighbourhood policy under the principle 'more for more'. however, the growing economic crisis and subsequent armed and political conflicts outside the eu's borders show that the union should engage more dynamically and decisively in partnership to support the transformation of our southern and eastern neighbours towards democratisation, the rule of law and greater respect for human rights. it is also important to separate the neighbourhood policy from the policy towards the eu's associated countries and to bear in mind the diversity and specificity of the eu's neighbouring countries, their different interests, motivations and different possibilities for change. i therefore support the report's call for the appointment of high representatives specialising in the eu's eastern and southern foreign policies. bilateral policies between the eu and its neighbours should also be coordinated and strengthened, particularly in the areas of security, border protection, and the fight against trafficking in human beings and economic crime. i also support the call for increased funding for the eastern partnership, whose importance is often underestimated, and for an evaluation of the procedures and appropriateness of the current spending on the neighbourhood policy.
in writing. ‒ since 2004, when the european neighbourhood policy was launched, we have seen a marked increase in threats in the eu's immediate neighbourhood. war has been raging for months on the eu's eastern border in ukraine, and russia continues to fuel political conflict in georgia and moldova for its own ends. on the southern border, the arab spring is having a devastating effect, with wars and an uncontrolled wave of emigration. the problem of war-torn syria remains unresolved, and the islamic state is growing in strength in the area, with its reach and criminal activities reaching further and further. an effective neighbourhood policy is needed now more than ever, which is why i voted in favour of the cookan report. the eu's security requires a firm and coherent stance towards moscow and concrete solutions to the challenges from the south. this cannot be achieved without eu diplomacy, and i hope that commissioner mogherini and her european external action service will step up their efforts in this regard.
in writing. ‒ the report adopted today is a signal to the european commission that some of the existing copyright, exceptions and limitations need to be reviewed and better adapted to the fast-changing digital environment. our priority should be to improve the protection of fundamental rights such as the fight against discrimination and the protection of press freedom, but also to adopt an exception allowing libraries to legally borrow works in digital formats for personal use. one of the most controversial topics of the discussion was the so-called freedom of panorama, that is, the possibility of taking unlimited photos in public spaces against the background of buildings or works of art. i voted with conviction today against paragraph 46 of the draft report, which introduced a restriction on this freedom. i am glad that this was not included in the final report and that is why i supported the final text of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because it guarantees the protection of the rights of authors and performers on the one hand, and access to culture and information on the other. it also strengthens some exceptions and limitations, but it ensures good conditions for the creative sector and promotes the preservation of european cultural diversity. i voted against paragraph 46 of that report, which restricts 'the freedom of the panorama', because the consequence of the amendments would be to prohibit the free use of images of objects in public spaces in photographs, which would significantly restrict access to information. i believe that such restrictions have no place in the modern information society.
in writing. ‒ on 9 july 2015, the european parliament adopted a controversial non-legislative report by a member of the council. the report focuses on aspects of the implementation of the information society directive ahead of the european commission's proposal for copyright reform, which is to be presented at a later date. among the report's findings was the controversial issue of the panorama, which has aroused considerable public discontent. the ecr group supports the maintenance of the status quo in the member states and voted to remove any references to the 'panorama law' project as the proposed solution is inappropriate and restricts citizens' rights. as a result, due to the fact that there are different views on this issue in different eu member states, the report was adopted without any reference to the 'panorama act'.
in writing. ‒ the mep's report has generated a lot of media interest and a lot of excitement among both the creative community and internet users, in particular on the issue of the so-called freedom of panorama, to which the final text of the report makes no reference. i have decided to abstain from voting on the final text for two reasons. firstly, it is an own-initiative report which does not change the legislation in any of the member states of the european union, but merely indicates a wish list of what needs to be improved and in which areas the commission should carry out analyses on the future harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights. the result is that we maintain the status quo, whereby each member state will continue to decide for itself whether to introduce restrictions on the freedom of the panorama. secondly, i think the report should focus on the implementation of the information society directive, but very little of the final text deals with this issue.
in writing. ‒ copyright, like the right of every creator to dispose of his or her own work, should be subject to special protection. intellectual property, like any other property, should be protected by law and no creator should feel that his legal position is weaker and that his rights to dispose of and benefit from his work are ignored or marginalised. the digital age has created many new opportunities for creators to present their works to a wide audience, but it has also led to the emergence of new forms of copyright infringement. the european union wants and must respond to this challenge and the need to regulate copyright properly. i think that the report adopted today is a good step in the right direction and that is why i voted in favour of it. but you can't go beyond the boundaries of common sense in trying to protect the interests of creators. this was the case with panorama freedom, which has been the subject of wide debate throughout the eu. i think that the imposition of very strict regulations on most member states in this area is unjustified and harmful. citizens cannot be held liable for, for example, taking photographs of familiar places when travelling in europe and wanting to share these photographs with their friends via social media platforms. that's why i voted against amendment 46 to restrict freedom of the press.
in writing. ‒ 11 july 2015 marks the 20th anniversary of the srebrenica massacre, which took place during the bosnian war. the city, despite being a safe zone protected by un troops, was taken over by bosnian serb forces and paramilitary units, including serbian irregular police units. over 8,000 muslim men and boys were murdered in the days of slaughter, and nearly 30,000 women, children and elderly people were deported in a massive campaign of ethnic cleansing. the process of european integration, and the creation of the european union, is based on the desire to prevent wars and crimes, such as those that took place 20 years ago in the former yugoslavia, from ever happening again in europe. i fully condemn the srebrenica genocide and have therefore voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution by the five largest political groups in the ep.

member of the commission.– mr president, i think we are discussing cambodia, so we can come back to the hungarian situation some other time. as many of you have pointed out, cambodia does indeed have a very vibrant civil society, and many ngos and associations are active in various areas. the cambodian government has for many years argued that an overarching law on associations and ngos was necessary to provide simple and transparent regulation to the sector. we in the european union have been following this very closely since the idea of the legislation first surfaced many years ago. the draft laws have been a recurring topic in informal and formal meetings between the eu and the cambodian government. our delegation and our ambassador there are very active and have frequent contact at different levels to make sure that our views on this are crystal clear and passed on to the government. we have made clear to them that the legislation that they are planning should enable, and not limit, freedom of association and expression in cambodia. we have pointed out that a democratic process needs to be transparent and include meaningful consultation with all relevant stakeholders. a culture of dialogue is the basis of any democracy – dialogue with the opposition, civil society and the private sector. it is only through this dialogue that the government can take into account the needs and concerns of those who are subject to the legislation, and an inclusive process enables government to enact laws that are truly in the interest of the people. the national assembly of cambodia has a very important role to play here, so we welcome the decision by the national assembly to organise consultations on the draft ngo law, and some of these have actually started to take place already. we hope that the results of this will be reflected in the text of the law. it is also important to have, as some of you do, peer-to-peer contacts between european parliament members and members of the cambodian national assembly, in order to help them strengthen the capacity to scrutinise and to improve legislation in close contact with civil society and in a spirit of dialogue. we will continue to monitor the situation and developments, because in times when civil society and trade unions often face increasing obstacles and restrictions in many countries, cambodia has an opportunity to prove that it is truly committed to strengthening its democratic credentials.
i'm closing the debate. the vote will take place after the debate.

in writing.– the legal basis for respecting the fundamental rights of eu citizens used to be in the references in the treaties to the echr. however, with the treaty of lisbon coming into force, the charter of fundamental rights was given the same legally binding status as all other treaties, meaning that all member states shall prioritize the respect of fundamental rights. the situation is not exactly desirable. of course, we seem to be within the limit of normal, there are no evident cases of capital punishment or tortures, nonetheless, as a member of the petitions committee i have observed that the petitions regarding breaches of fundamental rights exceeds the acceptable standards. most of them concern the discrimination on sex or origin basis. moreover, the easily noticed tendency is that the less economic stability, the higher the amount of fundamental rights violations recorded. i believe that we should be able to strengthen the monitoring mechanism in order to prevent the breaches from happening in member states of eu. unfortunately, having in mind the migration crisis, we must be prepared for the significant increase of number of petitions concerning violations of fundamental rights based on the origin, and since no consensus has been reached so far, we will not be able to control it.
i would like to draw the commission's attention to the situation of polish farmers, who are suffering from a drought on an unprecedented scale, as is clearly shown by the lowest water levels in our country's largest rivers in two hundred years. the losses estimated so far in crop production alone are in the billions of euros, and all indications are that they will shift to animal production in the autumn due to the dramatic shortage of so-called bulk feed. it is true that the polish government has announced support for farmers, but only as de minimis aid, which means that some farmers will receive it in a situation where the very basis of the existence of most farms is threatened. moreover, the budget allocated to this aid is around eur 100 million, which means that it is not enough to compensate for the losses or even to restore agricultural production for the following year. i therefore ask the commission once again to take an urgent interest in the effects of the drought in poland and other countries of central and eastern europe and to provide aid commensurate with the scale of the threat from the so-called crisis reserve. thank you very much. thank you.

member of the commission.– madam president, the commission would like to thank the rapporteur mr diaconu and the shadow rapporteurs for the quality and the comprehensiveness of his report. the report covers the full breadth of cultural heritage, making a wide spectrum of policy recommendations and suggesting next steps to be taken. the commission shares the report’s view that supporting, enhancing and promoting cultural heritage through an integrated approach is of paramount importance. in addition to its intrinsic value, cultural heritage contributes significantly to economic and social development and it touches the lives of all europeans, nurturing their sense of belonging and strengthening their european identity. as we speak, heritage is unfortunately the target of acts of vandalism, defacement and even destruction, as we can see in the terrible images of destruction in iraq and syria. but there are also other, less violent, threats to heritage. we are so used to our surrounding historic environment that we may forget that such a fragile beauty needs a lot of care to survive. the report will help the commission to fine-tune the existing instruments and to make further progress on putting into practice tools, policies and mechanisms in an integrated way to address the challenges the heritage sector is facing today. the commission has already taken action on many of the spheres of action mentioned in the report. the commission has started to work with the member states on participatory governance. in 2016-2017 this work will be continued on heritage skills, training and knowledge transfer. the commission is also promoting peer learning among cities and regions to support the exchange and transfer of the wealth of experience and good cultural practices, including heritage. the commission will also continue to enhance internal cooperation and availability of information on financing opportunities within the existing european funding programmes. if i might just respond to the honourable member’s observations: unfortunately, my answer is the same as it was during my hearing. the commission has no powers to handle debates between two member states and historic debates. we have simply no powers for that; these are bilateral conflicts and bilateral discussions.

in writing. ‒ a 21st century society should not tolerate forced labour in any form or under any circumstances in a free market. i am therefore pleased that the european parliament has agreed to ratify the protocol to the 1930 international labour organisation convention on forced or compulsory labour. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the protocol of 2014 on the forced labour convention of the international labour organization with regard to matters related to social policy. the protocol’s provisions are strongly connected to fundamental rights. forced labour is, in fact, a significant violation of rights stated in article 5 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which has a legally binding status since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon in december 2009. the protocol introduces new measures that can prove very useful in combating forced labour. one of the most important provisions focuses on making efforts to ensure that enforcement of legislation related to the prevention of labour exploitation applies to all economic sectors. moreover, the other purpose of the protocol is to ensure that labour inspection services are strengthened. this is essential for us to minimise the aforementioned problem; however, we must also take steps to help the victims of labour exploitation. this protocol establishes protection for them together with access to remedies such as compensation. i believe that this protocol will help us to move forward and hopefully eliminate forced labour from our society.
in writing. ‒ the forced labour convention is one of the eight fundamental ilo conventions. the council adopted a decision authorising member states to ratify the parts of the protocol to the forced labour convention falling within the eu's competence. the support for the council's decision in this respect is linked to doubts that have arisen at the time of the implementation of the convention by some member states as to the competence of the union to negotiate on behalf of the member states. the legal basis in the treaty allowing the council to adopt decisions defining a common position in an international organisation of which the eu is not a member was also called into question. the council decision therefore seems to be worthy of support.

in writing. – as we have already agreed in the committee on agriculture and rural development, cloning basically should be prohibited in the european market. scientific studies showed that cloning leads to malformations of the animal’s uterus and foetus. we cannot know for certain whether food from cloned species will be dangerous to human health or not. moreover, the question of traceability poses serious technical difficulties, especially to farmers, who would certainly need to bear additional costs for keeping track of cloned animals’ descendants. that is a heavy burden, both financially and administratively. other doubts are raised in connection with ethics and religious beliefs: cloning interferes in animal welfare and rises moral questions. animals should be treated as sentient beings, not a commodity. our task, as politicians, is to represent our citizens. european consumers do not like the idea of cloning, and, what is more, the idea of producing food from cloned animals. therefore, we reject the proposal.

in writing. ‒ the production of safe and healthy food should be based on natural methods. only then can we be sure that the products that end up on our tables are not time bombs. the use of cloning for animal husbandry is therefore unacceptable to all who have the welfare of both humans and farm animals at heart. the fact that we currently have little evidence of the impact of eating food that has been cloned or genetically modified is a testament to the difficulty of conducting such robust research. in this situation, we consumers will be the guinea pigs and bear the long-term consequences of the introduction of such products. europe is able to produce enough food using natural methods and it is unwise, even economically, to look for artificial ways of increasing its food supply, because it will hurt its producers. i therefore fully support the permanent ban on animal cloning and the extension of this ban.

in writing. ‒ for decades, it has been said that the european economy is based on family businesses, and that they are its healthy foundation. the recent economic crisis has made very clear the strength of these companies, which is mainly due to their long-term growth strategy and lack of a drive for quick profit. unfortunately, many family businesses face difficulties in accessing finance, over-stretched administrative requirements or a tax system. the fact that every year 150 000 european companies are wound up because of succession difficulties and that as a result nearly 600 000 people lose their jobs is a very clear indication of the scale of this phenomenon. action to protect family businesses is therefore necessary. i agree with the rapporteur that the member states have a key role to play in this respect. the union has little say in this area, as it is often a matter of tax policy and internal labour law. a good step could be to try to create a single european definition of a family business but this requires taking into account the local specificities in each member state. the union should also consider some form of promotion of this business model in countries with a small tradition of family businesses. it is also worthwhile to get involved in preparing family businesses for generational changes so that the number of businesses that are closed down does not increase dramatically in the coming years.
