in writing. ‒ this report highlights the particular importance and value of cultural heritage as a common good and resource. the commission was also asked to create a single eu portal dedicated to tangible and intangible cultural heritage, gathering information from all eu programmes financing cultural heritage and focusing on three main aspects: databases of tangible and intangible resources, possibilities for financing cultural heritage, data on the state of european cultural heritage and data relevant to the preservation of this heritage. it calls for support through targeted funding, analysis, research and pilot actions, and the establishment of a newly introduced principle of multi-source funding, which allows for the complementary use of different european funds in the same large-scale project. the issue of increasing the financial burden on small infrastructure projects to the level of funding received by unesco projects was also raised. member states were also asked to consider applying tax credits to restaurant work and to engage in a dialogue with representatives of the cultural sector. all this is aimed at increasing the level of care for cultural heritage, which is an essential part of the european tradition, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the cultural sector is not covered by community policies. that's good, that's good. by remaining in the hands of state governments, of various local governments, culture is better protected in its diversity and originality. it is good, however, that parliament, the culture committee, is taking up the subject of cultural heritage and the activities of contemporary artists on a fairly regular basis. recently, at my request, we have been looking at the situation in syria and iraq, where very valuable monuments have been destroyed. the act of aggression was not on the occasion, not as a result of the side effects of war, but because of the monuments themselves. this is an extraordinary act of vandalism. today we have a report on heritage, primarily european. a good report, preceded by an interesting debate in committee. i want to highlight its value and thank the rapporteur.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative (eci) is a new mechanism of participatory democracy that, since 2012, allows eu citizens to directly influence and shape the political agenda. the citizens' initiative 'right to water', known as 'right2water', was legalised with almost two million signatures from citizens from all eu countries, and became the first success of this mass petition. in view of this, we might expect the european commission to react accordingly. instead, we got a response that was vague, lacking ambition. in particular, the commission has not presented any legislative proposal that would be key to the right2water initiative. in response, the european parliament endorsed the report on its own initiative and encourages the commission to honour its commitments. however, we are witnessing an attempt to weaken this report and to present an alternative solution which lacks all the key elements voted on in the envi committee. the european citizens' initiative aims to show citizens that the eu is willing to get involved in the issues that matter to them. we must remember that the unity of the european institutions on such obvious issues as universal access to water is important not only from the point of view of the legislative procedure but also from a purely moral perspective.
in writing. – ‘right to water’ is an initiative to provide every human with access to water and sanitation and it is the very first initiative which has met the requirements set out in the regulation of the european parliament and the council on the citizens’ initiative. more than 1.9 million citizens supported the petition to bring it to the european commission and finally to the parliament. according to the citizens’ opinion, internal market rules do not apply to water since it is not commodity, but a public good. therefore it should be excluded from liberalisation. the united nations organization recommends that a household should not spend more than 3% of its income to pay for water. i agree with the author's opinion that we should give high priority to water access and sanitation within the official development assistance framework to support the sector in developing countries.
in writing. ‒ water is an essential element of human functioning, not only biologically but also economically. for these reasons, it must be considered a strategic resource for humanity, one to which every human being must be guaranteed equal access. the measures taken to achieve this are certainly right and worthy of support. however, in pursuing those objectives, states or public entities should not be regarded as merely reliable and certain in providing access to that resource. the private sector should also be able to carry out its business tasks in this area, directly or indirectly, for example through public-private partnerships, in conjunction with the obligations incumbent on the state.
president of the council. madam president, honourable members of the european parliament, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i have the honour to present to you the council's position on the draft budget of the european union for the year 2016, adopted unanimously by the council on 4 september. the main objective is to support economic recovery, investment and job creation on the one hand, and to stimulate the financing of the union's external action in the field of migration policies on the other. the budget is therefore a reflection of solidarity both internally and externally. i'm going to give you a three-part presentation. the first will be devoted to current affairs, the second to the seven main principles which guided the council's agreement and, finally, the third to the highlights. in view of the tragic situation we are facing and in view of the tens of thousands of refugees who have fled war and put their hopes in europe, i would like to stress the support that the european union is providing at the moment, in addition to the initiatives of the member states. the european aid to the current migration situation and the asylum-seekers crisis is one of the manifestations of this internal and external solidarity. some figures: the two main funds under shared management are the asylum, migration and integration fund and the esf, which have €3.1 billion and €3.7 billion respectively for the period 2014-2020. in 2015, more than 45 national programmes were approved for just over 1 billion commitment appropriations. the commission has already released just over 210 million in prefinancing. the emergency aid component of these two funds also made it possible to release just over 60 million. the council and the european parliament jointly endorsed the european agenda on migration in may 2015, which is based on four pillars and aims to improve the management of migration flows. we have also approved amending budget no 5 to this end. the european union is also one of the main donors in the region surrounding syria, with €855 million allocated for humanitarian aid to syrian refugees in lebanon, jordan and turkey in 2016. as regards the relocation of refugees, the council accepted all the commitment appropriations for greece and italy amounting to eur 150 million. these issues will certainly be addressed by commission president jean-claude juncker in his state of the union address tomorrow, where he will also highlight and set out a new package of measures in this area. the second part will be devoted to the seven main principles which have guided the council's work. first, we felt it was important to address and resolve the problem of late payments, which could be resolved by the end of 2016. the council position includes the appropriations necessary to implement the agreement on the payment schedule in 2015 and 2016. second, the council has retained all the appropriations for the european fund for strategic investments in 2016, which is a top priority. thirdly, the migration policy has considerable funds, including temporary measures for greece and italy to relocate 40 000 refugees to their own countries, and the asylum, migration and integration fund, which will receive 515 million euros, an increase of 35% in 2016 compared to 2015. the fourth great principle is humanitarian aid. payment appropriations increase by 16% in 2016 compared to 2015 to reach over eur 1 billion. the fifth principle is that the reductions in appropriations have been made in accordance with guidelines based on several parameters, namely the rate at which the project programmes are progressing, the rate of implementation of projects which has been achieved and is expected to be achieved and, finally, the foreseeable and realistic absorption capacity of the various programmes. the sixth guiding principle: the budget lines adjusted by the council are mainly those for which the commission had proposed very large increases. so it is to these very high figures that we have applied downward adjustments. but if you look at the absolute increase in appropriations in these areas, you will see that the increases are still substantial. the seventh and final principle: in the face of the political instability, sometimes dramatic, around the european union, the council has decided to leave sufficient room for manoeuvre to act in the event of increased tensions and conflicts. i shall very shortly review the details of the council's position, which was adopted unanimously on 4 september. the proposal covers commitment appropriations of 153.3 billion and payment appropriations of 142.1 billion. the increase in payment appropriations was 0.6% and the decrease in commitment appropriations was 5.4%. we are therefore very close to the 5% reduction proposed by the commission. the position we have adopted makes it possible to reduce the gap between commitment appropriations and payment appropriations and, therefore, the remaining balance to be settled, and therefore reduces the risk of payment arrears. let us now consider the highlights of each section. under the heading 'competitiveness for growth and employment', which is at the heart of the political priorities for investment and employment, payment appropriations increased by 8.6% and commitment appropriations by 7%. in order to implement the european fund for strategic investments, which is a top priority, redeployments have been selected for the following: the horizon 2020 programme and the connecting europe facility (cef). funding for major infrastructure projects has also been reduced, notably galileo, iter and copernicus, as well as for joint ventures. despite the reductions, the payment appropriations allocated to horizon 2020 increased by 9,3% (840 million) compared to 2015, to reach eur 9,9 billion, a considerable figure. the council also slightly adjusted the mechanism for interconnection in europe downwards. however, the commitment appropriations are increasing by 53% (eur 760 million) and the payment appropriations by 14% (eur 203 million), which is very close to the commission's proposals. the cosme and erasmus programmes, which are very popular, were not affected by the cuts. i would point out that the erasmus+ programme will have a budget of eur 1.8 billion in 2016, which represents an increase of 30% compared to 2015. in the heading 'economic, social and territorial cohesion', appropriations decreased very slightly by 0.45%. under the heading 'sustainable growth: natural resources', there was a slight reduction of 0.45% in payment appropriations and 0.32% in commitment appropriations compared with the commission's proposals. in heading 3 'security and citizenship', which i already stressed in my first part, commitment appropriations increased sharply compared to 2015 (8.7%) and payment appropriations increased by more than 15%. this increase mainly concerns actions in the field of migration, a political priority of the european union. the council also accepted the use of the flexibility instrument. in heading 4 the council largely adopted the commission's proposals. payment appropriations increased by 22.4% to over eur 9 billion. i would like to stress that the council has aligned itself with the commission's figures in such fundamental areas as humanitarian aid, civil protection, macro-financial assistance to third countries, the guarantee fund for external action and support for the palestinians. in heading 5 'administration', the proposal provides for a moderate reduction of 31 million which will not affect the proper functioning of the institutions of the european union. the council has not changed the administrative budget of the european parliament, but will remain vigilant about the continuation of the planned 5% reduction in staff until 2017. a meeting was also decided upon during our budgetary trilogue in july so that parliament, the commission and the presidency could discuss this issue together. in conclusion, madam president, ladies and gentlemen of the european parliament, aware of the challenges ahead, particularly on the migration front, and in view of the intensifying conflicts around the european union, the council has deemed it essential to find a balanced and responsible compromise which leaves a certain margin of manoeuvre to deal with the worsening situation which is obvious. the budget is therefore marked by this internal and external solidarity, which is very important to us all.
member of the commission.– madam president, i would like first of all to thank minister gramegna for his presentation of the council’s reading of our draft budget for 2016. the commission fully shares the view that budgetary discipline and sound management is what people expect from us, but our citizens of course also expect that we attend to urgent needs in these times of many ongoing crises. president juncker will present tomorrow, in his state of the union speech, proposals for the refugee crisis. furthermore, in response to recent market developments in the dairy sector, the commission announced yesterday a comprehensive package of measures for eur 400 million of eu funds to be used for the benefit of farmers immediately. the financial impact of the migration package and the agricultural basis will be reflected in an amending letter to be proposed in october. this amending letter will include the higher-than-expected surplus in the agricultural sector. let me now turn to the original proposal of the commission on which the council reading was based. the draft budget for 2016 is a comprehensive proposal covering all political priorities: to stimulate investment, growth and jobs, through the agreement reached on the european fund for strategic investments, amending letter no 1; to improve our capacity to meet the collective challenge of migration; to reinforce europe in the world. our proposal still leaves a margin of eur 2.1 bn in commitments and eur 1.6 bn in payments below the already tight mff ceilings. all in all our draft budget for 2016 is a proposal for a responsible budget, a budget for the many competing needs of europe, and a budget that has a margin for unforeseen events. regarding payments, we have a draft budget that respects the agreed payment plan and that will bring us back to a sustainable budget for cohesion policy. the commission welcomes the council’s reading with regard to the 2007-2013 budget for cohesion policy programmes in heading 1b. however, we are concerned about the proposed cuts on a range of selected budget lines across headings, supposedly justified by low implementation rates in mid-june. our proposal aims at reversing the effect of payment shortages from the last years, including in headings for external actions. for many of the budgetary lines affected by the proposed cuts, the situation has radically changed since last year. we now have high implementation rates, especially under heading 4, instead of delays, and from our point of view as a result there is no reason to reduce these budget lines. with regard to commitments, i see with satisfaction that the council is endorsing the commission proposal on migration. let me stress that important actions were already taken in 2015 to address migration challenges. twenty-three multiannual national programmes under the asylum, migration and integration fund and the internal security fund are approved, and some eur 205 million of pre-financing has already been paid out to our member states for both funds – eur 122 million from the asylum, migration and integration fund and eur 83 million from the internal security fund. money will now be able to flow. what we propose in 2016 is a continuation of the amending budget proposed in 2015, and more must be done in the next years. regarding heading 1a on growth and jobs, the commission does not share the council’s view on the reasons why the substantial cuts on programmes such as horizon 2020 or the energy strand of the connecting europe facility, are decoupled from political priorities like the energy union, or the spirit of our agreement on the financing of the european fund for strategic investments. under heading 4, cuts are proposed in our main programmes for the neighbourhood, pre-accession and development cooperation. reducing the extent of our assistance in the mediterranean will not increase security and will run contrary to the overall political goal for the economic development of this region so close to us. on administrative expenditure, for a number of years already the commission, as well as a number of other institutions, has shown self-restraint and sound administrative management. we have continued working with limited increases in administrative expenditure. we are progressing towards our achievement of a 5% staff reduction target over five years, yet the council’s position seems to ignore these efforts. i will just give you one example. for the commission, if we were to undergo the council’s proposal to cut eur 19 million we would have to freeze 206 posts on top of a 4% staff reduction to be achieved by 2016. likewise, cuts to administrative support expenditure, research staff and executive agencies across all the headings would be extremely harmful for the proper implementation of programmes. let me conclude my statement with some elements regarding the process. in mid-october, the commission will present an amending letter containing an update for agriculture and the budgetary implication of the new package on migration which president juncker will announce tomorrow before this european parliament. we look forward to parliament’s reading and trust that by the end of the conciliation period we will find a common way ahead for the 2016 budget.

often unrealistic economic assumptions in the area of the move away from fossil fuels in transport. to avoid similar failures in other areas, we must take the opportunity of the white paper review to clearly identify those issues that require our increased efforts so that european integration in the transport sector takes on real shape. first, therefore, it is necessary to emphasise the particular importance of the projects forming the trans-european transport network for the construction of a coherent transport network in the union. the ten-t project is crucial for deepening european integration in the area of transport, including for increasing the transport accessibility of the peripheral areas of the european union. the construction of the ten-t network should be the top priority of our transport policy in the years to come. secondly, the white paper in its current form does not sufficiently address the issue of public transport and urban mobility, and the commitment to modern forms of travel based on the principles of the sharing economy. i believe that a document as important and strategic as the white paper cannot ignore such important issues. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's transport policy and its implementation in the member states. it is worrying that some member states are seeking to protect their own entrepreneurs at the expense of the fundamental economic freedoms of the union, by camouflaging such practices with social issues. such actions should not take place and i am glad that the report by mr van de camp has underlined the importance of balancing the free market with the protection of workers' rights. i am confident that the european commission will listen to this voice and take these and many other comments in this report into account when updating the white paper objectives and their implementation in the years ahead.

in writing. no one can remain indifferent to the situation. every day we hear of new, dramatic attempts to reach europe. these are shocking images. the need to resolve this drama presents the european union with a particularly urgent challenge. this is confirmed by frontex data from january and february of this year. in the meantime, the number of migrants in 2014 increased significantly compared to 2013: the central mediterranean route by 42%, the eastern mediterranean route by 107%, the western balkan route by 990%. the largest group of asylum seekers in the eu in the first quarter were not syrians, accounting for 16%, but mainly people from the balkans: kosovo, albania and serbia. frontex predicts that next year this number could double to about 2.5 million people. the solidarity we should show migrants cannot be based on mutual appeals to order or blame, which undermine the effectiveness of action by building internal conflicts. this is why it is so important to develop a good strategy, including: increasing bilateral aid and aid programmes, with particular attention to transit and origin countries; stepping up action to combat trafficking and smuggling networks; effective control and protection of the european union's external borders; and stepping up cooperation with the international community, in particular the un, the african union and the league of arab states.
in writing. ‒ action is needed to further liberalise international trade, as it brings significant benefits to all parties involved. the protocol amending the marrakesh agreement is a good example of this. that's why i voted to accept it.
in writing. ‒ the protocol concerns the ratification of the trade facilitation agreement, which has been agreed by the ep's committee on international trade. studies and analyses carried out in the run-up to the wto's adoption of the agreement show that its implementation will bring more than eur 100 billion to the world economy and reduce the cost of trade by 12.5-17.5%. the adoption of the agreement could bring significant benefits not only to developing countries but also to eu member states and the union itself, leading to a multilateral trading system. i voted to accept the report.
in writing. ‒ the budapest convention was adopted by a diplomatic conference jointly organised by the central commission for the navigation of the rhine and the danube commission, in cooperation with the un economic commission for europe. it entered into force on 1 april 2005 and aims to harmonise contractual and navigational standards on inland waterways in european countries. the convention contains provisions concerning the choice of the parties' right to contract for the carriage covered by the convention. poland has expressed its interest in acceding to the budapest convention on several occasions. poland is keen to see a council decision as soon as possible, which will enable it to become bound by the budapest convention, something poland has been seeking for several years. that's why i endorsed the report.
in writing. ‒ the report deals with the asylum crisis in italy and greece and the launch of a system for relocating persons in need of and seeking international protection to other member states. the application requested the transfer of approximately 40% of all persons who entered the eu illegally to greece and italy in 2014. i don't think the forced relocation system is a good idea. a better solution would be to build trust and a lasting system based on the principle of voluntary participation by other member states. rather, such large migrations should be prevented by establishing stability in the region, cooperation with third countries, an effective return system and strong sanctions for trafficking in human beings. more frequent checks should be carried out in greece and italy and a system should be established to predict at which border the increased migration flows will occur. i therefore voted in favour of rejecting the proposal to introduce a relocation scheme.
in writing. ‒ better coordination of eu policies and instruments with the urban dimension, introduction of territorial impact assessments for new legislation and implementation of a multi-level governance model and partnership principle are elements that can facilitate greater coherence of urban policy strategies in the future. sensitizing policy decisions to urban issues, mapping the problems and challenges facing cities, and developing common solutions within the urban agenda can contribute to improving the quality of life of residents not only of metropolitan areas but also of small and medium-sized urban centres. noting the reservations about the choice of objectives and priorities, and the ability of local governments to finance the agenda's objectives, i decided to support the report.
in writing. ‒ the document adopted by the european parliament not only supports the urban agenda proposed by the commission, but also goes one step further by proposing that it should eventually become an urban policy of the union. the document also calls on the european commission to better coordinate eu policies and instruments with the urban dimension, to introduce territorial impact assessments for new legislation and to implement a multi-level governance model and the principle of partnership. if the european commission takes the proposals put forward by the european parliament into account, our cities can benefit from a completely different quality and additional support, which is why i decided to vote in favour of the document on the urban dimension of the union's policy.
in writing. ‒ managing urban areas requires the coordination of many activities and the consideration of many different infrastructural and social needs. the effective use of structural funds and the implementation of cohesion policy in urban areas is therefore impossible without the creation of an action programme that comprehensively identifies the needs of small and large agglomerations. it is therefore obvious that support is being given to the idea of an urban agenda, which will be the backbone of the eu's policy towards urbanised areas. cities are the driving force of the economy, generate the majority of european gdp, and are centres of education and science. this leading role of cities is also associated with a number of problems, such as high population density, transport difficulties, high levels of pollution emitted into the atmosphere and large disparities in the living standards of the population. the urban dimension of eu policy should take these aspects into account and take into account local and regional specificities, which can best be understood by giving a decisive voice to local authorities in the formulation of objectives. we should use all the financial instruments available, both those already in place, such as horizon 2020, and those that are being created, such as the european fund for strategic investments, to make cities as welcoming as possible, including for residents with special needs elderly or disabled people. i support the idea of creating such a comprehensive plan, which is why i voted for this report.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on investing in growth and jobs and promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion in the union. modernising and strengthening cohesion policy will further reduce disparities between regions and contribute to the union's objectives of employment and training growth. cohesion policy should focus more on the regeneration of eu industry, innovation, employment, training and support for entrepreneurship. we need new initiatives to tackle youth unemployment and new quality jobs. in this context, we should link the fight against unemployment with the digital agenda, the european structural and investment funds and horizon 2020. in addition, the role of education and training should be strengthened, with particular attention to ensuring equal access to and quality of education and promoting lifelong learning, vocational training and dual education.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is still the eu's main investment policy, also in the 2014-2020 budget. cohesion investments have undoubtedly helped to mitigate some of the effects of the crisis, providing a significant share of public investment in some member states. the main objective of this policy remains to reduce disparities between regions and to eradicate poverty in the poorest regions of the eu. in this context, and noting the objection to the ec's imposition of thematic concentration, limits and macroeconomic conditionality, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ if we want to have a competitive labour market in europe in the 21st century, we need to manage both supply and demand policies for employment. it is important that young people entering the labour market have the right qualifications and are aware of the need for continuous training or retraining. the european parliament's report focuses on increasing the competitiveness of the eu labour market, inter alia, through efficient cooperation between universities, enterprises, public and private employment services and workers, and by continuously monitoring future trends in labour markets and forecasting the demand for skills and qualifications. i have decided to vote in favour of the report because i believe that it properly highlights the problems and seeks solutions to them.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen! increasing life expectancy is one of the greatest achievements of mankind, but it is accompanied by greater social demands and the need for additional public services. the ageing of europe's population is a challenge for public budgets, but it also represents a great asset of experience and potential mentorship for the new generation. however, i would like to draw attention to a very important part of the report, namely the well-being of older people in a digital society. more and more services are available on the internet. more and more jobs are being created with the digitalisation of societies in mind. however, according to the european digital agenda scoreboard, only 20% of people over 55 have sufficient digital skills and 41% of people over 55 have never used the internet. this is related to the difficulty of accessing training and the lack of assistance in vocational retraining. these two factors should be the focus of further action if we want older people to be active participants in the labour market and not be digitally excluded. i congratulate the rapporteur on a well-written report and am pleased that the objectives of the european year of older persons and solidarity between generations for 2012 have been successfully implemented in many senior communities.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the evaluation of the 2012 european year for older persons and intergenerational solidarity, i would like to draw attention to the need to continue initiatives and programmes on active ageing and to increase their targeting at local and regional level. the need for this type of action is demonstrated by the large number of people willing to take advantage of this type of opportunity. for example, in my region, i regularly organise training for the elderly, which is very popular. in addition, action should be taken to improve intergenerational dialogue so that younger generations learn from the experiences of older generations, whose contributions and knowledge are duly recognised and exploited. in the context of demographic change and the ageing of european society, we must also ensure that we create a social and economic environment that is favourable to older people. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the purchase, hire, maintenance and repair of equipment and installations, and the purchase of equipment and installations for the construction, maintenance, repair and overhaul of buildings, including the purchase of equipment and installations for the construction of buildings, and the purchase of equipment and installations for the construction of buildings. following today's resolution, i hope that the commission will propose new initiatives to combat unemployment among people over 50 and, in cooperation with the member states, to propose solutions to make older people more attractive to employ.
in writing. ‒ 2012 was the european year of older persons and solidarity between generations. it was designed to facilitate the creation of a culture of active ageing in europe. i support the concept of active ageing (with one caveat: it must be voluntary, i.e. older people cannot be forced to continue working). that is why i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ 2012 was declared the 'european year of older people's activity and solidarity between generations' with the aim of facilitating the creation of a culture of activity among older people in europe, based on the principle of a society open to all age groups. the document voted on was intended not only to assess the european year 2012 but also to present concrete recommendations for the elimination of age discrimination, especially in relation to the labour market. i believe that in an ageing european union, it is necessary to promote a 'silver economy', one that sees older people as an opportunity rather than a threat. i therefore voted in favour of the evaluation document for the european year of older people.
in writing. ‒ mr van de camp's report reflects many of the assessments, proposals and conclusions made by the parliament's committee on transport and tourism. the white paper on transport requires substantial revision, change and adaptation to the new reality, especially as we are after difficult economic years in many member states. the financial perspective 2007-13 brought significant changes to the state of infrastructure in the new member states. however, we are still a long way from the vision of a single european transport area and a coherent infrastructure. the ten-t has not yet been developed satisfactorily, which would imply interoperability, the development of intelligent transport systems, safety on roads, railways and in the air. increasing transport efficiency, infrastructure charges, the role of public, mass transit are other important areas where we are making changes. drones and their rules of operation are a new technology, and i welcome the proposal to regulate them. the cef is an important new financial instrument which, when combined with the juncker plan, creates new opportunities; a prudent implementation policy by the commission is needed. in view of the above, i support this report, although i still have reservations about the european commission's conduct with regard to the german minimum wage law for car and bus drivers.
in writing. ‒ emphasising the need to eliminate disparities in the level of infrastructure development and maintenance, in particular between the eastern and western parts of the european union, and to develop a european transport policy and a free market in transport services, i supported the white paper review report. however, the report also addresses several issues, such as decarbonisation, a costly commitment to reduce emissions, reducing transport's dependence on fossil fuels, the creation of a european road transport agency, which directly threaten the polish economy and which i voted against.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's white paper on the implementation of the transport white paper outlines an ambitious strategy for future action to promote a competitive transport system, aimed at increasing mobility, removing existing barriers and reducing pollution from this sector of the economy. despite the very good intentions of the document, many of the demands contain difficult targets, such as a 60% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from transport by 2030, or a doubling of the use of public transport in urban areas by 2030, or even harmful demands that are completely detached from the realities of doing business, such as the introduction of a weekly rest for people employed in the transport sector. the european union should create a law that is not over-regulated and that is rational in its approach to the challenges of the present day, which is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i would like to point out that in 2011 the european commission set transport targets up to 2050. the objectives are clear: increase transport mobility, eliminate transport barriers, reduce carbon emissions. the problem is that in practice, the disparities between modes of transport have been increasing in europe over the last few years. the scale of road and air transport is increasing, which increases congestion and degrades the environment. this trend should be mitigated by allocating relatively more resources and energy to the potential of rail, short sea shipping and inland waterways. only then can we talk about more sustainable development, greater mobility and better protection of natural resources.
in writing. ‒ the 2011 white paper on transport is a necessary and important document. no major work can be done without a plan, and a task as complex and time-consuming as the construction of a tightly integrated european transport network requires a specific plan. it is clear that such a document needs to be updated frequently and the objectives formulated modified and adjusted as work progresses, so that the strategy does not function only on paper. in the white paper of four years ago, many objectives were formulated in too abstract a way, as is clearly shown at the stage of the present review. the assumptions made in 2011 to move away from fossil fuels have not only not been met, but their consumption has also increased slightly. there is no better proof that climate policy cannot be constructed in isolation from economic realities and consumer preferences. the white paper also needs to be revised in other areas. modern and electrified urban transport, the needs of pedestrians and cyclists in building transport infrastructure, the particular importance of the ten-t network in the context of the creation of the efsi, the protection of the free market and entrepreneurs in the road transport sector, unfair competition from asian airlines and the sharing economy - these issues need to be better highlighted in the white paper and are addressed in the tran report. i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ women represent more than 60% of graduates in the european union and almost half of doctoral students. however, the higher up the university hierarchy, the lower the presence of women - for example, only about 20% of women are senior academics, and their share in university board positions is similar. women in academia are disproportionately more likely to encounter barriers in the form of stereotypes and prejudices about their academic potential, which together create a glass ceiling blocking access to the highest positions. despite their high competence at the start of their careers, women are much more likely to drop out of the later stages of their careers, also because of the disproportionately higher burden of caring responsibilities than men. i voted in favour of the 'report on women working in science and universities and the glass ceiling problem' because it recognises the barriers to women pursuing scientific careers and the need for institutional and cultural change to overcome them. only breaking the glass ceiling will guarantee women the right to realise their potential on the basis of equal opportunities and the full use of women's talents and competences in science and innovation.
in writing. ‒ while one can agree with the report's general recommendations to encourage greater involvement of women in science, the report nevertheless refers to the istanbul convention and recognises the harmful role of stereotypes about traditional family roles. that is why i did not support the report in its entirety and abstained.
in writing. ‒ given that gender equality is a fundamental principle of the european union, all efforts should be made to combat existing discrimination against women in science. the european parliament document points out that women are still under-represented in most science, engineering and management positions, which, in addition to the social and moral dimension, has economic significance, as science is of fundamental importance to europe and requires more and more teams capable of, among other things, conducting ground-breaking research essential to enhancing the eu's productivity and competitiveness. the ep document, in addition to outlining the problems, sets out actions that member states and the european commission should take to change the current situation, such as incentives for research centres, removing cultural barriers or establishing a european parliament prize for 'women in european science'. i therefore voted in favour of the report on women in science and universities. however, i would like to stress that i believe that in order to achieve equality between women and men, action must be taken in a variety of fields and sectors of their activity, and not just in one, namely science.
in writing. ‒ the report goes far beyond the remit of the femm committee. the title of the report indicates that it concerns education, an area in which the european parliament does not have the necessary powers; moreover, the report recommends changes to the curricula in the member states. the report also called on the commission to initiate the process of eu accession to the istanbul convention. member states were also invited to take such action. for these reasons i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ empowering girls and other equality activities are of great importance to the european union as an organisation based on non-discrimination of people on grounds of gender, age, ethnicity or nationality. however, despite its very legitimate aims, the document contains many proposals which are impossible to implement and which significantly interfere with the exclusive competence of the member states, including in the field of education. too often, though, solutions that are presented in the name of noble goals but are pursued in an unwise way are counterproductive. so one-sided statements and goals and arguments must be avoided. for these reasons too, i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ european countries such as switzerland, norway, iceland, liechtenstein, monaco, san marino, andorra are very important partners of the european union, which is why it is so important to continuously monitor their mutual relations and to eliminate existing problems. relations between the union and the aforementioned countries go beyond economic integration and the expansion of the single market, they also contribute to increasing stability and prosperity for the benefit of all citizens and businesses. the report prepared by parliament indicates that there are still problems in relations between the partners, particularly with regard to the transposition of eu legislation, but also with regard to internal national policies on migration or transport which are incompatible with eu policy. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the ep report because it adequately outlines the problems that exist and points to the action that the commission should take to remedy these problems.
in writing. ‒ the challenges facing the union have never been so serious and urgent as they are today. the greek and migration crises, the fight against terrorism and the security of europe need an immediate and comprehensive remedy. since the beginning of the year, almost half a million people have crossed into the eu. despite the increase in frontex's budget in 2015 by an additional eur 13,7 million, it has become clear that the union is not able to cope with migrants and is not able to effectively protect its borders or to resolve in solidarity the problem of hundreds of thousands of migrants clustered in refugee camps on its territory. the new ec proposals for managing migration flows and their relocation, backed by a single asylum policy for all member states, supported by the principle of safe countries and legal migration routes to the eu, deserve support. it is also reasonable to allow refugees to apply for asylum from outside the european union. we have repeatedly said in parliament's resolutions that the eu must fulfil its role as a promoter of peace and democracy, but the european community as an economic organisation has limited economic tools at its disposal. without a real eu foreign policy based on the community method, the mediterranean refugee exodus cannot be counteracted, nor can the conflicts that cause it be resolved.
in writing. ‒ supporting refugees is both a legal and a moral obligation for eu countries. but the problem of migration cannot be solved by reacting to its effects alone; the causes must also be addressed. so in addition to supporting actual refugees, we also need to be able to identify non-refugees from the incoming groups. economic migrants are not entitled to the same support as refugees. the union and the member states should establish an effective system for returning such persons to their countries of origin. nevertheless, radical action should be taken against the exploitation of human tragedy by organised crime groups. however, all action will only have a positive effect if there is greater security in the countries from which citizens flee to europe. the union should therefore verify the effectiveness of existing forms of aid to developing countries. unfortunately, parliament's resolution did not address these challenges. it also proposed an automatic mechanism for allocating refugees to individual member states, which was unacceptable to many countries. it should be borne in mind that each country in the union has different levels of economic development and economic and infrastructural capacity, and should therefore have the right to determine the number of refugees it is able to assist. for these reasons, i abstained from voting on this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the european commission, as guardian of the treaties, should be the guarantor of the application of community law. to achieve this in practice, it is necessary to further improve the transposition of the law in the member states and to ensure that it is properly respected. in 2013, the court of justice delivered 52 judgments under article 258 tfeu, 31 of which were unfavourable to the member states. as in previous years, the most frequent failures related to environmental protection, health and consumer protection, the internal market, services and transport. the complaints in the field of justice mainly concerned freedom of movement, which is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the union enshrined in the treaty. it should be borne in mind that delays and irregularities in transposition and the incorrect application of eu law lead to inconsistencies between member states, which consequently have a negative impact on citizens. the report also highlights the need for greater coordination between the commission and the member states at earlier stages of the legislative process. in addition, the european parliament could help to review the application of union legislation by using its powers of scrutiny vis-à-vis the commission in situations where ex post evaluation proves insufficient.
in writing. ‒ full implementation of european union law by the member states is one of the conditions for deepening integration and for leveling the playing field for living and doing business in the individual member states. unfortunately, not all countries implement to the same extent and to the same extent, and what is worse, many add their own additional regulations to the already over-regulated eu law. in my view, the time has come to review the system of european union law-making, its scope of application to citizens and other legal entities, including the limitation of the impact of union legislation on the freedom to conduct a business and the freedom to decide on one's own affairs by individual citizens of the community countries. because the more freedom, the more social, civic and business entrepreneurship that drives growth.

beginning, it is a very important debate. i notice that we all agree that we are confronted with a multifaceted crisis. yes, it is a crisis of refugees and migration, but it is also a crisis that has to do with the european union and its institutions in general. it is a crisis that tests the values of the union, the credibility of europe and the validity of the principle of solidarity, but also the capacity of our institutions to react and act. i can assure you that in the commission we are fully conscious of our duty and, from the very beginning of the life of this commission, we have welcomed that. in a period of only seven months we delivered by presenting the european agenda on migration with the contribution and the approval of this house. let me also say that it is not about finger pointing. it is about finding a consensus. it is about keeping europe united. it is true that it sometimes takes more effort, but our role, the role of the commission and of the presidency – as mr asselborn said – is to discuss, to explain and to overcome differences. many of you made special reference to schengen. i want to tell you that the temporary reintroduction of border controls is explicitly foreseen in the legislation for exceptional situations and as a temporary measure. the commission is closely following developments and is also informing parliament at every stage. it is guarding borders with violent means is not compatible with european values and principles. we are here to preserve and guarantee freedom of movement in europe, but we also need to secure our external european borders. this is why the commission’s comprehensive approach needs to be adopted and swiftly implemented. yes, i expressed my frustration at the outcome of the recent council but, with your support and the excellent work done by the luxembourg presidency, we will all go this extra mile united. we are determined – as frans timmermans said – to build bridges and to prove that europe is up to the challenge, that europe is credible, and that europe is determined to stay united, resolved, solid and humane.
in writing. the wave of migrants entering europe from conflict- and poverty-stricken regions of africa and the middle east is a real and serious challenge for eu member states. within its treaty capacity, the eu should mobilise emergency funding to support countries such as italy, greece and hungary, which have been hit by the first wave of migrants. we have to realize that the migration from conflict zones has been going on for years. countries in my region have already taken in hundreds of thousands of immigrants from ukraine and other countries in eastern europe and the caucasus, including culturally diverse chechens, ingush and tatars who arrived after successive russian invasions. we will continue to show that solidarity. but i cannot imagine pressure being put on my country by representatives of other eu member states. the forced relocation mechanism is a non-treaty, unacceptable and counter-productive solution. even if it's mitigated, the voluntary after all the speeches and pressure, i'd consider it a complete fiction. the eu's borders must be strengthened and the member states that guard them must be supported.
in writing. i am deeply saddened by the current situation where borders are being closed out of necessity and european society is being ensnared by populist xenophobia. europe must now prove that the union's values of shared responsibility and solidarity are not empty words. member states must act now and they must do so together. relocation and respect for the individual right to asylum, and above all support for countries that need financial and organisational support, are expectations that should be discussed in the first place. the eu has also been active in the field of asylum, with a particular focus on the protection of refugees and migrants. the external borders of the european union must also be remembered and must be strengthened and protected together. the european union has given its citizens the freedom to travel across its territory without passport controls, but this 'common home' of ours must be protected from the outside, no matter who wants to enter it. it is therefore necessary to focus on the activities of frontex in this area. i hope that the extraordinary council meeting on 22 september will lead to a common solution. it is necessary to discuss the reform of the dublin regulation and of the european asylum law. in short, we need a truly integrated european migration policy that is binding on the member states and that will give us a social credit for our actions.

madam president! the 17 sustainable development goals, which form an ambitious follow-up to the millennium development goals, will be formally endorsed at the new york summit. some of these goals have been achieved: deaths from malaria and hiv have decreased, and about 80 percent of children in africa are now receiving an education. however, the new goals are intended to provide an even stronger incentive to tackle extreme poverty, eliminate social inequalities and act to reduce negative climate change. 2015 is also the european year for development and the european union has repeatedly reiterated its commitment to supporting development and ensuring that it is adequately financed. the fact that the union and its member states, as the world's largest donors of development aid, set the standard in this area is all the more gratifying. i would also like to highlight the important role of innovative sources of financing for development in the form of microfinance, non-traditional taxes and public-private partnerships, which effectively contribute to the achievement of the post-2015 sustainable development goals. the current humanitarian crisis and the difficult international situation further demonstrate that development aid is one of the key tools and the response to the challenges of the european union's long-term strategy to overcome the global development gap. in his last speech to the united nations in september 1963, kennedy, in describing the work of peace, quoted archimedes, who said, "give me a foothold, and i will lift the earth". half a century after the then president of the united states spoke those words, our generation has a chance to decide the shape of the world to come. we must therefore ensure that the new development agenda agreed by global leaders is reflected in eu regulations and implemented in the form of common european policies.

in writing. i dedicate these words to the participants of cop 21 in paris. climate change is leading to extreme events - flash floods and catastrophic droughts. the large amounts of money currently spent on reducing greenhouse gas emissions are not enough to reverse these trends. the issue of emissions has dominated the climate debate, while the issue of adaptation to climate change has become a burning issue, and it has been pushed back. if it is true that greenhouse gas emissions have led to adverse climate change (a claim that has not been proven by the ipcc), then the forthcoming conference should consider not only the problem of reducing them but also ways to increase the absorption capacity of our globe. the recent drought in europe, followed by floods, is a clear warning sign. this indicates the need to reassess the eu's climate policy, which should focus more on adaptation, including afforestation, to mitigate climate change and on which, rather than just reducing co2, the main financial resources should be directed. in the case of poland, this means a return to the ambitious concepts known as the unrealized "wisła program". the main aims of the programme were to reduce the steppe-like character of large areas of poland, to provide drinking water for future generations of poles and to protect the country from flooding.

in writing. cohesion policy is europe's main investment policy. as the sixth cohesion report showed, it also played its role well in times of crisis, helping national and local authorities to mitigate the effects of the economic downturn. cohesion policy is also, by definition, a solidarity policy. it's designed to help those areas that are doing worse than the others. for these reasons, i support the proposal to amend the regulation to grant special measures to greece. i believe that the solutions proposed will ensure that, in the exceptional situation in which greece finds itself, cohesion policy can continue to play its investment and growth-promoting role there. the new rules will allow greeks to complete existing projects and start new ones. at the same time, care should be taken to ensure that the proposed solutions do not have negative budgetary consequences for other countries. therefore, this change must be unique and one-off.
madam president! i would like to thank eleni theocharous for her work on this report, which highlights the importance of local authorities for development. local government is closest to its communities. like no one else knows their needs. we also see this in our work in the regions of the member states of the european union. building this awareness in developing countries is crucial not only for central and local governments, but also for citizens. the centres of power should support the process of decentralisation and transfer good governance models, competences and financial resources so that they can be used most effectively at local level. local authorities, on the other hand, must be open to dialogue with citizens as well as to cooperation with civil society organisations, other administrative bodies and private partners. these partnerships have a real impact on social inclusion by promoting education, strengthening micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, creating jobs and supporting sustainable economic growth in the region. i would also like to stress the key role of local authorities in crisis situations. the fair distribution of humanitarian aid, which must reach the most vulnerable groups first, is not possible without good governance and dialogue with partners and aid organisations. in view of all the above, it is appropriate that local governments are even better represented in the international negotiations for the adoption of the post-2015 development agenda.
madam president, a locally driven approach and greater civic participation are the keys to achieving more effective poverty reduction and equitable development. in implementing the post-2015 development agenda, the fact that the local dimension is of utmost importance must be further acknowledged. the engagement of local authorities in dialogue must be considered essential. in the resource-allocation process they reflect the closest possible connection between development aid and its intended beneficiaries. they are the first to respond to the changing needs of local society, and they provide basic services in terms of access to education, health and sanitation. by reinforcing decentralised public aid and fostering partnership with the private sector, we can improve social cohesion and inclusive economic growth. nevertheless, cooperation with local authorities must be monitored and controlled by good governance so that the results are lasting and do not dissolve when incentives are withdrawn.

in writing. the european union is committed to supporting local authorities in developing countries, as this leads to poverty reduction and the democratisation of local government. the weight of these efforts is shown by the fact that the world's population is projected to increase from about 7 billion to 9.5 billion by 2050. the bulk of this growth will be in developing countries, particularly in their urban areas. while i agree with the eu's support for local communities, i want to highlight an important issue. the european union's assistance cannot be unconditional. among the various conditions set by the eu, the fight against corruption must also be included. countries that are not making progress in the fight against corruption should not receive eu financial support. eu funds should be used to improve sanitation, access to education and transport. there is no justification for eu funds to be appropriated by local leaders.

in writing. ‒ a new protocol to the ilo convention on forced and compulsory labour was adopted in geneva in june 2014. the protocol addresses the gaps in the implementation of the provisions of the convention on forced and compulsory labour and aims to make progress in the prevention of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of forced labour, as well as in the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. the convention is an important step in the fight against modern slavery. although 80 years have passed since the original convention was widely ratified, at least 20.9 million people worldwide are victims of forced labor. therefore, cross-border cooperation in the prosecution of perpetrators of these crimes is a key element in ensuring that modern slavery is punished and brought to an end. member states cannot decide to ratify the protocol outside the eu institutions, as some parts of the protocol fall within the eu's competence. the council therefore adopted a draft decision authorising the member states to ratify those parts of the protocol which fall within the eu's competence. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ a 21st century society should not and cannot tolerate forced labour in any circumstances and in any form on the free market. the 2014 ilo protocol addresses the fundamental rights of victims and the fight against trafficking in human beings, a crime that has a degrading impact not only on individuals but also on society as a whole and on the economy as a whole. i therefore voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation on the convention on forced or compulsory labour and i believe that ratification of this protocol is an important step both in ensuring that the rights of victims are respected and in combating trafficking in human beings.
in writing. – i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the protocol of 2014 on the forced labour convention of the international labour organization with regard to matters related to judicial cooperation in criminal matters. my position in that matter can simply be explained by the following. during the last plenary session i voted in favour on the same protocol – on the issues concerning the social policy. at that time, i stated that preventing the trafficking of labour exploitation and compensating the victims of forced labour should be of high importance to us. i still believe this is a very important aspect. the aspect we, as the european union, should focus our attention on. according to statistics millions of people are forced to work – not only in undeveloped countries, but even in the developed ones! however, in order to stop this problem, or at least minimise it, we have to support the parts of the protocol that fall into competences of the eu such as the articles related to social policies as well as judicial cooperation.
in writing. ‒ smoking, as a common term for a wide range of products containing psychoactive substances, contributes to the health and lives of thousands of europeans every year. the fight against them is particularly difficult, not only because of the problem of detection of psychoactive substances in the body, but above all because of the fact that manufacturers of stimulants constantly change their chemical composition, which avoids the existing prohibitions on their production and sale. the extension of the list of substances subject to control measures is therefore a good step, but in the long term, the continuous addition of further additives with only a slight difference in composition from those previously prohibited is ineffective. therefore, another way of excluding harmful substances should be considered, i.e. not on the basis of a specific name or a specific chemical composition that is very easy to modify, but on the basis of the effects of taking harmful substances. otherwise, we'll always be one step behind the manufacturers and distributors of the doping.
in writing. ‒ the eu solidarity fund (eusf) was established in 2002 to provide financial assistance to eligible countries affected by large-scale natural disasters or exceptional regional disasters. the commission proposes to mobilise the eusf to provide financial assistance following the severe winter in bulgaria, which resulted in a disaster classified as a 'serious natural disaster', and two floods in greece classified under the eusf criteria as 'regional disasters'. i supported both proposals as both cases meet the requirements of the eusf and have a strong impact on local communities and economies. my group supports the principle and the objectives of the eusf and that is why i supported the resolution on the mobilisation of the fund.
in writing. ‒ the creation of eu protection in the form of geographical indications for non-manufactured products seems to be a necessity, given that the craft sector is also a driver of economic growth in the union. as an integral part of our identity, they are an important part of the cultural heritage of each member state and a guarantee of the quality of traditional products. the extension of the protection of geographical indications will also have a positive impact on both producers and consumers, increasing their confidence in products by including information on their quality, origin and production methods and conditions. the introduction of such legislation can stimulate innovation in traditional production processes and help to safeguard jobs in underdeveloped areas by providing small and micro enterprises with opportunities to increase sales through a more effective marketing strategy. moreover, the introduction of geographical indications will contribute to combating the counterfeit product market and the illegal use of geographical indications and other unlawful practices that mislead consumers and are harmful to traders.
in writing. ‒ the legal affairs committee of the european parliament has decided that we should introduce legislation to regulate the use of geographical indications on non-herbal products. under such a system, consumers would have access to information on the origin of a product, which would allow them to easily identify it and make a more informed purchase decision. the linking of the purchased product to a specific region would facilitate the assessment of its quality, production standards and the origin of its ingredients or components. moreover, the promotion of local products leads directly to the flourishing of the local economy, the preservation of traditional production methods, the protection of culture and the development of tourism. the instruments governing copyright issues, protecting the market against counterfeiting, must also be provided for. if we create the right legal framework for such a system, we indirectly support the development of entire regions where such goods are produced, and let us not forget that very often these are rural areas. by supporting local production, not just agriculture, we also support the local community.
in writing. ‒ the globalisation of the world's economies is significantly increasing the mobility of business, the production of goods and the provision of services. this is a positive process and it is difficult to imagine any limitations, for example, to the protection of the geographical origin of certain products or services. on the other hand, there are undoubtedly sectors and industries which, because of their regional or local characteristics, should be protected in terms of their origin or specific production methods. this catalogue of industries or fields includes the production of foodstuffs, but also crafts, handicrafts and local artistic creativity. these forms of economic activity should be subject to specific legal protection, not only to respect the rights of those communities that have been engaged in such production for decades, and often for centuries, but also to protect a particular tradition and culture for posterity. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the european parliament's report on the extension of the protection of geographical indications of the european union to non-perishable products.
in writing. ‒ proper indication of the origin of regional products is important for both producers and consumers. manufacturers are guaranteed that their product is protected against unauthorised copying by means of a certification system and compliance with specific requirements concerning the materials used or the manufacturing methods used. consumers, on the other hand, are given a tool to make informed purchases in line with their preferences and expectations. the establishment of such an effective labelling system at european level has been successful in the area of marketing agricultural products and has contributed to increasing consumer awareness. agricultural products from poland have also become more recognisable and, thanks to their high quality, have been permanently established on the markets of other member states. we can achieve similar success in the area of non-sexual products, which is why i voted in favour of this report. such a system will not only guarantee the protection of traditional production methods, but will also allow the creation of jobs in regions where local crafts are an important part of the cultural and economic heritage. however, a green light for the creation of a european labelling system does not mean an unconditional approval of possible shortcomings of this system. the creation of eu standards for the labelling of non-perishable regional products must of course involve a sound information campaign for consumers and must not create an administrative barrier for producers wishing to register their products in such a database.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed to release the last 5% of payments to greece from the eu budget until the closure of the programmes, to increase the maximum co-financing level to 100% and to make available additional initial advances for 2015 and 2016. i supported the commission's proposal on the condition that this action is exceptional, one-off and the change is budget neutral for the period 2014-2020; it does not entail any changes to the annual ceilings of the multiannual financial framework for commitment and payment appropriations. in addition, the annual breakdown of commitment appropriations for the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund remains unchanged.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr theocharous. most of my professional life has been spent in regional development and local government, which is why i believe so strongly in their extraordinary potential to identify the real needs of the region and its people and thus contribute to its faster development. i am therefore convinced that, wherever possible, cooperation with developing countries should be based on cooperation with local government, and i support the suggestion in mrs theocharous' report that the commission should consider making decentralisation the main area of eu external financing. i also believe that fighting poverty and improving living standards in developing countries, also with the support of local and regional authorities, is one of the important ways of preventing the migration crisis at its source, which is why i am in favour of increasing funding for this purpose in the 2016 budget.
in writing. ‒ the report on the role of local authorities in developing countries in development cooperation stresses the importance of involving local authorities and national parliaments in the planning and implementation of development strategies, with an emphasis on decentralisation of public aid. the mdgs have been overlooked by local authorities in the implementation strategy, and therefore the sdgs should pay particular attention to strengthening the capacity of local authorities in urban taxation and budget planning so that national resources can be effectively mobilised at local level. as a member of the acp-eu parliamentary assembly and of the committee on regional development, i understand the concerns of my colleagues from developing countries and also highlight the role of local authorities in strengthening local micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, creating new jobs and promoting sustainable and inclusive economic growth.
in writing. ‒ democracy is decentralisation. it is difficult to imagine the development of democracy in developing countries without strengthening local authority, especially in those countries that have previously had authoritarian or even totalitarian systems. in all these countries, in addition to supporting constitutional solutions for democracy building, efforts should be encouraged to develop civil society and its representation at the lowest level, local government. it plays a vital role in reducing various types of exclusion and in resolving social tensions. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the report on the role of local authorities in developing countries in development cooperation.
in writing. ‒ development as a social and economic phenomenon always has a distinct local context, and success in breaking down inequalities and raising living standards in developing countries is not possible without the involvement of local authorities. from identifying the most pressing problems to distributing finance and development aid, the involvement of local authorities must be adequately considered and supported. particularly in multi-ethnic and tribal communities, where large cultural differences are often not sufficiently addressed at the central level, local government is the best partner in planning and spending development aid. however, strengthening the role of local authorities in development cooperation should also include the creation of tools to support democratic and effective governance, which often struggles with a number of pathologies at this level: corruption, abuse of power or discrimination against ethnic and cultural minorities. close cooperation between international institutions, local governments and civil society organisations is essential to achieve development goals, to combat extreme poverty and to raise living standards in developing countries. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the eu has an important role to play in this process. the role it can play is, among other things, through greater involvement of local and regional authorities in this process.

mr. chairman, please! we have this debate every year. what's the reason? because we believe that every human being has the right to live. this law is a basic human right. it's a matter of human dignity, it's a matter of natural law. european civilization has gone through this period of capital punishment here, although there are still countries in europe that still use capital punishment there. but i also come from a country where we once -- over 25 years ago -- had a moratorium on capital punishment and then we abolished it. the question is always, do we have the instruments to abolish the death penalty in all countries? it's a process, of course. it's never an easy process, there are always strong arguments from the parties we talk to that they don't want to abolish the death penalty: because it's terrorism, because it's tradition, because it's a deterrent to crime. but it seems that words have power, too. we have many resolutions that have been passed here, that have decided that people sentenced to death for political reasons, for example, have been exempted from that punishment, that they are alive. and this is also part of our policy, which we are pursuing in the european parliament, among other places.
mr. chairman, please! human life is the highest value, except that i think it should be taken into account that we are dealing with different situations where the death penalty is imposed. in all cases, we are against it. but as was rightly pointed out in the debate, in the case of murder, in the case of the most serious crimes, international law allows for this, even though we are trying to get states to step back from this ancient, ancient right. now we have another situation where the death penalty is imposed for such crimes as adultery, political crimes, conversion, drug trafficking. these acts, even these death sentences, even dressed up as court judgments, are judicial crimes. we should have no doubt that the very people who are requesting these sentences, who are passing them, who are executing them, are criminals in the robes of a judge. after world war ii, nazi german prosecutors, judges, and judges were put on trial. i think that such judges who are sentencing people to death for adultery, political crimes, conversion, drug trafficking should be identified and at least blacklisted, unless they are judging in possible situations on the basis of universal jurisdiction.
president of the council. mr president, i could simply conclude what has just been said, namely that the death penalty has no place in the twenty-first century. i thank you for your very broad and very determined commitment against the death penalty. this commitment is also a very clear message to be given to those countries which have not yet arrived, in fact, in the 21st century, as you have said. there is no easy solution. clearly, persuasion is needed at every opportunity. we must talk about it, we must also mobilize our civil society, our non-governmental organizations to effectively attack this practice from another time. international public opinion can play an important role, and i am thinking in particular of all that has been done at the united nations. of course, it is a long process because thousands of people are being executed in the meantime, but i think this debate shows that europe is true to its values in this respect. these values must be made known to those countries which do not share them. we do this by including the principle of human rights in the various agreements we conclude with our partners. but we also have to be realistic. we cannot now block or punish, by refusing any agreement with countries that practice the death penalty, because that would not change them. it will be through dialogue, but also through very clear signals that we will change them. i remain optimistic that one day they too will arrive in the 21st century.
