the next item is the report by ms lidia joanna geringer de oedenberg, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 861/2007 of the european parliament and of the council of 11 july 2007 establishing a european small claims procedure and regulation (ec) no 1896/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 12 december 2006 establishing a european order for payment procedure (com201(0793) 4 c7-0414/2013 2013/0403 ((cod)) (a8-0140/2015).
the rapporteur. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. with the growth of cross-border trade in the european union, the need to provide effective and rapid redress mechanisms for both retail customers and small and medium-sized enterprises has become increasingly urgent as a means of supporting their business activities. the proposed amendment to the european small claims procedure raises the amount of claims from eur 2000 to eur 5000 and aims primarily at simplifying the procedures for settling cross-border disputes in civil and commercial matters, reducing the average duration of court proceedings from more than 2 years to 5 months and reducing costs by 40%. the increase in the amount threshold in disputes will further significantly expand the potential range of individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises that can benefit from this new simplified way of pursuing their claims. as the chief negotiator for the legal affairs committee of the european parliament, i am pleased that after a year and a half of debates with the council, the latvian presidency has finally managed to negotiate a solution which will now be put to the vote of the european parliament during the fourth luxembourg presidency since the start of work on the document. i am convinced that the new procedure for cross-border claims will help citizens to enforce their rights efficiently, quickly and cheaply. the case is really about billions of euros across the european union, which are small amounts that have not been recovered until now because the costs of litigation and legal services have often exceeded them. the result was a boom in companies that cheated their customers with notorious impunity. the new simplified procedure also provides for the administrative handling of cases without the need to retain a lawyer and without the need to travel to another country, since any hearings will take place, for example, by videoconference, teleconference or other means of distance communication; it allows for the payment of court fees by bank transfer or card (instead of at the court window as was often the case); it does not require the translation of all documents into another language the originals will now suffice, and only a brief description of the case will have to be translated. the costs of a cross-border inquiry will not be higher than the costs of litigation in a similar case in one's own country and will not be disproportionate to the amount of the claim. the original proposal, which i negotiated with the council, was to include certain aspects of labour law in the procedure, which would seem natural in an era of widespread mobility of workers in the european union. unfortunately, the resistance in the council was insurmountable, but the compromise reached includes a revision clause, both on the possibility of raising the threshold for the amount of claims and on the further extension of the procedure to include matters relating to remuneration. i think that with the implementation of this new simplified procedure (which will take place at the latest 16 months after the entry into force of the regulation), the judicial approach in cross-border disputes will finally be profitable and with it, i hope, the end of massive and impunity fraud on customers. finally, i would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs, the juri secretariat, the council and commission representatives, my advisers and assistants for their excellent cooperation. the compromise was reached thanks in particular to the contributions of the co-rapporteur, mr daniel boudin, the european commission's mr michael shotter and mr jacek garstka, the latvian presidency's minister for justice, mr dzintars rasnačs, and mr ilze lepiksone, mr vita sliede and ms barbara mekel. i also want to thank alexander keys, linda moldovan and annie czerwoniec for their great commitment to my parliamentary work.
madam president! i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and all those involved in the negotiations on the good outcome of the work on the reform of the small claims procedure. the changes will have two important effects. firstly, the procedure will become more widespread and familiar, and secondly, it will become more attractive to citizens and small businesses in the european union. the most important solutions are, first, raising the claim ceiling to eur 5000 and, second, obliging the courts to use modern communication technologies. these changes will therefore increase the attractiveness of the solution, while reducing the costs of its application also for the parties to the proceedings. this will therefore reduce, inter alia, travel and attendance costs for the parties. this has the potential to make the instrument more accessible and more readily available in europe. it should therefore become a tool that will positively contribute to closing the legal gap gap in access to justice in cross-border cases. at present, many businesses and citizens do not benefit from exercising their rights, mainly because of the costs that are too high in relation to the value of the claim. the most important thing right now is to promote this procedure. we're creating a very interesting instrument that, unfortunately, very few people know about. it can also increase the willingness of small businesses to do business in other countries. a change can remove the fear of having to sue for your rights, even if the amount in question is relatively small. for these reasons, this solution should be promoted also through the european commission and the member states.
member of the commission.– madam president, the compromise parliament has reached with the council will bring new advantages to citizens and businesses. they will be able to use the european small claims procedure more often and at a lower cost. also, the length of the procedure will be reduced. i would like to thank the honourable members again for their cooperation: after today’s discussion i am more confident that you will vote in favour of the agreed compromise.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - i have to go. i just wanted to thank you for your kind words about the quality of my work and our cooperation. i'm glad we're putting a useful tool for the public to claim. it is designed to work by principle: cheaply, quickly and simply. the so-called small claims procedure has been ineffective. first, the citizens were largely unaware of it, and they found it too complicated and expensive, and they often waved their hands, paying money as a lesson in their own naivety or stupidity. and with this tool, we're going to stop this behavior that's been rampant, especially on the internet. i ask you to give your strong support to this initiative, which has been unanimously approved by the legal affairs committee. i'd like to see a similar result in tomorrow's vote.
in writing. by raising the claim ceiling to eur 5000 and obliging courts to use modern communication technologies that reduce the costs of travel and attendance for the parties, the small claims procedure has the potential to become more accessible and more readily used. in the longer term, it should become a tool that will have a positive impact on closing the gap in access to justice in cross-border cases. many businesses and citizens simply cannot afford to enforce their rights nowadays, mainly because the costs of cross-border litigation are too high to be claimed. the most important thing now is to promote the procedure. we have a good instrument that unfortunately not many people know about, both on the part of legal practitioners and citizens. the existence of such a simplified small claims court procedure may, above all, change the approach of many small entrepreneurs to developing their business outside the country. i would therefore like to ask both the commission and the member states to actively promote this procedure, as it is a perfect example of the benefits and added value of civil and commercial law cooperation in the european union. it's worth it for the public to see and feel the benefits.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - i have to go. the directive we are voting on tomorrow sets limits on dust emissions sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides and introduces carbon monoxide monitoring without setting limits for combustion plants with a capacity of 150mw or more. in short, this directive is part of the air safety package. it also fills the legislative gap that we have between the ecodesign directive, which sets standards for combustion plants of less than 1mw, and the industrial emissions directive, which covers plants of more than 50mw. the emission limits are set at an ambitious level that ensures a gradual improvement in air quality, but also the protection of existing combustion plants and investments. this protection has primarily been extended to small installations of up to 5 mw, which are operated primarily by small and medium-sized enterprises or municipal corporations, or are an important part of the equipment of, inter alia, schools, hospitals, universities, and those which have already been upgraded or built to a high standard, but which would require significant additional efforts to meet the standards imposed by the new directive, such as those using biomass this is particularly the case in the nordic countries. heating plants that supply heat to dwellings in housing estates and thus allow the maintenance of their operating costs and thus the non-increasing of the costs of heat supply to final customers are given special protection. and this is important not just for social reasons, but also for environmental reasons, which i want to emphasize. it allows the promotion of policies to replace individual heating sources, in particular in single-family houses, with collective heating, which is particularly important for certain regions in central and eastern europe and can significantly improve air quality. i wanted to emphasise that the final text of the directive is an example of a good reconciliation of the challenges that arise from the need to protect the environment, economic reality and social needs. we have set ambitious targets, but they are achievable without imposing excessive costs on both operators and end-users. on 23 june, an agreement was reached in an informal trilogue between parliament, the council and the european commission. this agreement was also accepted by coreper on 30 june with only one country voting against and voted in the environmental protection committee on 15 july by a large majority of 59 votes in favour to 6 against. i admit, however, that the negotiations with the council were very complex and that all the provisions of the directive were subject to detailed arrangements, one after the other. this agreement should be seen as a package and changing any of its elements would require a new approach to reading this project. i wanted to thank everyone for their support, especially the whole negotiating team of the european parliament, all the counter-rapporteurs. i also thank the latvian presidency and the european commission for their cooperation, which has led to many very good solutions that satisfy all parties.

in writing. ‒ this request relates to small claims procedures up to eur 5000 in civil and commercial matters of a cross-border nature. it aims to ensure effective and rapid redress for consumers and smes in cross-border situations, i.e. where at least one of the parties is resident in a member state other than the member state in which it is established. in the past, it has often been unprofitable to pursue claims up to eur 5000 because of the excessively high costs involved. this created opportunities for frequent fraud that went unpunished. the proposed simplified procedure reduces the burden of taking evidence, allows for the hearing of parties by videoconference or teleconference, and includes methods of court fees, procedures for access to judgments and assistance to parties. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the average size of combustion plants includes residential heating and cooling units for electricity generation, or industrial applications, and according to the european commission there are close to 150 000 in europe. the 2009 and 2010 directives of the european parliament and of the council set emission limits for certain pollutants from small (up to 1 mw rated capacity) and large (above 50 mw rated capacity) installations. the document we adopted today complements the rules by regulating emissions from medium-sized plants (between 1 and 50 mw). in order to improve air quality, the limits set limit pollution by nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide and dust and this is a community regulation because only this form of unification of the rules has a chance of success. after all, many air pollutants emitted in one part of the eu can reach another country or region. it was therefore necessary to supplement the legislation with the current provisions. the delay in the introduction of restrictions for newly established establishments will simultaneously reduce costs for both producers and end-users. let's reduce pollution and take care of the environment, but considering the impact of such actions on our economy, especially in countries where energy production is still largely based on coal.

in writing. ‒ i support the report on financial changes, as they relate to the implementation of the new eu directives on public procurement. these directives rightly do not focus solely on the cost of procurement, but emphasise that social and labour law and the need to protect the environment should also be taken into account in the public procurement procedure. the bids cannot be assessed solely on the basis of whether they are the most economically advantageous. equally important is whether the people employed in the execution of the tenders are paid a decent wage and whether their labour rights are respected. as the regulation of the european parliament and the council is moving in this direction, i voted in favour of it.

in writing. according to available data, women are better educated than men, but this does not translate into their position in the labour market. statistically, women are less active in the workplace, earn less in the same job and are underrepresented in decision-making bodies in different areas of the economy. the data show that if the current trend in the increase in female employment in the eu continues at the same level, the europe 2020 employment rate of 75% for women and men aged 20-64 will be delayed by 18 years. addressing labour market disparities requires coordinated action at european and national level in cooperation with employers and trade unions. to increase women's participation in the labour market, we need an effective family policy aimed at facilitating work-life balance, including through the provision of good quality childcare. in addition, women should be facilitated to re-enter the labour market through appropriate training and vocational counselling. we also need to promote more women's employment, support their entrepreneurship and their active participation in decision-making processes. i also draw attention to the role of education in promoting equal opportunities for women and men in the labour market and in combating gender stereotypes and discrimination.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the outcome of the vote of 7 october 2015, in which the european parliament adopted a resolution on the death penalty, strongly condemning its use and supporting any action to abolish it. the death penalty is still widely used in many countries around the world. according to the latest data, at least 2466 people were sentenced to death in 55 countries in 2014, an increase of almost 23% compared to 2013. such sentences are imposed for crimes such as drug trafficking and distribution, acts of terrorism, but also for homosexuality and adultery. the legal basis for such a declaration is determined by the country's legal system, tradition, culture and religious beliefs. in this context, i express my deep concern about the increasing use of the death penalty. the abolition of the death penalty is one of the main objectives of our community and its application is incompatible with the fundamental principles of the european union as enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights. our resolution calls for the immediate abolition of the death penalty and for reforms to the justice systems of those countries which still provide for it.
in writing. ‒ the total abolition of the death penalty is one of the main objectives of the european union's human rights policy. thanks to the efforts of international organizations and social change, more than 160 united nations member states have now abolished the death penalty or do not use it. however, last year nearly 2,500 executions were carried out in over 55 countries, a significant increase over previous years. the increasing use of the death penalty in the fight against terrorism and drug trafficking is particularly worrying. it is therefore necessary to take further diplomatic, political and economic steps to eradicate this inhumane practice. the european parliament resolution calls on the european external action service, the european commission and the member states to step up their efforts to abolish the death penalty in the world. for these reasons, i have decided to support this resolution.
in writing. ‒ in 2010, a waste tank at an aluminium smelter near the city of ajka in hungary burst, releasing nearly one million cubic metres of highly alkaline so-called red mud. several nearby villages were flooded, 10 people were killed, about 150 were injured, and a significant area was contaminated, including an area protected by the natura 2000 programme. the commission therefore concluded that the union industry suffered material injury within the meaning of article 3 (5) of the basic regulation. the disaster in hungary exposed shortcomings in the application of eu legislation and in inspection methods. the oral question to the commission and the council on this matter concerns the lessons learned from this disaster, in particular how the relevant legislation can be properly implemented and whether the institutions would favour the adoption of an eu mechanism to enable financial claims to be made in the event of similar events. the experience of the disaster in hungary shows the need for a more effective prevention system and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ ensuring equality between women and men in employment and work is one of the european union's priorities. the member states have adapted their national regulations to ensure that they comply with union law. the european parliament's report is generally accurate in outlining the difficulties in applying directive 2006/54/ec, but when it indicates what action the european commission should take to address the issues, it points to solutions that are sometimes highly controversial. examples include the requirement to introduce gender balance on boards of listed companies, the audit of the remuneration structure of companies with exclusionary sanctions against companies, or the curious proposal to impose the burden of proof on the employer that he is innocent of the alleged discrimination. beyond these examples of interference in the private sphere, there are vague proposals for the public sphere, such as the call for gender budgeting by states. these and other issues make the document presented imprecise and many of the proposals almost impossible to implement. i therefore decided to abstain from voting on this report.

in writing. ‒ the adoption of a draft resolution on gender equality and women's empowerment is a clear signal to the european commission that action on this issue needs to be accelerated. every year, 14 million girls are forced into marriage worldwide, and 62 million are not in school. in many countries, discriminatory laws and practices continue to deny women basic rights, access to employment and political and economic participation. this not only limits women's personal development, but also hinders their countries from achieving economic and social adjustment to the norms of the democratic world. women should be safe at all latitudes. the promotion of cultural change at institutional level and the emphasis on the eu's role in the international arena must be clearly visible in the text. women's health and reproductive rights must also be respected, especially now in areas of armed conflict. the real test of the effectiveness of our policies will be when women in developing countries start to feel the difference in the way they are treated by their local communities. we must do everything we can to keep our promises and put them into practice as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the application of directive 2006/54/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 5 july 2006 on the implementation of the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment. there is no doubt that the gradual elimination of the gender pay and pension gap is necessary. however, i regret that the european parliament has once again voted in favour of a report that promotes such demands as gender parity and lgbt issues. i believe that the commission's guidelines would be a better solution for the harmonisation of the definition of labour law concepts such as the gender pay gap or equal pay for equal work. as a member of the european conservatives and reformists group, i do not support the imposition of mandatory pay controls in publicly traded companies or the mandatory disclosure of average pay by gender for individual positions, as these would represent an additional administrative and financial burden for companies.
in writing. ‒ the principle of equal pay for equal work is an integral part of eu law and one of the key foundations of anti-discrimination policy in the member states. in practice, however, the average gender pay gap in the european union remains constant at 16.4%, and the so-called total pay gap, which takes into account the gender employment gap, is as high as 39%. i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of directive 2006/54/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 5 july 2006 on the implementation of the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation, as it recommends the introduction of practical solutions to reduce the pay gap, such as job classification and evaluation systems based on clear and comparable criteria. at the same time, it points out that the full closure of the wage and salary gap and the related pension gap also requires broader action in the form of an effective work-life balance policy that ensures equal participation of women and men in the labour market.
in writing. ‒ discrimination, as a social and economic phenomenon, is clearly an evil that must not be tolerated. the deliberate exclusion of a group from access to the labour market on the basis of gender, political beliefs, religion or ethnicity is contrary to the rules of democracy. however, equality is not a concept that can be considered in abstract terms and detached from social reality. it is not possible to require that there be equal representation of women and men in every area of life, that the choice of each position is determined primarily by mathematics and gender parity, rather than by the competence and experience of the candidate. the demands to encourage and encourage member states to include transgender and intersex people in diversity training, as well as the need to take gender into account in vocational training, which is also mentioned in this report, must be considered absurd and difficult to accept. once again, we have an example of using the noble idea of the need to empower women in the labour market to promote extreme leftist ideology and justify social experiments. the call to the european commission to hold member states accountable for failing to introduce explicit protection against gender-based discrimination is also scandalous. i am surprised that some of my polish colleagues supported such a call.

in writing. the rise of intolerance and the increasingly unspoken hate speech require the search for ways to curb these phenomena. the radicalization of attitudes is always facilitated by growing fears. today, the economic and refugee crises are the main drivers. in the 1950's, american psychologist gordon allport identified behaviors that can lead to escalation if ignored. the "pyramid of hate" he has created consists of negative comments, avoidance, discrimination, physical attacks, extermination. historical examples support this model. the council of europe has defined 'hate speech' as 'all forms of expression which propagate, incite, support or justify racial, religious, xenophobic, anti-semitic or other forms of hatred based on intolerance, including intolerance expressed through aggressive nationalism and ethnocentrism, discrimination and hostility towards minorities, immigrants and persons of foreign origin'. hatred and intolerance come in many forms. these may be jokes told among friends, drawings on walls, publications, advertisements, and increasingly, public statements by radical politicians that are translated into election ads. so each of us should respond to hate speech by demanding that hate signs and signs, hate websites be removed, and by notifying law enforcement agencies, which must be obliged to accept the notification. but the most important thing is to look at the causes of the phenomenon in depth, to act effectively in three directions: prevention education prosecution.

in writing. ‒ the resolution aims to express an opinion on the date of entry into force of a new implementing decision aimed at ensuring an adequate and effective exchange of information between member states and europol in order to combat cross-border crime (the so-called vis visa information system). the decision follows the judgment of the court of justice of the european union which annulled the original council decision no 2013/392. the court maintained the effects of the previous decision until the date of entry into force of the new decision. in order to ensure the continuity of the vis, the council proposed that the new decision 2008/633/jha should apply from 1 september 2013. the report accepts this proposal, is purely technical and uncontroversial and has not been the subject of any amendments during the committee stage. i therefore voted in favour of adopting a resolution approving the draft decision 2008/633/jha.

in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that climate policy is one of the greatest challenges facing humanity in terms of sustainable development, health and the global economy. we must take care of the environment not only for our own health, but also for the future generations who will also benefit from the same environment. the continuing climate change, from melting glaciers to frequent droughts and floods, requires a rapid response from the international community. and that's the response that's going to be the paris climate agreement. i am fully convinced that efficient, global action based on international solidarity is the right thing to do, but it must be done responsibly. the objectives should be reasonable and not harmful to the economy. first of all, those which do not eliminate many jobs or reduce them in part. they must not place undue burdens on industry. the financing of the proposed measures remains an important open question. by 2020, developing countries are to receive $100 billion a year to help finance greenhouse gas emissions reductions and other projects to protect vulnerable populations from the effects of climate change. i hope that the provision of new funding will, however, be the basis of the paris agreement.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that the climate change we are currently witnessing requires urgent action on our part, as it could lead to irreversible risks for societies and the entire biosphere. it is therefore essential that all parties to the climate negotiations make specific commitments to meet this challenge - one of the greatest challenges of modern civilization. the european parliament's report on the new international climate agreement to be concluded later this year in paris is the right step in the global fight against the changes that are taking place on our planet. but i think that there are many provisions in this document which, if implemented, would lead to a disruption of the european economy, an increase in unemployment, and, in the end, an increase in poverty in europe. it is clear that if the fight against climate change is not global and is confined to europe, we will not only fail to achieve our objectives, but worse, we will significantly reduce the competitiveness of our economy. some companies will move their operations outside the eu to save their profitability. others will go bankrupt or severely limit their activities in europe. i therefore decided to vote against the ep report because i believe that the position it outlines that the european union should present in the climate negotiations has not been properly balanced.
in writing. ‒ the 21st un conference on climate change (unfccc) is to be held in december 2015. it is widely believed that an international agreement on carbon emission limits will be reached. the agreement would take the form of a protocol or other legally binding document binding all parties to the unfccc. the envi committee decided to draw up an own-initiative report based on the commission communication on the paris protocol of march 2015. unfortunately, the report echoes the myths about the harmfulness of coal that have been repeatedly repeated in the eu institutions. such projects violate the principle of neutrality and infringe the competence of member states to decide on the structure of their energy supply. the introduction of further co2 restrictions will be of enormous importance for poland, negatively affecting the country's energy security. the restrictions that the eu has put in place so far, with poland at the forefront, are sufficient, and if the major emitters do not commit to restrictions at cop 21, the union's action in this area will continue to be pointless. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ there is a very tangible cost to making climate commitments, which no one in this institution wants to remember. this is a high price to be paid, especially by poland, for whom coal is a source of energy and economic security. the climate is constantly changing. it was changing before the industrial age, too, although the dogma that human activity is the major cause of global warming seems to be accepted by many. the paris climate summit, which raises such high hopes for a binding global agreement, will only show once again how far the european union is ahead of a number of world economies in its demands for decarbonisation. big players like china and the united states, despite declarations to reduce co2 emissions, calculated to win the approval of left-wing public opinion, will never give up what really shapes their prosperity an industry based largely on the use of fossil fuels. of course, we should look for ways to reduce our use of natural resources and to be as efficient as possible in their use, so that they last as long as possible. however, this should be done gradually and taking into account the interests of countries such as poland, which has no alternative to coal. the eu is offering to liquidate a key industry and sell us expensive green technologies. is this what european solidarity should look like?

in writing. ‒ the council's proposed decision amending the agreement between the european community and the swiss confederation is a further step towards making tax avoidance more effective. this is particularly relevant where those actions are undertaken by natural and legal persons established in the union with the assistance of financial institutions established in third countries. in its report, the european parliament endorses the draft council decision, while regretting that some improvements could not be made, particularly as regards the scope of the exchange of information and the automatic, mandatory and unhindered nature of this exchange. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are able to access the internet and to use it for their own purposes.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted against the council decision adopting a protocol amending the agreement between the european union and the swiss confederation on measures equivalent to those laid down in directive 2003/48/ec. the agreement is to be updated in the light of the change in the legal status on which it was based. the proposal to repeal directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income and the amendments to directive 2014/107/eu on administrative cooperation that extended its scope made it necessary to modify the content of the existing agreement. the amending protocol implements the oecd standard on the automatic exchange of financial data in tax matters. this makes it possible to effectively combat tax avoidance, which eu citizens have used financial institutions located in third countries to do. i therefore voted in favour of the council's decision to adopt the amending protocol.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted a non-binding opinion on the repeal of directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income. it aims to introduce a uniform standard for the exchange of financial information in tax matters. the amendment of directive 2014/107/eu on administrative cooperation, which will introduce the oecd global standard for the flow of such information in the european union as from 1 january 2016, has made it necessary to adapt the existing rules to the new legal situation. in order to avoid the parallel application of two standards, i consider it necessary to repeal directive 2003/48/ec. at the same time, given the risk of possible legal loopholes in relations with the 12 associated territories, i support efforts to agree as soon as possible on appropriate agreements with non-eu-regulated entities. the need to combat tax avoidance and to avoid imposing unnecessary burdens on businesses has led me to vote in favour of the resolution as it stands.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with decision 2008/615/jha on the strengthening of cross-border cooperation, particularly in combating terrorism and cross-border crime, the supply of personal data provided for in this decision may not commence until the data protection provisions have been implemented in the national law of the member states. poland, belgium and sweden completed the data protection questionnaire as well as the questionnaire on the exchange of dactyloscopic data and carried out pilot projects. on the basis of the overall assessment carried out, the council concluded that those countries have fully implemented the general data protection provisions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the decision to launch in poland the automated data exchange for fingerprint data. it is one of the pragmatic steps to improve cooperation within the european union in the effective fight against terrorism and international crime. poland has already adapted its legislation to the union's approach to the protection of sensitive data and the exchange of dactyloscopic data. moreover, and very importantly, this has been confirmed in practice by a successful pilot operation with austria. this means that poland will be entitled and prepared to transfer personal data to the authorities of other eu countries and to receive similar information itself. no doubt this is helpful in the fight against crime.
in writing. ‒ the report contains the conclusions of the negotiations between the institutions accompanying the second reading on the amendment of the package travel directive. the directive has been in force for over 20 years and is seen as an effective and useful tool for consumer protection in the travel and tourism industry. the amendment aims to adapt the legislation to new practices in the tourism industry, including the move away from comprehensive package holidays towards self-organised holidays via the internet. such bookings are not covered by the protection provided for under the directive, for example in the case of the consumer's return to the country in the event of the bankruptcy of the travel service provider. the directive aims to resolve this conflict while maintaining the ability of online travel service providers to innovate and offer the best deals to consumers. i therefore supported the amendment which will help to clarify and improve the situation of consumers, while at the same time reducing the burden on tourist event organisers.
in writing. ‒ the tourism industry, which is often undervalued, is very often a driver of economic growth in most countries and has a significant impact on gdp. the european union should therefore act to develop this sector. one of the more important elements should be, firstly, to support, mainly in access to external sources of finance, especially those small and medium-sized enterprises. on the other hand, it is necessary to take steps to deregulate the tourism sector. at the same time, it is necessary to take account of consumers of tourism services, who, due to the specific nature of the sector, require special protection. as we know, it is extremely difficult to combine all these elements and to balance and maintain the right symmetry in the entrepreneur-client relationship in the tourism industry. i believe that the council's position at first reading on tourist events and related tourist services was not appropriate, and that is why i have decided to vote against the recommendations for the second reading of the european parliament, and i believe that in the future a compromise will be found which will take into account the interests of both the providers and the recipients of tourist services.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased with the outcome of the european parliament's vote today on the final form of the ep and council regulation on the european single market for electronic communications. we have thus completed the final stage of the legislative work on the introduction of regulations that will ensure net neutrality and the abolition of roaming charges throughout the community. these issues have long been in need of settlement. the final abolition of roaming charges in the eu is planned for june 2017. the regulation is the result of long-term parliament negotiations and efforts to improve consumer rights across the eu. in 2014, the commission presented the results of a survey which showed that 94% of europeans limit their use of internet services when travelling abroad precisely because of the cost. the european union should make a continuous effort to look after the well-being of its citizens. the regulations will remove outdated business practices in the telecommunications market and remove barriers that have prevented the free use of digital services. access to the internet is a human right and the digital future is one of the pillars of a modern and strong europe. unifying the rules on networks and roaming calls is particularly important as it affects millions of eu citizens and will have a significant impact on their lives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing measures relating to open internet access and amending directive 2002/22/ec on universal service and users' rights relating to electronic communications networks and services and regulation (eu) no 531/2012 on roaming on public mobile communications networks within the union. i believe that the negotiated agreement is beneficial for the citizens of the european union, as it will free consumers from roaming charges from june 2017. the compromise also includes rules to protect the open internet in line with the principle of net neutrality.
in writing. ‒ i support the comments in the recommendation for second reading of the instrument laying down measures for the position of the european council on the eu regulation on roaming on public mobile communications networks within the union and on the single market for electronic communications. among the many positive decisions taken in the documents covered by this recommendation, the most important one concerns the abolition of eu roaming charges as of july 2017. at the same time, the current fees , already significantly low compared to non-european countries, will be reduced once again from april 2016. in an era of highly intensive electronic communication, with the telephone being used almost constantly, mainly for data transmission over the internet, this decision is of great importance and is next to the possibility of traveling without a passport one of the key symbols of community and integration in the european union.
in writing. ‒ the text of the agreement at second reading lays down rules on the abolition of roaming charges when travelling within the eu from june 2017 and the introduction of rules to secure the open internet in the eu, in line with the principle of 'net neutrality'. from june 2017, mobile phone charges when travelling in the eu will be the same as at home for a monthly subscription for free calls, sms or data transmissions abroad within the eu, the charge will be the same as at home, without any additional charges. these rules will prevent abuses, such as when a customer buys a sim card in another eu country where prices are lower to use it at home. the regulation also introduces important consumer protection measures, in particular providing access to information on their rights in roaming and the use of facilities and the power to detect possible breaches of the open internet principles. i therefore support the report.
in writing. ‒ the abolition of roaming charges in the european union is a reality. the commission notes that the price reduction is not a decision that will take effect immediately, as it will be fully effective from june 2017, but that customers will already experience a significant price reduction from 1 april 2016. this decision and the benefits it brings to eu citizens show how much good can be done when the eu institutions focus on addressing a specific problem that is really making life difficult for citizens in the member states. the situation where freedom of movement is associated with the costs of absurdly high roaming charges, especially for data transmission, has not been adapted to the requirements of the digital age. fortunately, the resistance of the telecommunications companies was overcome and the matter was settled. however, the proposed solutions are not absolute and contain a number of safeguards to protect the market through so-called shopping tourism. this solution addresses the specific needs of people travelling within the european union, but is not intended to introduce a mechanism of competition between telecommunications operators operating in the member states. i voted in favour of this solution because of the benefits it will bring to the citizens of the european union. i believe this is a good forecast for the future and a harbinger of the positive changes that will come from working towards a digital single market in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i fully support this report, which aims to contribute to the abolition of the death penalty worldwide and the prevention of torture through eu controls on the export of goods used for torture and drugs used for lethal injection. i particularly welcomed the introduction of a clause allowing customs authorities to detain any goods, whether or not listed in the annexes, which are reasonably suspected of being used for torture.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a leading and responsible actor in the fight against the death penalty and the elimination of torture at global level. the european parliament's report aims to tighten current rules on so-called ancillary services related to the transfer of goods, as well as transit, technical support and the introduction for commercial purposes of goods that could be used for capital punishment. the amendments to the report, which envisage the creation of a periodic review mechanism and a more systematic exchange of information and reporting in order to strengthen surveillance and effective implementation of the regulation, seem to be a very appropriate amendment to the commission proposal. in my view, any effort to abolish the death penalty and to prevent torture should be introduced and promoted in all areas of eu policy, especially trade policy, which is why i decided to vote in favour of parliament's report.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur's proposal to extend the scope of automatic exchange of information from cross-border to all tax interpretations and the suggestion to introduce an immediate exchange of information instead of a periodic exchange will require more work from national tax authorities. i am also aware that the increase in the amount of information exchanged will also require a number of changes to national reporting requirements. however, if the stakes are to curb tax fraud or the use by some entities - especially large corporations with a strong global legal base - of existing loopholes in legal systems to avoid paying taxes where they actually do business, then i am sure that it is reasonable to expect the public administration to adapt its procedures to the requirements of the situation. existing technological solutions and the increasing digitalisation of the work of the administration create the conditions under which much more operational activity can and should be required from public offices than has been the case until now. the european parliament's report is consultative in nature to solutions already agreed within the council. however, even in this situation, it is important that the representatives of european societies send a strong signal to brussels and national authorities to take more advanced measures to combat aggressive tax avoidance by big business.
in writing. ‒ fair competition is the engine of development, but to do so, all the principles of equal business competition in the global market must be respected. one key element is the fair enforcement of the tax obligation. cooperation between states in this area is therefore important and necessary. the amendments to directive 2011/16/eu on the mandatory exchange of information in the field of taxation proposed by the commission are a legitimate step towards improving the current law. i have decided to vote in favour of the report and i believe that the council will take the right decisions as soon as possible, which will benefit the member states but also, in the end, the businesses themselves.
in writing. ‒ the document put to the vote is the council's non-binding position on the draft submitted by the european commission. in order to effectively address the cross-border problem of tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and harmful tax competition, the commission has put forward proposals to amend directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation, which aims to increase the transparency of administrative cooperation in the field of taxation. in response, the european parliament proposed that all tax interpretations should be covered by directive 2011/16/eu, not just those that may have a cross-border effect. there is therefore a concern that the significant increase in the circulation of information will require changes in national reporting requirements. parliament also proposed the creation of a central database to collect the annual reports submitted. in view of the excessive reporting obligations imposed on member states and the concerns about the confidentiality of the data disclosed in the annual reports, i voted against parliament's position on this matter.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur criticises the international community's response in the first months of the crisis and stresses the importance of a rapid response and the eu's role as the world's main provider of development aid. the international community should start thinking about the post-epidemic period today. the eu's response will have to focus on two areas of development assistance, including investments in health care and the economic recovery needed in countries affected by the ebola epidemic (sierra leone, liberia, guinea). i therefore supported the report.
in writing. ‒ since the outbreak last year, ebola has claimed more than 11 000 lives, mainly in sierra leone, liberia and guinea. that's why prevention is so important, to prevent similar epidemics, all over the world, not just in africa. the ep report properly outlines the conclusions for the future and the action the eu should take both within its own continent and in its relations with the countries where the outbreak has occurred. it is also worth remembering that the tragedy of the countries affected by the epidemic does not end with thousands of deaths. the ebola virus has led to the devastation and inhibition of the socio-economic development processes in sierra leone, liberia and guinea. according to recent estimates, the epidemic cost the economies of west africa alone more than $2.2 billion. multilateral support for these countries is therefore needed.
in writing. ‒ the vote was on a resolution which parliament had worked on on its own initiative. the rapporteur regrets the slow response of the international community in the first months of the ebola crisis in sierra leone, liberia and guinea. it stressed that the eu, as the main donor of development aid, should respond decisively. its assistance will be particularly needed in two areas: the rebuilding of health care and the economies of countries affected by the crisis. i support the solutions proposed by the rapporteur to improve the situation in the regions at risk: the creation of a european rapid reaction team of experts and the revision of the programming of the european development fund to take account of the new needs of these countries. the european union cannot afford to downplay this humanitarian crisis. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, although unfortunately it does not cover all aspects of the problem of car emissions. it is sharp, suggesting a more ambitious approach to the far-reaching emission limits of new vehicles, not only on test benches but also during the in-service operation of the diesel engines that power them. the resolution omits the environmental and human health damage that older engines have caused and continue to cause. it is almost certain that, for example, the euro 4 and euro 5 standards, as well as euro 6, were not respected in practice. the resolution does not call for the adoption of a repair clause by all member states, although it could improve the maintenance of low emission operating standards throughout the european automotive market.
in writing. ‒ following the volkswagen emissions cheating scandal, the european parliament adopted a resolution on the matter on 27 october. i supported the motion for a resolution and had earlier made a speech in parliament criticising the eu's regulatory inertia on this type of abuse. i also pointed out the hypocrisy of the eu's climate policy, which 'looks the other way on car pollution'. in its resolution on emission measurements in the motor vehicle sector, parliament calls for, among other things, the measures i mentioned in my speech: stricter testing requirements, measurement of real-world emissions, comprehensive monitoring of the motor vehicle market. the house also called for an urgent inquiry into the fraud of the car group, for other car companies to be audited and for the role of eu and national authorities in the fraud to be investigated.
in writing. ‒ deliberate criminal behaviour by any company, no matter how large, will not be tolerated, as it not only causes a loss of public trust and undermines the quality of european products, but also causes significant harm to the health of europeans. to prevent similar situations, real-world emissions tests to ensure that new cars meet euro 6 emissions standards should be introduced by 2017 and an independent european body responsible for emissions testing should be established. we must first of all prevent the negative effects of this scandal on the workers management decisions must not result in job cuts.
in writing. ‒ following reports published on 18 september by the us environmental protection agency (epa) and the california air resources board (carb) on emissions-disrupting devices installed by volkswagen in its cars, the european parliament decided to take a position on the matter by adopting a resolution. it calls on the european commission to ensure a full assessment of the possible manipulation of the automotive sector and to assess the possibility of strengthening the involvement of national authorities in the type-approval procedure. it is also proposed that real driving emissions (rde) procedures be introduced as a matter of urgency, with a target date of 2017. i believe that the disclosure of falsified measurement data is evidence of the compromise not only of the vw group, but of the entire european union. however, i do not agree with the argument put forward in the resolution that a special supervisory body would be necessary at eu level to ensure the enforceability of existing legislation. this is contrary to the calls to avoid unnecessary administrative burdens and, above all, to the principle of subsidiarity. i could not therefore vote in favour of the measure.

position of the european union and of the international community through the quartet is much more united than members are able to manage within their own political groups. this is not the time for us only to call for something or to condemn something. do we realise that we are in a serious, dramatic situation which could be the end of the oslo framework? so, if i hear readiness from both sides to work together, to restart talks and to work together in implementing some measures on the ground, i ask you in this room what you think our role as the european union is: to condemn and to call for something or to try to bring them to do it? i believe our role is the second one, partly because i do not see many actors pushing to play this role at this moment. there are plenty of other crises competing with this one, and we europeans are one of the few still focusing very much on this. but we have to do it with the right approach: trying to help them to get out of this bubble. i am also a historian through my studies and i love history, but the problem we have here is that there is too much history. if someone does not help the parties and the people – the israelis and the palestinians framework. someone said at the beginning of the debate – i think it was gianni pittella – that we are losing generations. there are generations in israel and in palestine who do not believe in those two states anymore. on both sides, there are young people who believe either in no state at all or in one state only. i believe that the oslo framework is still a valid perspective for both, with all that goes with it. but we are at the edge. it is not going to continue like this. so this is what i am trying to do: passing the message to the leadership – and hopefully also to the people, but that is not only my job – that if you say you want two states, either you do something now or it is gone. we do not have the safety net of a plan b. we will have to reinvent it if we leave the oslo framework. it is no longer about what we call for or what we condemn. if it is done, it is a totally different story. the world does not need another complication in the region. that is why, of all the conflicts we have, to me this is one of the most urgent because its global ramifications go everywhere in the world and the presence of the holy sites makes it even more serious. it is, paradoxically, also a conflict that, if there is enough political will, can be resolved, because they have been discussing for decades how it should look in the end, and there is – as someone rightly whether we can do something together. there are moments where violence is higher, like this one, that could also be the turning point in a crisis because the parties realise that they are risking too much internally. violence in israel also comes from the inside. the situation inside the west bank means that, in my view, both leaderships realise that it is in their interests to tackle this seriously. i might be wrong: it could be that this does not lead anywhere, and then we will need to see, together with our friends in the rest of the international community, what we do about that. but my role at the moment – and i will ask you, as europeans, to be united on this – is to try to see if there is one chance for the two sides to start doing something useful on the ground instead of having their people killing each other, and to facilitate this to happen because we are not going to have many chances in the future. i feel a sense of urgency and that a dramatic moment has come. i do not think that this is just another chapter of a long story. the situation is different today. we can come back in another month or another month and a half and discuss our statements, our options, our condemning, whatever. in the meantime, we need to try to bring them together again, together with arab friends and together with the international community. but this is our work and i am sure that this parliament will support this effort. this is a crisis where the european union has a lot to spend in terms of political capacity. i said this exactly one year ago in the hearing in the committee on foreign affairs. this is the crisis where we are the biggest player if we want to transform the money we have spent and the economic, political and cultural relations we have with both madam president! cohesion policy is without doubt one of the most pro-growth and pro-investment policies of the union. however, i am convinced that by simplifying this policy we could make it more effective and achieve even better results. last year, over 1,500 irregularities were reported in cohesion policy projects. it should be remembered, however, that a large number of these irregularities are not the result of the bad will of the beneficiaries, but of a misunderstanding of the guidelines and regulations. simplifying the language as well as making clearer the expectations of beneficiaries would certainly have a positive impact on subsequent audits. the commission should also avoid introducing changes to the rules during the lifetime of projects. this practice not only imposes additional costs on the beneficiaries, but also involves a workload that prevents them from concentrating on the project. the lack of adequate financial impact analysis of the new rules and the long procedures are also frustrating. it cannot be that the procedural costs are disproportionate to the activities of the project and the length of the procedures makes the project unjustified. i also support greater flexibility in cohesion policy based on mutual trust between the european commission and the member states. today, that trust is not enough.
rapporteur.– madam president, we are here because we decided to amend the european union electoral law. this law dates back to 1976 and, in the meantime, as we all know, europe has been through major and unimaginable changes, in terms of both the scope and the substance of eu integration. the european parliament has also changed dramatically, in size and in relation to its competences, especially as a co—legislator, with its decisions having huge impact on people’s lives. it should not come as a surprise that we want to adjust the electoral act of 1976 to the new reality. this report highlights the right of the european parliament to decide on its own electoral procedure. we all have similar experience, as european parliamentarians, of elections to the european parliament, which continue to be extremely national. no european issues are discussed during the electoral campaign and the european dimension of this democratic process is not sufficiently visible. that is why we have proposed a change to the european electoral act of 1976. in the proposal, we give the european parliament the right to decide on the date of the election. we ask member states to ensure that all citizens working or living outside the european union are granted the right to vote and enabled to do. we also propose machinery to avoid double voting. we are asking member states to create the conditions for voting by electronic means, via the internet or by post. people with reduced mobility will certainly benefit. i know that some colleagues worry about internet voting, but it can be made safe. we have the example of estonia which started internet voting in 2005, when 2% of estonians decided to use this tool. this year, 30% of estonians voted via the internet. we also want to see more gender equality in the lists, so we are proposing the alignment of deadlines for some elements of the electoral process, such as the establishment of lists. let me also mention the possibility for national parties of informing voters, via the ballot paper, of their affiliation with european political parties. citizens should have this information. through these and other measures we hope to contribute to making elections to the european parliament truly european, and to increasing citizens’ interest in participating in this important element of european decision making. let me conclude by saying that people’s impact on europe starts with their informed participation in the european elections.
on behalf of the ecr group. - madam president! - i have to go. the group of the european conservatives and reformists has a good view of the current european parliamentary rules and we do not see the need to change them, and we certainly do not see the need to change them in the direction of centralisation, of unifying electoral law. there are two important things to look at here: first, the belief that if we encourage lowering the voting age to 16, or encouraging light voting, in the form of online voting, then the attendance at the european parliament will go up a lot. we're not convinced of these measures. the ballot has its dignity, its gravity. online forms should not be used as standard forms. but more important is the idea of centralising electoral law, including ideas such as the obligation to use the logo of the european party alongside the logo of the national parties. we don't see the need for that, it shouldn't be an obligation. there are new political parties in the life of our countries that can make this choice later, when they sit in the european parliament. why force them to do it during the election campaign? but above all, the legitimacy of the european parliament must be based on respect for national traditions, constitutional traditions and the sovereignty of nations. the closer to the national context, the closer to the citizens. the more centralised and uniform legislation is, the more the european parliament will distance itself from the real problems of its citizens. that's why we're voting against this bill.
rapporteur.– madam president, i would like to thank both those who were saying that we lack ambition and those who were saying that we are too ambitious, because basically those were the two groups we heard here in the chamber. to those who consider that we lack ambition with this report, i would say that sometimes in our work, and you all experience this, we want to bring more people on board for the ideas we consider important for european citizens – then, of course, our level of ambition falls to that of the common ambition. to a certain extent, that is why we could not do certain things. another reason, however, has to do with the procedure involving the council: we have to go with this proposal to the council, and the council, under the treaty, can completely ignore our proposal. that is why we are trying to build something that will get through the whole system and take us a step forward in the evolution of the european parliament’s right to decide on the procedure for its own electoral process. these points may constitute an explanation in response to the first group of comments. to all those who consider we are going too far, i have to say that i totally disagree with you. in response to those who say we are moving too far in the sense of taking responsibility for issues that should be addressed at national level, as matters for national sovereignty, i would say that this proposal brings members of the european parliament closer to the voters, and also brings european citizens closer to europe. so through this proposal i believe we are addressing what is on behalf of the ppe group. - madam president! - i have to go. a well-functioning judiciary is one of the most important pillars of a democratic state. the european union is a family of democracies, and a well-functioning european judiciary should therefore be of great importance to all of us. so it is with great pleasure that i say on behalf of the ppe group that this difficult, very arduous negotiating process of reaching a final compromise is finally coming to an end. tomorrow we are going to vote on the compromise which was negotiated between the european parliament and the council last week. this compromise is based on the recognition of the need to increase the number of judges in the court. there is no doubt that the court needs more judges to function efficiently, so that we do not incur financial penalties for lengthy trial periods. but i also want to express my deep gratitude that the european parliament has managed to introduce two important elements: first, a review clause that will allow us, as soon as the reform is completed in 2019, to look at how it has affected the functioning of the court and whether it is really as effective as we see it today. and the second thing is the adoption, together with the council, of a european parliament resolution on the need for gender equality in the court of justice. but i want to say that this is just the beginning of the road and that this gender equality should be manifested everywhere. it cannot therefore be established for one institution without looking at the other institutions. this is the beginning of the road we're going to take. the ppe group will vote tomorrow to support the agreement reached with the council.
in writing. the reform of the court of justice of the european union is dictated by the ever-increasing number of cases to be heard. in 2010, there were less than 600, in 2014 there were 912, and by march 2015 there was a record 1393. the waiting period for a decision is now 4 to 5 years. it should be recalled that the right to a judgment within a reasonable time is guaranteed by article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights and that access to justice is a cornerstone of democracy. in this context, it is necessary to strengthen the court of first instance with a larger number of judges so that it can give judgment effectively. at the end of the envisaged reform, it will consist of 56 judges, two from each member state. furthermore, given that the pursuit of equality between women and men is one of the objectives of the union, i am pleased that we have also managed to introduce an amendment stating that member state governments should ensure, as far as possible, equal participation of both sexes in the selection process of future judges. the proper functioning of the judiciary requires expenditure. the commission notes that the court of justice has consistently held that the principle of proportionality is not applicable to the application of the principle of proportionality. i am satisfied with the compromise reached with the council.

rapporteur.– mr president, i would like, on behalf of the epp group and also in agreement with my colleague and co—rapporteur representing the socialists and democrats, jo leinen, to request that the vote on the european electoral law be postponed to the november i part-session.
in writing. ‒ maintaining the european parliament's three seats, in three different countries and cities, i.e. brussels, strasbourg and luxembourg, is extremely costly and difficult for europeans to understand, especially for citizens of those member states to whom the european union institutions address appeals for public spending cuts. it therefore seems perfectly rational to choose one city for the seat of the european parliament, most likely brussels, where the other eu institutions are also located. i understand perfectly well the symbolic importance of the city of strasbourg for the franco-german reconciliation after the second world war. however, it should not be forgotten that the city is home to other very important european institutions, such as the council of europe and the european court of human rights. i therefore believe that we should once again turn to the question of a single seat for the european parliament, which would be more in line with both our needs and our capabilities.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 as regards the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. i do not think that rejecting the commission's proposal is enough. the regulation in its current form is not ideal and requires more precision, in particular in terms of definitions, in order to ensure its effective implementation and legal certainty. however, rejecting this proposal is not a good solution, as action is needed as soon as possible on a matter of such importance to public health. the current legal framework allows the european commission to authorise a product after obtaining a positive opinion from the european food safety authority, as member states are not able to take a qualified majority in the standing committee. as a member from poland, where the majority of citizens oppose the marketing of genetically modified organisms, i believe that the current rules are not satisfactory and must be changed.
in writing. ‒ one of the most important problems facing the european community since the end of the second world war was the problem of hunger. producing pest-resistant food and feed that does not deteriorate quickly and retains the colour expected was a priority. the effects of genetically modified food and feed on human health and life shall be clearly identified. there is no reliable research to answer the question of whether genetically modified food and feed have a positive effect on human health and life or the opposite. some opponents point out that they may cause the extinction of bees, the growth of weeds that are harder to eradicate, an increase in allergies, and finally, an increase in diseases, especially of the digestive system. the wishes of those who do not wish to consume genetically modified food should be taken into account. for this reason, such food should be appropriately labelled to enable the consumer to make informed choices. i think the eu institutions should do more to promote organic food. at the present stage of knowledge, the subject of genetically modified food and feed should rather be approached with caution. in the european union, almost half of food is wasted, mostly in households, and an information campaign to raise consumer awareness of this issue is therefore needed. in view of the above, i voted against the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ i have voted against the commission's proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 in regards to the possibility for the member states to restrict or prohibit use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. the reasons explaining my decision in that matter, consider both practical level of implementation of this proposal, as well as the possible consequences on eu agricultural sector. the implementation of this proposal is basically nearly impossible to achieve. this is due to the fact that the border control has been already abolished and the only way of monitoring the exports and imports of gmo food is to introduce the border control again. this measure is absolutely pointless, since it would actually constitute the regress of economic achievements of european customs union and the single market. in terms of the consequences on eu agricultural sector, the proposal will have a direct negative impact on it. the research shows that, nowadays, eu is highly dependent on gm imports to feed the livestock and banning such imports would highly reduce the livestock production within the eu, and therefore, in the long-term scenario our economy would suffer severely.
in writing. ‒ the term 'novel food' refers to a type of new food that has not been consumed in the european union before or is produced by previously unknown methods. this applies to non-eu regional products, newly produced nutrients and extracts from known foods. the first provision on these products appeared in european legislation in 1997 and has not been updated since. the proposed amendments are designed to update and harmonise the existing standards in order to remove legal uncertainties and increase consumer safety. it is necessary to take account of technological progress and to simplify the provisions in order to exclude from their scope products covered by other regulations. it is necessary to introduce criteria to enable member states to clearly identify which products belong to the appropriate category 'novel foods'. a transparent and easily accessible product list is necessary, which will be regularly updated and thus sensitive to market changes. amendments to streamline the legislation are necessary in the face of rapidly changing production technologies and increasing access to goods from outside the eu. however, it should be borne in mind that the proposed amendments are designed to ensure consumer safety and this must remain the fundamental condition for any changes.
in writing. ‒ the rapid development of the food market, combined with the introduction of innovation in this field over the last 20 years, has forced us, as a co-financing partner of the european union, to take appropriate decisions that will ensure consumer safety. i want to say that i am very pleased that a trilateral agreement has been reached on this matter. the emergence of so-called new foodstuffs in europe requires the adoption of legislation at community level, which is why i voted in favour of it. it is worth noting that the planned regulation will also cover traditional food from non-eu countries, which has been considered safe and harmless for health for years. i would like to stress that this will avoid excessive and numerous controls by the member states, and will speed up the introduction of these products on the european market. i think this will be a good solution for smaller businesses, because the whole procedure will be less costly, more transparent and simplified and uniform. we must not forget that the products of this sector are currently treated differently in different member states. by voting for the project, i also want to ensure that entrepreneurs have equal access to and sale of the products. the standards developed in the tripartite compromise will not only make novel foods more competitive and attractive, but will also provide an adequate level of protection for the lives of eu citizens, which i believe is one of the most important elements of this regulation.
in writing. ‒ the report was put to the vote in the context of the legislative procedure to update the legal framework governing the authorisation procedure for novel foods. the current regulation was adopted in 1997 and does not provide for any measures to help businesses to introduce innovative products on the market. the need to change the procedures for placing novel foods on the eu market over the past 20 years has led to the need to change the market situation. the draft regulation envisages, inter alia, simplifying the procedure for traditional foods from third countries by allowing for notification only, maintaining the precautionary principle for the commission's action in the field of novel foods and introducing a principle of transparency of uses, under which the commission will be required to provide information on restrictions imposed by third countries. in my view, the text presented is a reasonable compromise on the above issues. i have therefore decided to support the resolution.
