in writing. ‒ a few months ago, eu environment ministers agreed that the level of air pollution on our continent is too high (according to ec figures, some 400 000 europeans die prematurely every year from diseases caused by inhaling harmful compounds). it therefore decided to reduce emissions of hazardous compounds from industry, traffic and power plants by 2030. however, in addition to the limits on sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter, it has also been decided to limit emissions of methane, for example, a gas produced by animals, mainly cattle, and such a limitation can cause serious disruption in the livestock sector. we are firmly opposed, together with the members of the european people's party and colleagues from other groups, to the introduction of measures to limit methane emissions, which could harm european agricultural production in the long term. i hope that, despite the unfavourable outcome of the vote in the ep, the council will take account of the voice of reason in the negotiations and that the amendment of the directive on national pollution ceilings will not harm our farmers.
in writing. ‒ the draft revision of directive 2001/81/ec on national emission limits (nec directive) is part of the strategy 'clean air for europe'. the existing legislation provides for national emission limits for certain substances to apply from 2010: sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), non-methane volatile organic compounds (nmvocs) and ammonia (nh3). the proposal for a directive provides for the continuation of this mechanism for 2020-2030 and reporting obligations, and extends the existing catalogue of restrictions to include new substances: fine particulate matter (pm2,5) and methane (ch4). according to calculations carried out for the commission, the entry into force of this regulation could result in a reduction of up to 42% in the number of beef cattle in poland, 24% in the number of dairy cattle and 12% in the number of pigs. in view of the far-reaching restrictions that could be imposed on my country, i have tabled amendments with mr wojciechowski to keep methane out of the directive. the draft as proposed by the rapporteur is unacceptable to me.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative (eci) was created to enable citizens of the union to take part in legislative initiatives and to influence eu policy and legislation. the eci was intended to increase social mobilisation and strengthen a sense of european citizenship. in the first three years of operation, 51 calls for initiatives were received, supported by over six million eu citizens. only three claims were considered admissible. none of them have led to the introduction of new legislation. the initiative has not met citizens' expectations and much remains to be done to realise its full potential. the main objective of this report is to improve the functioning of the eci, to make it more user-friendly and to remove obstacles that make it difficult for organisers to take up the initiative. lessons can be drawn from the fact that six eci organisers, accounting for 30% of all rejected proposals, brought a case against the ec before the european court of justice. in addition, the number of applications received is currently decreasing. the initiative should aim at engaging society and promoting dialogue between citizens and institutions. this instrument should encourage as many community citizens as possible to participate in the further development of the european integration process.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the european citizens' initiative. the european citizens' initiative is one of the best instruments for creating eu law. the european citizens' initiative allows citizens to be actively involved in the development of eu legislation and thus also gives citizens a better understanding of the functioning of the eu institutions. i fully agree with the report that, despite the unquestionable added value of the european citizens' initiative, its functioning needs to be improved and facilitated. the first is the need to promote the initiative more widely among citizens so that they are fully informed of their rights as citizens of the union, including the right to participate in a citizens' initiative. the practical aspects of the operation of the initiative should then be examined in order to help the organisers of the initiatives to implement them effectively and efficiently. in this respect, i support the creation in each member state of an information unit, for example at the european commission representation, which would provide information and legal advice on european citizens' initiatives. in addition, in the context of the creation of the digital union, consideration should also be given to facilitating and increasing access to software for collecting online signatures, for example for persons with disabilities.
in writing. ‒ 51 citizens' initiatives have been submitted so far. three of them reached the required threshold of 1 million citizens' signatures (including the 'one of us' initiative, which gathered nearly 1.8 million signatures). however, none of these initiatives was followed up, as the european commission refused to initiate the legislative procedure. the shape of regulation 211/2011 means that it is the european commission that actually decides on the fate of a citizens' initiative, regardless of whether the initiative has fulfilled all the conditions required by law. this procedure makes the citizens' right to initiative unrealistic and fictitious, mainly because of the arbitrary power of the european commission. moreover, the regulation as it stands creates a whole series of requirements which are, in essence, an unjustified obstacle to citizens' initiative. for example, different personal data are required to support citizens' initiatives in 28 member states under different national rules. the european union, meanwhile, cannot allow the creation of de facto dead institutions and 'internally blocked institutions'. the direction of this report is clear, aiming to correct existing errors, as well as to strengthen and improve the institution of the citizens' initiative, to communicate it better and to make it a more realistic instrument. that's why i endorsed the report.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative (eci) has been in operation since 2012 and its main objective is to enable citizens of the union to participate in the legislative initiative process. unfortunately, based on the views of civil society and the commission's report, it is concluded that this instrument does not fulfil its basic functions. since 2012, 51 initiatives have been submitted, none of which have resulted in the adoption of the proposed legislation. in addition, the organisers of many of the rejected initiatives have appealed the commission's decisions to refuse registration of these initiatives to the court of justice and the european ombudsman. the decline in the number of new initiatives is also widely highlighted. the reasons for this are disproportionately stringent requirements and an unnecessarily complex system. the main points are: insufficient communication activities on the eio at european and national level, a very different system of providing personal data to support the eio in the different member states, the mistrust of citizens towards the provision of personal data required for supporting the eio and the personal responsibility of the organisers for the protection of personal data, the lack of detailed and exhaustive reasons for the rejection of the eios submitted by the commission, too short a timeframe for the collection of declarations of support by the organisers.
in writing. ‒ the source of democracy's strength is civil society. for it not only to function well but also to develop, it must be able to influence the outcome of government not just once every few years in an electoral act, but also on a regular basis, which is what the european citizens' initiative is for in the case of the european union. i am in favour of it being operational and of taking measures which can help to make citizens more effective participants in the solution of issues which are important to all of us. i therefore decided to vote in favour of parliament's report, which contains a number of proposals to simplify the formal and procedural requirements for the submission of a european citizens' initiative.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on european citizens initiative. eci is a new political right introduced for our citizens, which allows them to play an active role in the creation of eu law. the initiative was introduced in april 2012, and from that time, we have received a number of complaints suggesting that eci is not working as well as intended. first of all, the report focuses mainly on increasing the public awareness of eci. in order for the initiative to be effective, it is crucial to raise the awareness amongst both our citizens and that appropriate media, and also to ensure its transparency. moreover, the provisions of that report point out several difficulties that organisers have encountered since the regulation entered into force in spring 2012, and it suggests the measures that should be undertaken in order to eliminate those problems. hence, the idea of establishing a dedicated eci office is very promising and it may, in fact, prove to be a sufficient way to ensure that the eci is working well enough.
in writing. ‒ the recent economic crisis has had a significant impact on the adriatic-ionian countries, in particular high unemployment, debt levels, inefficiency and inhibition of economic growth and a decline in investment. the countries of the region have a huge potential that is currently not being exploited. i voted in favour of the resolution because it creates legal instruments to enable the countries of the region to develop a common strategy and coordinate their action under the commission's guidance, and thus, in my view, gives them a unique opportunity for rapid and sustainable development and for the western balkan countries to move closer to the eu. i believe that the implementation of the development strategy envisaged in the resolution will benefit both eu member states and third countries. the requirements of good water management, harmonisation of water legislation, cross-border cooperation, a common environmental policy, the construction of road and transport infrastructure, and the promotion of public-private partnerships should contribute to increased competitiveness, job creation and investment, including from foreign operators. the resolution underlines the importance of tourism to the countries of the region and encourages them to promote a diversified and competitive tourism offer. the implementation of this principle would also benefit poles, including voters in my constituency, who often choose italy and the balkans as their holiday destination.

in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is a key instrument for deepening european integration, including by reducing economic, social and territorial disparities in all eu regions. the eu's current objectives for growth and development are largely reflected in the europe 2020 strategy. the resolution we have voted on is in fact a report on the mid-term review of the strategy, drawn up by the european parliament's committee on regional development, of which i am a member. the main conclusions and demands contained in the resolution concern the need for the continued involvement of the member states in the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and the linking of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) to it, while defining their subsidiary nature to cohesion policy, in particular the impossibility of any change in the financial allocations to the member states agreed under title 1b of the mff for the years 2014-2020 in response to the potential needs of this fund. the importance of eu investment policy for regional and national development was also underlined, and an appeal was made for the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy to be stepped up, given the delay in the current programming. i believe that the adoption of the resolution will have a positive impact on the effective implementation of cohesion policy and the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and will set the direction for the work of the other eu bodies in this area.
in writing. ‒ experience shows that the europe 2020 strategy and cohesion policy very often work side by side, although they should be very closely linked. this is best illustrated by the fact that the cohesion policy programming or reporting rules do not provide for mechanisms for flagship initiatives and the contribution of the european funds to their implementation. the european commission, in its review of the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, does not sufficiently address cohesion policy. the employment and social policy areas are clearly suffering, as the strategy's objectives of creating quality jobs and combating social exclusion are not sufficiently achieved through cohesion policy. of course, it is to be welcomed that the amounts allocated to these purposes are higher in the current programming period than in the previous one. however, this increase is not sufficient when we take into account the problems faced by most member states. the main problem with the lack of linkage between the two areas seems to be that they are prepared and implemented at different times. i therefore welcomed the report by fernando ruas on cohesion policy and the europe 2020 review, which highlights the opportunity offered by the mid-term reviews of cohesion policy and the europe 2020 strategy and the need to link the two areas even more closely.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is now closely linked to the objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive development set out in the europe 2020 strategy. the commission is currently working on a mid-term review of the strategy and is due to present further proposals by the end of 2015. i support the pursuit of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, in particular those related to the eradication of poverty and social exclusion and the fight against unemployment. i would remind you, however, that the structural funds have a specific task to perform, namely to support the regions, or more precisely to make up for the differences with the richer, more developed regions. i therefore warn against any attempt to 'blur' the original shape of cohesion policy and to treat the structural funds as mere instruments for implementing the 'europe 2020' strategy. i supported the report with this reservation.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is the eu's main investment instrument. it is a third of the eu budget. in view of the alignment of the structural and investment funds for the 2014-2020 programming period with the priorities of the europe 2020 strategy, cohesion policy should be seen as a very strong eu financial instrument contributing to the achievement of the strategy's objectives. the contribution of cohesion policy to the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy was also demonstrated in the previous programming period 2007-13. it is worth noting that following the 2008 crisis, cohesion policy was the only source of financing for growth policy in some member states or regions, due to the lack of public funding at national level. the need to fully implement the common strategic framework provided for in the common provisions regulation, which aims to achieve integrated development by coordinating the european structural and investment funds with other union instruments and with union policies in other areas. recent voices, particularly from southern european countries, are worrying about the revision of cohesion policy with a view to redistributing resources more to the countries most affected by the economic crisis at the expense of the less developed regions of central and eastern europe. such attempts to dismantle cohesion policy, which is intended to reduce development disparities rather than provide anti-crisis aid, cannot be tolerated.
in writing. ‒ article 23 of regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 in its first part provides for a procedure for reprogramming or optional suspension of the structural and investment funds. there are legitimate concerns that the linguistic interpretation of the standard could lead to a breach of the subsidiarity and partnership principles underpinning cohesion policy, as well as to macroeconomic instability, to the direct or indirect exposure of local and regional authorities to negative economic and social consequences or to the financial instability of regions in economic distress. the aim of this regulation was to ensure the most sustainable and effective cohesion policy possible, which is now largely implemented in the europe 2020 strategy. the current partnership agreements and programmes with the member states focus on the implementation of this strategy, so the application of article 23 in the adoption of a functional interpretation seems possible only in a situation justified by specific, exceptional circumstances. in view of my shared concern about the potential consequences of applying article 23 in practice, i voted in favour of the resolution, which seeks to ensure a reasonable and balanced application of the reprogramming procedure and to draw attention to the undefined role and insufficient participation of the european parliament in this procedure.
in writing. ‒ allowing countries that do not respect budgetary discipline to suspend funds, in accordance with article 23 of the common provisions regulation, is the most controversial provision of the package of regulations and one that i do not support. since it cannot amend this regulation, the european parliament shall endeavour to ensure that it is applied in the most reasonable and balanced manner. it is worth emphasising that the guidelines contained in the report relate only to the first part of article 23 and concern the optional reprogramming or suspension of the structural funds and the investment funds, and not to the second part on the mandatory suspension of the funds. in addition, the report stressed the need to reduce reprogramming to the minimum necessary and stressed that the specific and relevant economic situations of the member states must be taken into account when applying article 23. any request for macroeconomic conditionality should be transparent, justified and clearly favourable to the cohesion policy objectives of the region or regions concerned. i therefore supported the report.
rapporteur.– madam president, the recent financial and economic crisis has demonstrated that the european union economies are strongly interdependent and that national policies in one member state can have important spillover effects on other member states. we have realised that more coordination of national economic policies is needed within the eu in order to prevent imbalances, ensure convergence and exploit potential synergies. the european semester, introduced in 2011 within the six—pack, is the most important instrument for national policy coordination and surveillance in the eu. each year the commission undertakes a detailed analysis of eu member states’ budgetary, macroeconomic and structural reform plans and provides them with policy recommendations for the next 12 to 18 months. these country—specific recommendations (csrs) provide guidance and advice to member states on how to stimulate growth and jobs in conformity with the europe 2020 strategy, while at the same time avoiding excessive imbalances. each year the european semester cycle starts with the annual growth survey published by the commission in the late autumn, in which key policy priorities are specified for member states and the eu a whole. it is then followed by an assessment of draft budgetary plans and country report analyses. on that basis the commission proposes country—specific recommendations, which are then discussed with national governments and are then endorsed by the european council and adopted formally by the council. drawing on experience from the previous cycles, this year the commission has proposed to shorten and streamline the whole process in order to give member states more time to react and also to focus on key priorities. we welcome these changes, while underlining the fact that further action is needed to make the coordination process more efficient and less bureaucratic. this year, priorities focus on the most important growth drivers and include investment for growth and jobs, growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, structural reforms in the labour, product and services markets, and active employment policies. we support these priorities, but we think that more effort is needed to implement them effectively, especially in the area of structural reforms that are necessary for increasing potential growth in europe. these reforms should concentrate on removing barriers in the product and services markets and on making labour markets more flexible, while balancing this with the adequate protection of employees’ rights. equally important is the need to radically improve access to finance, especially for small and medium—sized enterprises, and to make the legal and administrative environment more friendly for businesses and to deal effectively with excessive indebtedness in the private sector. we share the commission’s view that continued fiscal consolidation is needed in member states with unsustainable debt levels and that strict compliance with eu fiscal rules under the reformed stability and growth pact is absolutely crucial for sustainable recovery. however, we also recognise that countries with sufficient fiscal space have the potential to further accelerate domestic investment. we also share the commission’s opinion that the actual implementation of csrs by member states leaves much to be desired. less than 15% of all csrs were actually fully implemented in 2014. thus the potential positive impact of coordination is seriously diminished. in this context, we call on member states to radically improve the implementation record through faster transposition, more active political support and, above all, strengthened national ownership. the european semester offers an opportunity for securing faster growth in europe and avoiding devastating crises in the future. i call on this house to support our report.
on behalf of the ecr group. - madam president! - i have to go. each year, the commission undertakes a detailed analysis of the member states' plans for budgetary, macroeconomic and structural reforms and makes recommendations to them for the next 12 to 18 months, and we in parliament also assess each year the state of play and the degree to which the member states have implemented the recommendations made to them by the commission. the european semester report analyses the overall economic situation in europe, the state of implementation of reforms and possible future economic initiatives of the union. if we want real economic improvement, we must have a frank debate about the changes that need to be made and admit openly that some of the steps taken so far in the european union or in individual member states have not had the intended effect. i'll say more, we have to admit to many mistakes as well. i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question. we are dealing with a clash of political views, not a documented analysis of the reforms needed. this will not achieve the desired effect and will allow the european union to become even more uncompetitive in relation to other economies in the world.

vice-president of the commission. – mr president, first of all i would like to thank members for this fruitful debate. parliament has an important role to play in the debating of european economic policies and the future of emu, so i have carefully taken note of members’ remarks and the points raised today. while different views and opinions were expressed during the debate, i note that there strategy. but i would emphasise that we are streamlining the european semester, we are trying to focus on key social economic challenges in the member states and we are applying the ʻtell only onceʼ principle, so we are not doubling some of the advice that we are giving to the member states in the context of other eu policies. the low csr implementation is a cause of concern. it is something we need to address, but we believe the best way to address this is through improved membership in the member states so that member states, stakeholders, national parliaments, governments and social partners are better involved in decision-making and are better informed about the economic challenges both at the euro area level and the eu level, and how it goes in a national context. then on some account surplus. we recommend strengthening investment and strengthening and stimulating the demand side of the economy. indeed the demand side of the economy is part of our economic strategy, so what we need to focus on is how to strengthen the economic recovery in europe, and of course the demand side is one of the answers. some questions were raised on the ambition of this current commission proposal and reference was made to some specific instruments, for example fiscal capacity. it must be noted that some of those elements were, for example, in the five presidents’ report where there is looking at ways of how to ensure stronger involvement of the european parliament in the european semester and macroeconomic policy decision-making, and indeed i sense also from today’s debate that there is some further work and consideration needed.

the next item is the debate on the oral question to the council by mr thomas händl, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the council recommendation on the integration of the long-term unemployed into the labour market (o-000121/2015 - b8-1102/2015 - (2015/2820 ((rsp))).
madam president! it is realistic to say that among the longterm unemployed there is a group for whom it is difficult or even impossible to motivate them to work, that they have no desire to improve their living conditions and that there is little that can be done for them. others, though, can be helped by using better methods. this requires a deliberate effort and the individualized application of sociological and psychological knowledge. the general training courses, such as computer skills or assertiveness, which are so often offered, are not appropriate. you have to train people in specialized fields, and that training should be much more individualized, i would say, intelligent. the way in which the effectiveness of employment offices and other training centres for the unemployed is assessed needs to be fundamentally changed. the measure should be the actual results in the occupational activation of the unemployed.
in writing. the problem of long-term unemployment affects all member states and the challenges associated with it are extremely difficult. i am all the more pleased that an attempt has been made to develop a comprehensive approach to this subject at european level. although the proportion of longterm unemployed varies considerably across the member states, the group is quite heterogeneous across the union and i believe that it is possible to develop a uniform strategy. i think it is important that the commission, alongside other activities, focuses on capacity building of competent, well-trained staff in public employment services. this is a very important issue, especially in the context of the creation of 'single points of contact' in many member states. this will be a new approach and the preparation of the points will require a considerable amount of time and resources for training. i look forward to the commission's further concrete proposals.
in writing. while many countries are trying to tackle longterm unemployment in different ways, the ideal solution to the challenge has not yet been found. i believe that, as with many other problems, the key issue in longterm unemployment is job creation. only if the european economy grows in a sustainable and stable way will we be able to improve employment rates. this is linked to the creation of a friendly environment for investors and businesses, and this is what member states should focus on. the second, equally important, issue is the provision of appropriate and personalised support for the longterm unemployed. more efficient and decentralised employment services are part of the answer to this challenge. it is also very important to activate the unemployed by addressing them with solutions tailored to their needs and to the situation in the local labour markets. in this context, structural reforms are also needed to adapt labour markets to new challenges, as well as, as has been emphasised so often recently, better cooperation between employment services and educational institutions. in addition to support and self-esteem, the long-term unemployed need the relevant skills and qualifications that are currently in demand in local markets.
in writing. continuing and intensifying action to tackle long-term unemployment is crucial, especially in view of the lack of clear progress in this area. in my country, the longterm unemployed account for almost 50% of the total unemployed. long-term unemployment often leads to poverty and social exclusion, further isolating people from the labour market. in the context of the fight against long-term unemployment, i would like to draw attention to the effectiveness of training programmes for the long-term unemployed. i am often approached by people who have completed numerous vocational education courses and who, despite having acquired many additional skills, are still unable to find a job. to counter such cases, we need more effective tools to activate the unemployed and support public employment services in this respect. the vocational programmes and training for the long-term unemployed proposed should take into account the possibility of practical training and traineeships in the field. this approach will allow the unemployed to validate their skills, gain experience often already required for the job, build self-confidence and thus increase their chances of getting a job.

the next item is the debate on the report by mr renato soru, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the reporting and transparency of securities financing transactions (com (2014) 0040 - c7-0023/2014 - 2014/0017 (cod)) (a8-0120/2015).
on behalf of the ppe group.– mr president, this new regulation will certainly bring an additional dose of transparency to the ways in which the financial sector functions. we will have a better view of what is going on in the shadow banking system – who transacts with whom, when, with what type of assets and under what conditions. this will certainly help market participants. i also trust that transparency might prevent activities migrating from the banking system to the less regulated non-bank system. in this respect i find it particularly important that information on the securities financing transactions entered into by funds – and i am thinking here of undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) and structured financial instruments (sfis) – is disclosed to investors. the good news is also that the three institutions agreed to use the opportunity of this regulation to make two amendments to the european market infrastructure regulation (emir). one will give the resolution authorities established after the entry into force of emir the right to access information retained in trade repositories. we all know the importance for resolution authorities of having good quality supervisory data. we have also made a technical change which is expected to make it easier for the commission to declare the supervisory arrangements of a third country as equivalent under emir. i am personally happy that we agreed on the exemption of smes from the reporting requirements: when they transact with a fund, a bank or an investment firm, it is the counterparty that will deal with reporting on behalf of both parties.

in writing. ‒ the main objective of these rules is to strengthen the supervision of securities financing transactions and to increase the transparency of these transactions. the rules are in line with international work in this area and require the reporting of securities financing, securities lending and securities borrowing transactions. that's why i corrected the report.
in writing. ‒ looking at current macroeconomic indicators, there are signs of economic recovery in eu markets. however, it should be stressed that its foundations are fragile, which has a negative impact on the eu's steady growth and international competitiveness. the eu's single market remains fragmented and lacks innovation. in some member states, there are persistent macroeconomic imbalances (high levels of public and private debt, large current account gaps, excessive risk in the financial sector). the persistently high unemployment rate in most member states is a worrying phenomenon. attention is drawn to the need for significant structural reforms, as well as to focus on creating the conditions for flexible labour markets, adapting education systems to labour market needs and shifting the tax burden from labour to other areas. in addition, the very low implementation rate of the recommendations for individual member states is to be noted, which makes it difficult to coordinate national economic policies with european recommendations. it should be noted that the number of countries under the excessive deficit procedure has decreased from 11 to 9 in the current year. the entry into force of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) regulation, which is intended to stimulate private and public investment in the eu, is a step in the right direction. the eu's business environment needs to be further improved and productivity levels raised by a balanced combination of public and private education and innovation policy.
in writing. ‒ long-term unemployment now affects 12 million eu citizens, or half of the unemployed. the long-term unemployed are 'difficult clients' of employment agencies, usually with low qualifications, a narrow skill range or unregulated residence and recognition issues, as in the case of immigrants; they have a harder time entering and remaining in the labour market. the necessary resources, such as personalised services and programmes, are expensive and not always available. despite the cost and scale of long-term unemployment, only 20% of the programmes to combat unemployment cover them. i therefore support the commission's guidelines to member states to improve the way in which long-term unemployed people are helped to return to work: individual assessment and counselling for those who have been unemployed for more than 12 months and a written agreement on vocational integration offering a concrete, individual plan for returning to work before 18 months of unemployment. in the context of these efforts, i would like to draw attention to the social economy and social cooperative institutions which effectively exploit the potential of the longterm unemployed and the excluded. an example of the use of this institution is the polish organization barka from poznan, which has helped thousands of excluded people in poland and abroad, bringing them back into the social mainstream through work. barka bases its method on social cooperative institutions and social support programmes built at the local government level. i therefore call for the wider integration of social cooperatives and the social economy into european policies to combat longterm unemployment.
in writing. ‒ the report on the civil use of remotely piloted unmanned aerial systems (rps), commonly known as drones, aims to ensure that any proposed eu regulation in this area is consistent with a global, harmonised and proportionate approach and is also developed with a view to risk taking, which will promote the safe use of these systems while not creating unnecessary burdens for industry. parliament stresses that technology originally developed for military purposes is now increasingly used commercially and provides significant societal benefits through the ability to carry out safety audits of infrastructure such as railway tracks, dams and power stations, natural disaster assessment, precision agriculture operations and media capabilities. there is a huge potential for growth in this sector, from the producer to the end user level, both for large companies and for a supply chain of thousands of smes, and any policy framework at eu level must be growth-friendly if european companies are to be globally competitive. parliament recognises the need to safeguard the public interest and stresses that while safety and security are of paramount importance in all actions and policies relating to the gsp, data protection and privacy are also of paramount importance in order to gain public acceptance for the development of this type of service. that is why i support the report.
in writing. ‒ remotely piloted unmanned aerial systems, or popularly known as drones, are a permanent part of our environment. from military to commercial to recreational use, the number of such unmanned machines is steadily increasing. new problems are also emerging that are not well defined. one of the most important is the safety of these machines. the cases of drone disruption are the most spectacular, but there are other areas that need to be regulated, such as the privacy concerns of drone users. despite legislative efforts by member states, it is necessary for the european commission to develop a legal framework that sets a european standard for the production and use of remotely piloted aerial systems. it is important to establish rules for the mutual recognition by member states of the privileges to fly such aircraft for commercial purposes. we need to create a system of registration of such machines which, in the event of a threat to life and health, will make it possible to identify the owner easily, also in another member state. it is necessary to establish a catalogue of technical parameters identifying drones intended for different purposes in order to make this distinction clear and understandable for both manufacturers and users. the report by ms foster sets out all these challenges in a comprehensive and precise way and draws clear conclusions for the commission. i voted to accept it.
in writing. ‒ the report is a contribution to the commission's deliberations to be presented at the ordinary meeting of the european tourism forum. it proposes actions in the areas of the sharing economy, digitalisation, sustainable and responsible tourism, and the promotion of europe as the main destination for tourist trips. it also calls for better cooperation between the member states and the commission. as regards the actions undertaken since 2010, the report requested the commission to report to parliament on the use of the structural funds and relevant eu programmes for tourism. the report stresses the need to promote, protect and preserve europe's cultural heritage. without prejudice to the separate budget line for tourism in the next multiannual financial framework and the initiative to create a european tourism agency, as another example of the growth of european bureaucracy, i decided to support the report.
in writing. ‒ europe is now the world's number one tourist destination. however, global trends in tourism are undergoing significant changes. europe is projected to be overtaken by other continents by 2030 as a result of globalisation. tourism in the eu is under strong pressure from other international tourist destinations, especially emerging and cheaper ones. tourism is the third largest economic sector in europe (generating almost 10% of european gdp). other sectors of the economy, such as agriculture, transport and culture, also benefit from tourism. tourism plays a significant role in job creation. it is also crucial for the economic recovery of those countries that have been particularly affected by the economic crisis. it also draws attention to the fact that tourism is an area where smes are particularly active. they make up 99% of the industry. the challenges facing tourism in europe are the effects of demographic change, high youth unemployment, changing consumer behaviour, the increasing demand for high quality customer service, the need for digitalisation. the european institutions should take action to attract new investment, to stimulate growth, to improve the business environment. european funds must support tourism in europe. the key issue seems to be to ensure a well-functioning single market for services. in addition, it is necessary to follow market trends and to take advantage of the opportunities offered by the digital revolution. digitalisation seems to be the key to the development of tourism.
in writing. ‒ a report produced by the european parliament on its own initiative highlights that europe is the main destination for tourists from all over the world it is estimated that by 2025 the number of visitors each year will reach 140 million. this is linked to the need for the european union to take action to promote the sharing economy, digitalisation, sustainable and responsible tourism and to promote europe as a top destination. to this end, it is necessary to strengthen cooperation between the member states and the commission and for the commission to report to the european parliament on the use made of the financial resources allocated to tourism under the structural funds and the relevant union programmes. it is clear to me that the tourism services sector in europe is developing very rapidly and that action is needed to promote, protect and preserve european cultural heritage.
in writing. ‒ the importance of tourism to the european economy is best illustrated by the figures. it generates around 10% of eu gdp and directly employs 13 million workers, not counting the huge number of seasonal workers. our position as the world's leading tourism provider is under threat, however, as globalisation and falling travel costs are giving other continents a premium. so we have to face this challenge now and find a way to maintain and strengthen our current advantage. an interesting tool that can help with this is a new tourism brand promoting europe as a destination for foreign tourists. the aim of the project is to develop a european tourism strategy that will be more effective and more efficient in terms of the promotion of tourism in the regions. we must also make better use of the unique cultural heritage of our continent, including its christian heritage. the tourism sector, including the resorts in the kujawy-pomeranian voivodeship, has the potential to attract large numbers of tourists from other continents. the internet and new technologies offer a huge opportunity to reach new customers with the european tourism offering, and the sharing economy offers new tools to take advantage of this offer. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on the digital single market and its impact on the tourism industry. i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ the resolution calls for action to be taken and improvements to be made to current air navigation systems, which do not allow for the timely identification and location of aircraft in distress. this was illustrated by the tragic flights of malaysia airlines flight 370 and air france flight 447. one technology that can be helpful in tracking flights outside the most densely populated areas where other types of ground-based aircraft tracking systems operate in a limited way is identified as ads-b (automatic dependent surveillance - alert) satellite technology. the international civil aviation organisation (icao) has requested the international telecommunication union (itu) to allocate the necessary radio spectrum band. parliament supported the commission's efforts to rapidly develop effective global flight tracking systems that would enable the location of public transport aircraft to be determined at any time, even in remote areas. the commission also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. the resolution calls on the commission to take the necessary steps at the world radiocommunication conference in 2015 to allocate the radio spectrum band necessary for this future global satellite flight tracking system. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ this decision establishes a programme for interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens (the 'isa2 programme') for the years 2016-2020, following on from the successful isa programme which is coming to an end. the main objective of the isa2 programme is to facilitate efficient and effective electronic cross-border or cross-sectoral interactions between european public administrations on the one hand and between european public administrations and businesses and citizens on the other. the modernisation of european public administrations and the enhancement of their interoperability are important in order to enable european citizens to benefit fully from interoperable e-services. such modernisation will contribute to the digital transformation that will make public services more transparent, efficient and user-friendly. the digital transformation of cross-border services is the next step towards the creation of a digital single market. the cost of the isa2 programme is estimated at eur 131 million. that's why i supported the resolutions.

in writing. ‒ the report provides for the harmonisation of rules on, inter alia, the visibility of european political parties, the introduction of a mandatory voting threshold of 3-5%; the introduction of the rule that elections end at the same time in all member states, i.e. at 21:00, the harmonisation of the minimum voting age of 16 years, and the guarantee of gender equality on the electoral rolls for the european parliament. this report clearly aims at the introduction of a uniform electoral procedure in the member states, as is explicitly stated in its content, and it interferes with the sphere of member states, which should be considered as a violation of the principle of proportionality. that is why i could not support this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the electoral law of the european union. the report aims to introduce several direct changes to the electoral act 1976. those changes are the harmonised ideas created in order to strengthen the democratic dimension of the european elections and to reinforce the functioning of the european parliament, as well as the governance of the whole european union. i find this report to be a fresh perspective and it is rather an interesting proposition which comprises several new, innovative factors. firstly, it covers the idea of improving the visibility of european political parties by placing their names and logos on the ballot papers, which is a simple strategy that may in fact prove to be very effective. moreover, it tries to introduce an obligatory threshold for the allocation of seats in single-constituency member states and constituencies which comprise more than 26 seats, ranging between 3% and 5% for member states using the list system. i believe that the provisions of the report will enhance the electoral equality of european citizens, which is one of our fundamental values.

in writing. europe is characterised by a highly fragmented energy market and significant differences in the state and capacity of energy and transmission infrastructure. despite the investments made at union level and by the member states themselves, although the situation is improving, it is not sufficient to have a real impact on europe's energy security and to ensure access to energy at favourable prices for consumers and businesses. eu strategies often place a strong emphasis on reducing emissions, given their environmental impact and the climate change that is occurring. however, this objective of union policy should not be misinterpreted as aiming to eliminate fossil fuels from the member states' energy mix as soon as possible, as this is not possible in the short term. excessive pressure and further restrictions on energy-intensive eu industries can only lead to a decline in their competitiveness and the relocation of production outside the eu, causing not only capital outflows but also the loss of hundreds of thousands of jobs. the union should pursue its emission reduction targets in a manner that is based on technological progress, allows for better use of certain resources and takes account of alternatives in long-term european and national strategies. we cannot make hasty decisions here that could weaken europe, block the development of the internal energy market and jeopardise the status of transit countries such as poland or ukraine.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament, the council and the commission agreed in 2003 that action was needed to reduce the number of eu rules, simplify them and make them more transparent. in order to achieve these objectives, the commission is, inter alia, implementing a regulatory efficiency and performance programme (refit). the activities of the programme shall focus on analysing existing union legal acts and identifying those which have become outdated, either by their temporal nature or by their incorporation into other acts. in its draft regulation repealing certain acts relating to the area of freedom, security and justice, the commission identifies a number of such regulations: 11 decisions of the executive committee on the common visa policy (sch/com-ex) and one council regulation, which are no longer needed because they no longer serve any purpose. i fully support the refit programme and believe that the outdated decisions and the regulation should be repealed. i am glad that the form of the act voted on has finally been changed from 'decision' to 'regulation', as regulations produce direct effects in eu law and do not require further bureaucratic efforts to implement them. i remain hopeful that the commission will continue the refit programme and that redundant and obsolete acts will be removed from eu law.
in writing. ‒ the european union institutions should ensure that the law is drafted in the best possible way, including by ensuring that it is transparent. unfortunately, there is often a lack of coherence in legislation, which is the absence of derogation from acts whose continued application is superfluous after the introduction of new ones or the absence of repeal of acts which have exhausted their legal effects. in its assessment of the schengen acquis and of the legal instruments in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters, the commission identified a number of legal acts which should be repealed on the basis of those criteria. these included sch/com-ex (93) 14, sch/com-ex (97) decree 13 rev 2 and sch/com-ex (98) 52, the latter of which was incorporated into the new act, while the subject matter of the first two was fully regulated in the new legal acts. the draft ep regulation on the repeal of certain acts of the schengen acquis in the field of police and judicial cooperation, other than those referred to by me, envisaged the repeal of council decision 2008/173/jha, which had exhausted its legal effects in 2013, and of decision sch/com-ex (99) 11 rev. 2 adopting an agreement which had never entered into force and remained in the legal system essentially without binding force. i voted in favour of the draft regulation, believing that this would help to make eu law more transparent and to reduce the scope of unnecessary provisions.
in writing. ‒ mr claude moraes, member of the european parliament, tabled a draft legislative resolution on the draft regulation of the parliament and of the council repealing certain acts in the field of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. i think this resolution deserves our support. it rightly proposes to reduce the number of provisions of eu law by repealing obsolete acts. the analysis shows that 7 earlier but still valid legal acts have already been incorporated into the subsequent solutions. this shall in particular apply to the exchange of objects and documents to be used in criminal proceedings. in addition, the previous provisions concerning europol staff are being abolished, as they have been replaced by the eu regulation on europol.
in writing. ‒ the draft regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing certain acts in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters is another document that aims to eliminate redundant regulations and outdated legal acts from the european legal system. with the entry into force of the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between member states and the 2009 council decision establishing the european police office (europol), some of the abovementioned material has been exhaustively standardised, while the derogation from the previously applicable provisions has been forgotten. the adoption of the regulation will have a positive impact on streamlining and increasing the transparency of the current cross-border police and judicial cooperation procedures. in addition to eliminating dead and obsolete provisions, the commission has proposed the repeal of the council framework decision on the european evidence order, arguing that it has lost its usefulness as it is currently only applicable between two eu member states. i think it is reasonable to take such a pragmatic approach to the issue of removing from the legal system acts that no longer serve any purpose. as a supporter of reducing the number of provisions in eu law and simplifying them, i did not hesitate to support the draft regulation.
in writing. ‒ the european union is actively involved in all fisheries organisations whose aim is to ensure the rational and sustainable management of marine resources and to combat illegal fishing. one such organisation is the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt) extended commission, in which the eu has had the status of a cooperating non-member entity since 2006. the ccsbt is responsible for the conservation and management of southern bluefin tuna throughout the area. the adoption of a resolution agreeing to the conclusion of the agreement will allow the eu to become a member of the ccsbt and to participate fully in its work. today, the eu as a cooperating entity is bound by, amongst others, the catch limits set by the ccsbt, on which the eu has no influence (the cooperating entities fully participate in the activities of the ccsbt but do not have voting rights). as vessels flying the flag of member states fish in the southern hake area, it is in the interest of the eu to become a full member of the ccsbt. in view of the above, i have supported the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the insurance mediation directive 2 (imd2). the proposed directive is a follow up to the former directive regarding the same matter called imd1. it is designed to ensure an equal playing field between everyone involved in the retail insurance market. the imd2 seeks to expand the scope of application of the former directive to all distribution channels. this is supposed to enhance the effectiveness of the insurance sector. furthermore, since the proposal covers the entire distribution chain, it is likely to benefit both consumers as well as retail insurance investors in the following ways: the most important change is the improvement in transparency. this means that insurance distributors will have to be more lucid about their prices, which will hopefully boost the level of competitiveness in this sector. also, the provisions of this directive seek to ensure the greater access to the information regarding all insurance products offered by the insurance dealers so that it will be unambiguous and clearer for the customers. all of the above is an interesting combination which will have a positive impact on each one of us as soon as it becomes real.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns the sale of insurance services. the newly amended title of the directive includes, by negotiation, intermediaries and representatives in the distribution network. insurance products, including car and life insurance, are also covered. in line with the existing principle of flexibility for commercial practices, questions arise as to whether or not insurance sales should be preceded by advice and whether member states will use systems of mutual referrals. therefore, consumers and retail customers will receive information on the price and costs of the insurance of the product concerned and whether the insurance seller has financial backing and receives orders for the sale of the product concerned. the commission will also be able to use the information provided by the member states to assess the impact of the new rules on the market for insurance products. it won't affect your life insurance. the issue for me was also the requirements for vocational training. introducing 15 hours of training per year is a more balanced and adequate proposal. i therefore voted in favour of the text of the report.
in writing. ‒ according to eurostat, the number of children at risk of poverty and social exclusion in the eu is increasing year by year. this problem is directly linked to social inequalities, which are exacerbated by, inter alia, inadequate and financially irrational public policy strategies implemented in many member states. in nine of them, including poland, even children from families with high work intensity are at risk of poverty. more than 20% of eu citizens are under 18 years of age, which should be a particular incentive to work towards improving their current situation. first, tackling child poverty should become a top eu political priority, which should then translate into the policies of national governments. it is worth noting that the europe 2020 strategy aims to reduce the number of people living in poverty by at least 20 million by 2020, and that this objective could be achieved by using the structural funds, which have so far been seldom used for such purposes. however, it is essential that member states are fully involved in trying to address this problem, which i believe should be expressed primarily in the development of national policies to combat child poverty at central as well as local government level. i voted in favour of the resolution because i care about the youngest citizens of the eu.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on reducing inequalities, with a special focus on child poverty. in the context of this report, i would like to draw particular attention to access to free, high-quality education for all as a tool to tackle social inequalities. providing children and young people with equal educational opportunities reduces the risk of marginalisation and social exclusion and provides an opportunity to improve their quality of life, employment and socio-economic status. it is also necessary to monitor and prevent early school leaving among young people, which contributes to the risk of social exclusion and poverty and is a major barrier to economic growth and employment. while the rate of early school leavers is falling across the european union, there are still significant disparities between countries and regions. in some member states, we are even seeing a worrying increase in this rate. i call on member states to increase investment in education and childcare. increased financial expenditure and its effective distribution to the areas most affected by child poverty will ensure optimal conditions for their further development and prevent any social and economic consequences of poverty.
in writing. ‒ the existence of significant social inequalities is a very serious problem in almost every country, not just in europe but also worldwide. poverty, lack of access to basic education, healthcare and transportation infrastructure mean that these inequalities are passed on from generation to generation and often worsen. according to the un convention on the rights of the child, 'all children should have guaranteed rights to education, health care, housing, protection, participation in decision-making that affects them, rest and leisure, a balanced diet and family care'. these are essential elements for the proper development of future generations, and spending on improving the living conditions of the youngest, even though it may seem costly to some, is in fact the best investment in their future. increasing member states' efforts to combat poverty, with particular emphasis on improving the living conditions and development opportunities of children, seems to be a necessary and urgent issue. this is evidenced by available analyses showing that the level of at-risk-of-poverty or social exclusion in the eu-27 increased from 26,5% to 28% between 2008 and 2012, and a 2013 eurostat study estimates that there were 26,5 million children living in the eu-28 at risk of poverty and social exclusion at that time.
in writing. ‒ the europe 2020 strategy aims to reduce the number of people living in poverty by at least 20 million by 2020. the very ambitious nature of the challenge requires action at all levels - eu, national and regional - to combat it as effectively as possible. the european parliament report indicates that more attention needs to be paid to the use of the structural funds to combat the alarming and growing rates of child poverty in europe. the report also stresses the need for member states to provide free and universal education, health care and social security for the poorest. i believe that this document accentuates the problems and challenges we face in the right way, which is why i have decided to vote in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the problem of child poverty is a multi-dimensional phenomenon and it is imperative that action be taken in accordance with the principle of the best interests of the child, which is fundamental to international law. the report makes recommendations to improve the financial situation of children and their healthcare, such as working towards more effective social support and universal healthcare. however, i do not believe that the report was prepared in a neutral worldview. i find it unacceptable that children's plight is used to promote the right to sexual and reproductive health. this formulation is unclear in the light of international law and in the face of strong tendencies to derive from it the right to freely and non-discriminatory decision about one's reproduction - and therefore also about when to terminate a pregnancy - cannot win my support. it surprises me that a report that is supposed to improve the situation of children reinforces the claims of those who want to avoid parenthood. in view of the above, i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i am aware that the marginalisation of certain social groups is a complex problem, often caused by factors other than discrimination. whatever the cause, this phenomenon cannot be underestimated. maintaining the status quo, i.e. leaving the issue of marginalised communities to local politics without additional financial support, is a short-term solution that only exacerbates the problem. it should be noted that, according to criminological studies, factors such as housing exclusion, education, unemployment and poverty create favourable conditions for demoralization and pathological behaviour, and often result in high crime rates among those exposed to these factors. attempting to help and, above all, educate people from marginalised communities will bring mutual benefits, both for these people and for society as a whole. i am aware that people from groups affected by the problem of marginalisation are often reluctant to give in to attempts to activate them in the labour market and to change their habits of living on welfare. but this should not be an excuse for not trying to help such individuals function normally in society. a particularly important point for me in the resolution is the call for linking national poverty reduction strategies with cohesion policy, which should result in a common strategy at eu level to reduce poverty, unemployment, exclusion of young people, children and disabled people, not only among marginalised groups but within society as a whole.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is the most important and costly policy currently pursued by the european union. its task is to bridge the gap between the most and least developed regions of europe. i would remind you that poland is currently the largest net beneficiary of the cohesion fund among all eu countries. the aim of cohesion policy is the integrated development of the regions, not only economically but also socially. this applies in particular to 'marginalized communities', such as roma minorities, but paradoxically there is currently no clear definition of such communities in european legislation. however, discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity, culture, religion and disability still occurs in the eu. however, this is the area in which cohesion policy can work to contribute to the elimination of all forms of persecution through an integrated approach in the economic and social spheres. the key to success is integration, which must come from both the minorities and the member states' authorities. partnership and mutual understanding are needed.
in writing. ‒ the report is intended to provide a basis for discussion on the future programming period for improving the living conditions of marginalised communities. in the end, however, the inclusion of marginalised communities will depend on strong political will on the part of local and territorial authorities and national authorities. the report points out that cohesion policy must address the key challenge of poverty and exclusion of young people and children, adults and people with disabilities. that's why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy aims to strengthen economic, social and territorial cohesion, reduce social inequalities, including reducing and eliminating poverty and exclusion. the existing eu funds, both the european social fund and the european regional development fund, are very important tools for the wider inclusion of marginalised communities. in its document, parliament not only highlighted issues that have been widely discussed, but also pointed to issues that have rarely been discussed, such as the marginalization of roma and other ethnic and national minorities living in the european union. furthermore, i also agree with the call for a coherent and common definition of marginalised communities that has been made in this report.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the role of the european union in the un. the committee on culture and education has prepared an opinion on this report. as a member of this commission, i have highlighted in my amendments the importance of education as an instrument for achieving the eu's foreign policy objectives, such as peace and stability in the world, sustainable development, intercultural dialogue and the fight against poverty both in the eu and worldwide. in this context, it is crucial to increase cooperation between the eu and the un to promote education for all, improve access to education, improve its quality and strengthen education systems worldwide. following up on the report, cooperation between the eu and the un should also be ensured in the field of education in the context of rescue programmes in the event of humanitarian crises, armed conflicts or natural disasters.
in writing. ‒ the future of the european union is linked to global peace, security, development and human rights, which are guaranteed by the united nations. for several years now, the union has been able to articulate its needs and concerns, and to submit proposals and amendments to the un general assembly, not only through its member states but also on its own. however, this law requires eu countries, especially those in the security council, to coordinate their positions within the un. this is particularly important now, when the conflict in ukraine, syria and the growing terrorist organisation isis pose serious threats to the security of our continent and the entire globe. it is also important that the eu and its institutions make a clear and strong call for global solutions to global problems, as no country can cope with emerging threats on its own in today's world. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the european parliament's document on the eu's role in the united nations.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on the role of the european union within the united nations in regard to how to better achieve eu foreign policy goals. due to the fact that the future of the eu is highly dependent on human rights development, security and global peace, i think it is important to strengthen the eu role within the un. the un is indeed a forum in which we can promote our biggest interests and values. the report lists several ways on how to contribute to the un work system so that it can have a positive impact on our society. the first interesting idea that brought my attention is to reform the security council. the reason for it is that such a reform will contribute to the better reflection of the new world reality and will cause the sc to be more effective in overcoming future challenges. moreover, provisions of the report focus on enhancing both eu coordination and cooperation in fields such as humanitarian aid and development. all of the above will hopefully strengthen our position in un and therefore globally.
