in writing. ‒ the joint draft general budget of the eu for the financial year 2016 has been approved by the conciliation committee. it is a good compromise and achieved without the 'dramatic' scenes and threats of rejection that have taken place in recent years. the overall level of commitment appropriations for 2016 is set at eur 155 billion. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation. under the flexibility instrument, eur 1.5 billion will be allocated to the security and citizenship strand and eur 24 million to commitments under the global dimension of europe strand. i am pleased that the issue of reducing youth unemployment remains a common political priority. it is important to make the best use of budgetary resources, in particular the youth employment initiative. in addition, the phasing out of the backlog of unresolved payment applications under the 2007-2013 cohesion programmes is an important point. efforts should be made to improve the monitoring of any outstanding accounts, in particular through the establishment of an early warning system. from 2016, the budgetary implementation status will be actively monitored and the budgetary measures will allow to reduce the level of accumulated end-of-year arrears to around eur 2 billion. i am pleased that the european parliament, the council and the commission will continue to summarise the state of play of payments and forecasts at special regular interinstitutional meetings.
in writing. ‒ europe is currently facing a number of challenges in a number of areas, such as the migration crisis, the current european security and counter-terrorism problem, and the ongoing russian embargo and crisis in the milk market following the abolition of quotas. in the face of numerous and highly diverse challenges, it is necessary to ensure that, in this period of uncertainty and insecurity, the union budget is sufficiently flexible and focused on clear priorities, designed to deliver concrete results. we should realize that few problems that arise suddenly will be solved so quickly. many of these require time and a series of specific actions over a number of years. for example, it is hard to expect that the migration challenge will be solved anytime soon. this problem will enter phases that are currently difficult to define and predict, when even their extent is difficult to estimate precisely. in the current situation, the focus should be on ensuring the security and adequate protection of the eu's external borders through joint action, information exchange and a coherent action plan of services in the member states. it is also necessary to have emergency funds available in the context of unforeseen expenditure.
in writing. ‒ despite the growing difficulties in financing the migration crisis, the european parliament and the eu council, representing the member states, unanimously agreed to increase the budget for 2016. the decision was therefore taken to allocate eur 4 billion to respond effectively to the increasing number of migrants coming to europe. however, the budget for the coming year also includes room for other priorities, in particular those relating to promoting growth and creating jobs. moreover, the ep's intervention will also provide more money for research and development, thus responding to the challenges facing the european union.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that the negotiations on the eu budget for 2016 have gone so smoothly this year and that a compromise has been reached. it also welcomes the increased funding for the erasmus+ programme as one of the priorities in the budget. this is an important signal that the eu is finding means to support youth exchanges with the eu and neighbouring countries. we have applied for funding for pilot projects and preparatory actions under title 3 and these have also been secured, albeit not fully. we are also gradually improving the ratio between current payments and already due commitments, making up for the backlog of previous years. this is very important. in the future, we should aim to increase the stability of proven projects, improve the duration of guaranteed funding perspectives and improve the funding of those projects that provide knowledge of the state of culture in europe and its funding mechanisms.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur calls on the commission to submit a new draft implementing decision which would reject all applications for authorisation to prepare soft pvc recycled preparations containing dehp. i think that objection would be disproportionate. it would also cover materials safe for recycling. furthermore, the question of form, i.e. whether parliament has any competence to object to implementing acts, is questionable. i believe that a threshold should be set up up to which the use of dehp can be considered safe and that strict rules should be established for monitoring the use of this phthalate. such a procedure would be in line with the recommendations of the opinion of the european chemicals agency (echa). there is also a need to discuss the use of dehp for industrial recycling, as the cost of producing new pvc is 28 times higher than the cost of producing recycled pvc. i therefore voted against the resolution not to grant authorisation without exception for dehp.
in writing. ‒ the report adopted today (24.11.2015) aimed to describe tax controls in eu member states and to make recommendations on this issue. this was the result of six months of intensive work by the taxe committee, including expert hearings and delegations to many member states, to explain how to interpret and apply national tax legislation. given that tax fraud and tax avoidance cause losses to the eu budget of around €1 trillion each year, the specific issues of corporate tax base erosion and aggressive tax planning practices have been examined in detail at international level. the globalisation and digitalisation of the economy have completely changed the way markets work. the majority of large companies today are cross-border in nature, requiring international tax rules, and corporate tax models were developed in the first half of the 20th century when such activities were limited in scope. the mismatch between national laws and legal loopholes facilitate tax evasion. in conclusion, both a tightening of national measures to combat tax fraud in the member states and a coherent eu position on the phenomenon are necessary.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the interpretation of tax law and other measures of a similar nature or effect because i am not in favour of introducing a common consolidated tax base. i particularly disagree with paragraph 170, which undermines the principle of unanimity in the council, because i believe that each member state should have a veto on tax policy. i regret that the european parliament has adopted a report which falls within the competence of the member states, in the direction of harmonizing tax law in the european union. uniform rules in this area are unnecessary and harmful to the competitiveness of the member states.
in writing. ‒ the recent tragedy in paris and other terrorist attacks in europe this year have shown that european citizens are often the perpetrators of attacks. it is estimated that over 5,000 of them have joined terrorist organizations such as isis and jabhat al-nusra. given the potential danger posed by individuals from extremist backgrounds, the european union should take decisive action as a matter of urgency to prevent further radicalisation of its citizens and persons temporarily staying within its borders. as you can see, the current repressive measures are not enough. the european parliament resolution on preventing radicalisation and the recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations proposes that preventive measures be used more widely. the need to improve the system of monitoring and information exchange on persons arriving from outside the eu and moving between member states and to analyse websites for the dissemination of content in support of terrorism was highlighted. the need for wider education of people at risk of radicalisation and dialogue between leaders of different communities is also an important point. recognising the complexity of the problem, the need for coordination at all levels, from local to international, was also emphasised. i believe that the adoption of the resolution will contribute to improving security in the european union and prevent the tendency for extremist attitudes to become more popular.
in writing. ‒ for years, the european union countries have been blind to the fact of the increased activity of islamic radicals. policy makers paralyzed by fear of political correctness didn't even have the courage to properly name the threat. this is evident in the debate and the report voted on today. like fire, he avoids the names islam and muslim. yet they are the backbone of most of the terrorist groups threatening europe today. if we can't get together to identify the threat and name it, how are we supposed to fight it? europe is itself weaving the rope on which it will hang in a few years' time. it opens up borders wide, but it can't control who comes into europe. the paris bombers were among the immigrants. they could easily cross the road from greece to the french capital. how many times have they received help and free rides from the authorities of successive european countries? they bought guns in paris. if the french people had more legal weapons, they could fight off the attack. today, instead of giving europeans guns to defend themselves, they are discussing how to limit their access to them. this bloody example shows that the most effective defense is to close the eu's external borders to migrants and at the same time to strengthen the monitoring of muslim communities in europe by increasing the number of weapons they possess. it is time for the european commission to take off its political correctness glasses and see the problem.
in writing. ‒ terrorism and radicalisation are both transnational and internal problems no eu country is immune from a threat that no longer comes from outside but from radicalised groups within the union itself. the fight against these phenomena can therefore only be effectively tackled through a common eu strategy, which must be based on prevention. if the union is to uphold the values that underpin integration such as the free movement of persons it must develop a strategy for responding early to radicalisation and hate speech and develop a policy for the promotion of tolerance and social inclusion. i agree with the author of the report on preventing radicalisation and recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations, who says that the internet has become a virtual training camp for radicals and a space for recruiting and radicalising potential followers. developing controls, with full respect for freedom of expression and the right to privacy, on hate speech content in cooperation with online companies is one element of the strategy. however, a systemic approach of early prevention by promoting tolerance for diversity through formal education, training and social campaigns across the union is needed above all. equally important is the pursuit of social justice policies to promote social inclusion and cohesion, which prevent exclusion from fostering radicalisation.
in writing. ‒ the recent tragic events in paris and the increased police and military action in the streets of brussels should make us all aware of the importance and the danger of the growing problem of terrorism. a phenomenon that can only be fought by acting together. one of the european union's core values and ideas is now very desirable common security. i am very pleased that this has been achieved, and that it has led to the drafting of a resolution on the prevention of radicalisation and recruitment of citizens by terrorist organisations. in voting for the resolution, i fully support its message and the concrete solutions it contains, which are a response to the phenomenon of acceptance by people of opinions, views and ideas that promote intolerance and often lead to extremism. it is estimated that some 5000 european citizens have left to fight for terrorist organisations in iraq and syria. therefore, our actions cannot be purely repressive. i want to express my approval for a strategy based more on prevention. preventive measures such as education, countering violent extremism and terrorist radicalisation in prisons and online, better information sharing on the subject, and strengthening links between the eu's internal and external security will be helpful tools in the common fight against terrorism. i am glad that parliament has once again taken a stand for the safety of millions of eu citizens.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's adoption of a resolution on preventing the radicalisation and recruitment of eu citizens by terrorist organisations by such an outstanding majority is a testament to parliament's unity in the fight against barbarism in our region and beyond. however, the measures proposed in the ep report must be implemented as soon as possible to be effective. the european parliament has adopted a resolution on the situation in the middle east, calling for the eu to take action to combat the spread of terrorism and to strengthen its capacity to combat terrorism. now both the member states and the other eu institutions must implement the recommendations written by the ep, otherwise we may find ourselves completely defenseless in the face of the growing danger.
in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attacks that have affected europe and the significant increase in the number of eu citizens with radical views, a project has been prepared to present the best ways to deal with this problem. one of the issues is the elimination of foreign fighters' travel within the eu. the recommendations address the issue of segregation in prisons, as well as the introduction of educational and community initiatives. international cooperation within the eu in the fight against terrorism, the exchange of practices that will help to counter radicalisation of opinion at a global level, is also important. the commission will also be able to provide information on the implementation of the eu's external borders policy, including on the implementation of the eu's external borders policy. it is worth mentioning here the mission of the internet companies. together with the uniformed services, they are tasked with detecting any online activity that is strongly linked to radicalisation. i voted in favour of the report because of the compromise amendments which have been made.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr christensen because i believe that a good compromise has been reached in the negotiations and that we will ultimately be voting on a text that addresses many of the key challenges facing employers in the field of osh. i am particularly pleased that the report has made room for two points. first, attention was drawn to the growing phenomenon of new and precarious forms of employment and their negative impact on the occupational safety and health situation, including the mental health of workers. secondly, i welcomed the fact that the report focused on the effectiveness of osh management in micro and small enterprises. it is clear that the level of protection of their employees must be as high as in larger establishments. however, we must realise that compliance with standards and requirements is more difficult for micro and small employers. i therefore believe that micro and small enterprises should be given special attention in this respect, and above all that the law on osh, both european and national, should be clear, transparent and easy to implement.
in writing. ‒ good working conditions that protect physical and mental health are a fundamental right of workers. it is common knowledge that the costs of prevention are much lower than the costs of treating occupational diseases, and therefore both undertakings and member states should take all measures to reduce the risk of occupational diseases. the european parliament's report rightly emphasised the need for the european commission, member states and businesses to work together to develop an eu osh strategy. in addition, it is important that the needs and compliance difficulties of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises are given special attention when developing the union framework for occupational safety and health, so that the legal framework does not become a significant obstacle to their development.
in writing. all forms of violence against women are undeniably evil and must be fought and prevented. this is a matter that we all share. what separates us is the choice of instruments. each member state has laws prohibiting violence and providing for penalties for the use of violence. i believe that new instruments such as the istanbul convention or the proposed eu directive on combating violence against women will do nothing to actually tackle the phenomenon of violence. instead, they're used to fight ideology against the traditional family, against the values that our civilization is based on, and to promote gender ideology. if violence against women is still a problem in our societies today, it is because no law can ever completely eliminate crime. but we can take action to reduce the scale of this phenomenon, which often increases in pathological environments characterized by unemployment, alcoholism and other social problems. by improving the living conditions of these communities, we can reduce the scale of violence, including against women. this is the best way we can help women.
in writing. despite the clear progress made in the area of gender equality, gender-based violence, the most radical form of discrimination, is a daily reality for millions of women in europe and around the world. violence against women is universal and affects all member states, and the european union as a whole should therefore develop a common strategy to combat it. the council of europe convention on preventing and combating violence against women, recognised as the gold standard of anti-violence policy, is one of the most effective legal tools in the fight against gender-based violence. the convention makes it clear that nothing, including religious or cultural elements, can justify violence, and prevention is rightly based on linking anti-violence policies with gender equality policies. the istanbul convention also guarantees the introduction of concrete, effective measures to combat violence, such as a 24-hour hotline and shelters for victims of violence or interrogation procedures to prevent secondary victimisation. the popularity of the convention is shown by the fact that 25 eu countries have already signed it, 12 of which have ratified it. in order to support and accelerate these processes, every effort should be made to ensure that the eu becomes a party to the convention. that is why, today, on the international day for the elimination of violence against women, i call on the commission and the european council to implement as soon as possible the plan already drawn up for the european union's accession to the istanbul convention.

priorities, impact – this is what the discussion on the budget absolutely must be on. we do have now in the new mff a better platform, because we have placed performance front and centre. we introduced performance reserve – 6% of the money we hold back, and if you do well, we give you more money. we have to work with our people in the commission and, of course, in the member states on a culture shift. this is not an easy thing, but it is a must if we are to be successful in making the best use of our taxpayers’ sacrifices. for every project, for every penny, we have to ask ourselves if this is the best use of money. i really appreciate each and every one of you who spoke in support of this rebalancing. it does not mean we turn our backs on compliance with the rules – not at all. rules are there to be followed. right now they are too complicated to be followed! we have multiple projects with thousands and thousands of people who have to grasp the concept of project management that we have introduced from the eu – a concept that may be easy for some, but it is certainly not easy for a small farmer or for an sme owner, so we have to work on simplifying the rules so they can be followed, and then we have to come with a hammer when the rules are not followed. i agree with those who have said that the persistence of the error rate is something that is undermining the credibility of the european union. we know why this persistence is there. rules are part of the problem, but so is how much commitment we build on to make sure that these rules are indeed followed. as i have said many times, we also have to find a way to reward those who take measures to correct errors, because this is what it is in the majority of cases – error, not fraud. proven fraud is 0.2% of our budget – 0.2% too much. i am not at all defending it, but what about the remaining 4.2%? how do we encourage people to do what the court tells us could be done if you take corrective measures and the error rate will go down? there we hit a problem, which is the multiannual nature of our programmes. when an error is detected in one year but only corrected in the next, that is not reflected in the error rate, and this is why in the commission we strongly recommend that we think about a residual error rate as an acceptable measurement, because if people take measures to correct, then that should be a positive thing. we should be saying bravo, we recognise you have done it. at the moment it is difficult to do it in a multiannual fashion. we are caught in this annuality in how we measure. finally, i do agree that we have to persistently balance performance and compliance. we should avoid the reasoning according to which focusing on performance is somehow interpreted to mean ‘oh well, compliance with the rules is not that important’ – it is important! let me finish with the question that was posed to me on ‘name and shame’. well, it is complicated as to which member states are performing the worst. if you look at the court of auditors’ report, there is a table that shows frequency of detected errors in audit sampling for 2014 for the member states. it is very clear that it varies from one area to another. in some areas some countries are doing better, in others they are doing worse. so i would be very reluctant to make general sweeping conclusions but rather say the following: we have to work with member states day in, day out, because at the end of the day, 80% of our money goes in shared management, and it is only when member states buy into being diligent and working with us that we can achieve that objective. finally, many thanks go to the court of auditors for the report that it has presented. a lot of it is something that has been coming up year after year, but we are now seeing a very welcome change of direction towards performance. we have, with this interinstitutional group, a very important task to see performance eye to eye, because the worst thing we can do is to have a different interpretation of what performance means and then get into not very productive arguments about who is right and who is wrong on what has been achieved in that area. so i very much look forward to working with parliament, the council and the court of auditors on giving a very clear direction for the commission – though the commission is not the most important actor – and for those who implement projects, so we get the european budget to serve our people the best possible way in the future.
court of auditors.– madam president, i would like first to thank you for the kind words addressed to the european court of auditors; on behalf of all those working there, thank you. your words encourage us to do better and to practise what you preach. we do that every day, so i want to reassure mr marinescu that we are doing that and striving for it. i am very pleased to hear from the vice-president that the commission greatly welcomes our call for a wholly new approach to the european union’s spending and investment. i am also pleased to see the broader consensus in this house on the need for that new approach. we simply cannot ignore the fact that it is a common task that needs interinstitutional cooperation from all institutions within member states, because it is the best possible way to tackle the financial challenges ahead of us. i stress the need to use the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework and to take it as a golden opportunity to make progress. members of parliament have raised a number of issues in their speeches. i will not address every one of them, but i am encouraged by their willingness to reach a greater common understanding of what a new approach means, what a culture of performance means, and what we are looking for. that is something which will not be done overnight and which needs to go hand in hand with simplification of the rules as well as with clear objectives. i have understood the call for ways of reconciling transparency and simplification. this needs to be addressed in the best way possible. we need simplification because debt is amplifying the risk of error, but we also need to be transparent so that we can then say what we are achieving with the funds we are investing. so we have to have, first and foremost, a clear overall framework that provides direction. but we also need to be aware that spending funds is always risky. i am sorry to say this so bluntly, but geography is not the root cause of the errors. as we have demonstrated, management modes are, likewise, not the main cause of the problem. the main reason for the errors that we have found, and for their persistently high level, lies in the way this house and the council decide on the legal framework for reimbursing costs. if you continue to have costs reimbursed on the basis of self-declarations by the final beneficiaries, then you will always have a higher risk of error. simplification does not mean forgetting about control. it needs to have cost-effective arrangements to ensure that we comply with the rules but, at the same time, we need to ensure that these are used to the best effect. then performance has a key part to play. what we are intending to measure is the interinstitutional work that we have to do. flexibility is also an important consideration, so some members estimate. i think that it is also vital to better address the backlogs which we have identified and which have been recognised on all sides. we need to use the budget in a more flexible way, together with all the financial instruments available, otherwise we will have funds committed but not being used. we know that at the end of 2014, the funds not yet used by all the member states for the structural and investment funds were of the order of 23% of the total. that situation is better today, i believe, but that means that we are not making full use of resources, and there are reasons beyond that. probably there are administrative capacities to develop. probably there is also a need for member state authorities to identify sustainable approaches that would make a difference to the lives of their citizens. in addition, a lot needs to be done to determine what makes a difference to citizens, for they will not think that building, say, a water-park is enough to make a difference. we need to see how sustainable approaches work and how they change citizens’ lives. i would like to conclude by saying that our call for a wholly new approach has to be followed up in interinstitutional dialogues, because that is the only way in which we can help to address the new challenges. it is the only way to tackle the long-standing issues that we have, but we need to take the opportunity afforded by the mid-term review of the mff to move forward. we look forward to contributing to the dialogue and we stand side by side with this institution, the european parliament, to further cooperate in that direction. but we cannot fail. if we miss this opportunity, we shall be failing to address the trust of citizens, and that is a crucial point in these times.
in writing. in its 2014 report, the european court of auditors calls for a new approach to the management and investment of eu funds. according to its guidelines, the budget should be better aligned with the community's long-term priorities and take greater account of possible crisis situations. in addition, the union should address the problem of financial backlogs without delay, in order to free up resources and direct them where they are needed. some member states still have problems absorbing the eu structural funds allocated to them. the total eu budget in 2014 is eur 142.5 billion, and the error rate for eu expenditure was 4.4%. however, the auditors considered that they had no objections to the reliability of the accounts and to the eu's revenue. they found the same estimated level of error (4,6%) for expenditure under shared management with the member states as for expenditure managed directly by the commission. the highest levels of error were found in expenditure under the headings 'economic, social and territorial cohesion' (5.7%) and 'competitiveness for growth and jobs' (5.6%). the lowest estimated level of error was in administrative expenditure (0.5%). however, the report stresses that more errors could have been corrected and calls on the commission to use its powers to further reduce the level of error and recover more of the funds wrongly spent.
in writing. the court, the eu's independent external auditor, is responsible for examining whether the collection and spending of eu funds is in line with the principles of economy, efficiency and effectiveness. this is particularly important in times of crisis, when the growing problems are followed by a natural decline in the confidence of europeans in the union in difficult situations. this is why systematically increasing the level of accountability and transparency in the process of overseeing the use of public funds is so important in order to rebuild this trust. close cooperation between the parliaments of the member states and the union's public auditors is also of great importance. in the process of building trust in the union institutions, the purposefulness of expenditure is essential, in addition to the pursuit of maximum transparency and economy. public funds must be used for the purposes that are most important to citizens. the european union budget is a major source of potential investment for many member states. they provide significant support for national initiatives not only to improve economic efficiency, but also to create jobs, secure borders and protect the environment. in order to best fulfil its tasks, eto should continuously analyse and draw conclusions from them. the call of the eto to adopt a new approach to the management of investments and expenditure of eu funds by introducing a number of significant changes in the activities of the entities responsible for the control of eu funds should therefore be welcomed.

in writing. ‒ the wto still faces many problems and unresolved issues, but it should be borne in mind that reconciling the interests of countries at different stages of development and often with conflicting interests is not an easy task. the abandonment of support for farmers and agriculture, especially in areas with difficult economic conditions, would lead to the depopulation of many areas and generate unemployment. if agricultural production is phased out and a part of the population moves away, it is much more difficult and costly to restore life in the region than to support local production and offer farmers additional forms of activity. agriculture in areas of natural handicap, peripheral and mountain areas also provides important environmental and climate services. in the context of combating climate change, it should also be noted that the specific nature of agriculture is that it not only emits greenhouse gases but is also responsible for absorbing and capturing huge amounts of them. we cannot forget the importance of agriculture to people's daily lives and the quality of the food they eat, as it relates to their health and lives and the environment around us. in the context of multilateral negotiations and the progressive liberalisation of world trade, we must not forget that agriculture is not just one of the sectors of national economies, but a supplier of products that are crucial to our lives and strategically sensitive.
in writing. ‒ the doha round was launched 15 years ago, and to date the wto countries have been unable to reach an agreement to create new trade opportunities and redress existing inequalities in the international trading system. the european union has always been a promoter of multilateral solutions and should therefore also lead the talks in the current negotiations. the early conclusion of the negotiations on the doha development agenda is particularly important in view of the existing and emerging non-tariff barriers that impede open and fair multilateral trade. moreover, for the first time, the wto has placed a particular emphasis on addressing the special needs and interests of developing countries, which are often unable to compete with the economic giants in a globalising world. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of the resolution and i believe that the ministerial conference in nairobi in december will prove to be a turning point.
in writing. ‒ the resolution sets out the objectives and tasks to be pursued by the international trade commission at the 10th ministerial conference of the world trade organisation in nairobi. the aim of ensuring that the trade facilitation agreement resulting from the previous wto ministerial conference is ratified by a sufficient number of states to enter into force was identified as a priority action. the agreement agreed at the 9th conference implements the demands of the 2001 doha round to create new trade opportunities, strengthen multilateral trade rules and correct existing inequalities in the trading system by focusing the negotiations on developing countries, in particular the least developed countries. i believe that it is important to make it easier for the least developed countries to access the international trading market, which will be a real opportunity to improve their economic situation, and i see the possibility of the european union having a positive influence on the final agreement. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the text of the proposed resolution.

in writing. animal welfare is a very popular issue of recent times and relates not only to breeding rules but also to the provision of comprehensive veterinary care to animals, including regular vaccinations, appropriate transport conditions and humane slaughter. this is the backdrop against which animal rights activists and producers are clashing. it is in the breeder's interest to sell as much as possible at the lowest cost, which unfortunately can lead to abuse in terms of inadequate housing or medical conditions. beyond the moral dimension of such actions, this may result in a lowering of the quality of meat and other animal products. it should be borne in mind that the more comfortable the animals are, the higher the quality of the products they produce. there is also the other extreme: if the highest possible standards were introduced and enforced, production costs would increase several times, leading to higher prices and consequently affecting consumers in the first place. it is necessary to analyze all the pros and cons of this case. only on this basis can legislation be drawn up to the benefit of animals, breeders and, above all, consumers.
in writing. ‒ 37 million children are currently out of school due to conflict and crisis. we now face the risk of entire generations being deprived of access to education, which could have serious consequences in the future, further increase in violence and ultimately escalation of further conflicts. at the same time, education is the most underfunded humanitarian aid sector in the world. it accounts for only 2% of all humanitarian aid. we need to break this vicious cycle and start investing in education, which is one of the fundamental rights of children around the world and is a very important tool to fight conflicts and crises. greater access to education leads to improved living standards, better economic prospects and the promotion of dialogue, tolerance and peaceful resolution of problems. it is estimated that increasing the proportion of young people with a secondary education from 30% to 60% could halve the risk of conflict. quality education is also a key to helping to combat radicalisation and extremism. through education, young people develop critical thinking skills, social and civic competence and respect for diversity.
in writing. ‒ the un estimates that one billion children live in conflict-affected areas and are denied their basic right to education. it is highly likely that, in the context of the current migration crisis, the number of children with limited access to education will increase. this is why it is so important to take action both within the union itself and in our external relations to help these children. it is certain that no country's economy can develop without a young and educated workforce. therefore, it is our duty to provide education to children in emergencies and in times of protracted crises, as they will be an essential part of the process of rebuilding societies in countries where conflicts have ended. parliament's resolution is a legitimate part of the eu strategy, which is why i decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on simplification in cohesion policy. although the results of cohesion policy are encouraging and lead to real growth and higher investment, i am convinced that these effects could be further enhanced if the administrative barriers that reduce the effectiveness of this policy were removed. the lack of trust between all the beneficiaries, the managing authorities and the european commission is undoubtedly at the root of many problems. i am convinced that greater flexibility, based on mutual trust between the various actors, would allow us to respond quickly and effectively to the needs that arise, and thus unlock the additional potential of cohesion policy. refinements and simplifications also require often unclear guidelines and rules, as well as the formulation of expectations from beneficiaries. these factors, which are not the result of badwill on the part of the beneficiaries, are often the cause of irregularities detected at the audit stage. i am convinced that the resolution voted today is an important step towards the much needed simplification and i hope that it will be implemented soon.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support the efforts to simplify burdensome financial procedures and management and reporting procedures in the implementation of the european structural and investment funds, which were part of the reformed cohesion policy for 2014-2020, while stressing that a sensible balance should be struck between simplification and ensuring effective financial control measures. i also support the creation of a new group of high-level independent experts to monitor simplification and the european commission's better regulation strategy as positive steps towards greater simplification. however, much remains to be done to improve legislation, support the e-cohesion system, identify good practices and, in the longer term, simplify the structures and processes associated with the european structural and investment funds. the areas of shared management, including implementation, management, reporting and control activities, continue to place an undue burden on both managing authorities and beneficiaries, including municipalities and small enterprises, and may have negative effects in terms of investment and absorption of funds. i therefore supported the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ despite the reform of cohesion policy and its significant simplification, the application, supervision and management of the funds remain problematic for both beneficiaries and managing institutions. the complex procedures may therefore discourage potential beneficiaries from using eu aid programmes. in its resolution, the european parliament rightly pointed to the need to promote the simplification of the rules on financial instruments under the european structural and investment funds in order to better adapt them to the needs of the beneficiaries, which could, in turn, contribute to an increase in their use. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the ep resolution.

in writing. construction materials change their original structure in a technological process. there's a decrease in the exergy of these material systems, accompanied by an increase in their entropy. therefore, restoring them to their original state would require additional energy, which would result in an unavoidable increase in co2 emissions. this is the case with steel produced by the recycling of scrap, which increases impurities, especially copper, which reduces its plasticity and increases its brittleness. this is the case with recycled thermoplastics, where the polymer chains shorten, leading to a decrease in strength. this is the case with complex materials, with electronic and composite scrap, which practically create waste that is not suitable for further processing. the history of technology provides numerous examples of technologies that were once used, but which were accompanied by significant waste, creating the large, currently exploited, dumps. such technological niches are already excluded. in conclusion, a circular economy, or a waste-free economy, is not simply recycling but a creative search for other uses for secondary raw materials, from their production use through the recovery of the energy contained in them to the permanent and useful deposit of residues, for example in the form of substrate materials.

in writing. the european year for development has a special role to play in communicating and actively engaging european citizens and civil society organisations in development aid and political dialogue. according to official figures, some 20 million eu citizens are personally involved in development ngos, some 130 million people donate to organisations helping developing countries, and 72% of the european public support the idea of helping the least developed countries. this is a good result, and it also shows that more and more people are understanding that development starts in their own country through mutual aid, fair trade, and participation in political processes. the key to the success of the previous thematic 'european years' was the close cooperation between the eu institutions and civil society, both at national and eu level. multi-level actions play a key role in shaping policy processes and should therefore be given the highest priority and receive sufficient funding. most of the official development assistance (60%) comes from eu member states, with some support from the eu budget. the establishment of a broad and all-inclusive civil society alliance should be pursued, which should, as in previous years, play a leading role in the planning and implementation of the european year of development.

in writing. the designation of 2015 as the year of development was linked to the expiry of the deadline for the millennium development goals, agreed by the world in 2000. it is also the time to set the sustainable development goals, the priorities for the coming years. one of the objectives of the european year for development was to campaign for eu citizens to learn how development aid is making a difference in countries that need it. it was also intended to demonstrate the european union's special commitment, as the world's largest donor of development aid, to combating poverty, climate change and protecting the earth's natural resources. not only the eu institutions but also the member states have been involved in promoting the year. information campaigns, conferences, events and debates were organised all over europe. and with digital and social media, the message has reached young people as well. it is important to remember that development aid is about building a safer and more prosperous world. over the past 10 years, eu funds have helped 14 million children go to school, more than 70 million people have access to clean drinking water and 7.5 million births have been attended by qualified medical staff, saving the lives of mothers and babies. the european year for development has, in my view, met its objectives and proved a success.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of eu, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of lichtenstein providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the report is designed to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. it represents a very important step in the ongoing efforts to eliminate tax frauds and tax evasion. according to that report, the eu and lichtenstein will be able to automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of each other’s residents. this is going to lead to addressing those situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide capital representing income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. due to the above, i believe that this is a very useful tool in combating the tax frauds, therefore i fully support the report.
in writing. ‒ in 2012, the european ombudsman launched an inquiry into the implementation by frontex of its fundamental rights responsibilities. the draft recommendations provide, inter alia, for the introduction of a mechanism for the submission and examination of individual complaints. the ombudsman's recommendations have been largely followed by frontex to date. its work has resulted in fundamental rights mechanisms such as the introduction of an incident reporting system, the development of codes of conduct, the establishment of a consultative forum on fundamental rights and the establishment of a fundamental rights office. frontex has also established a detailed procedure for dealing with internal reports of serious breaches of fundamental rights by its staff and invited officials. in addition, in the face of increasing humanitarian and legal challenges, frontex needs a mechanism to deal with individual complaints concerning alleged violations of fundamental rights. such a mechanism should be both efficient and cost-effective. frontex and the member states share responsibility for the actions of the officers involved in frontex's activities and are therefore invited to cooperate with each other in order to ensure the effective functioning of the complaints mechanism.
in writing. ‒ frontex has been in operation for over ten years, but many people are not aware of its existence. in addition, due to its lack of transparency and leadership, frontex has been criticised by numerous institutions and ngos, and more recently by the european ombudsman. as the ombudsman's report points out, there is strong evidence that frontex operations are not in line with human rights, and the current migration crisis has further highlighted this issue. among other things, many people trying to get to europe have been sent back, even though they should have been granted asylum. it is therefore important to take measures to increase the transparency of the agency, including through public access to information on the complaints mechanism in the context of the annual general report of frontex and the enhancement of the powers of the fundamental rights officer. the agency must also ensure a better balance between ethnic, national and gender diversity in its work. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the ep report and i believe that frontex will start the process of change as soon as possible in order to increase not only its effectiveness but also the degree of respect for eu fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the recommendations made by the european ombudsman in a special report on the obligations of frontex to respect fundamental rights. i believe that the european agency responsible for managing the union's external borders should create a mechanism to receive complaints about violations of the fundamental rights of migrants and refugees. this is particularly relevant today, with the growing number of humanitarian and legal challenges at the eu's external borders.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on sustainable urban transport because it contains numerous inaccuracies and gaps in the discussion of issues important for the introduction of sustainable transport in the eu member states. the promotion of sustainable transport is important, in particular for urban agglomerations. the development of sustainable mobility can have a significant impact on improving the environment, the quality of life and health of the inhabitants of european union cities, or contribute to climate protection. such initiatives are worthy of attention and support, but when they are developed, particular attention should be paid to the disparities in the innovation performance of the eu member states' economies. in this particular report, many key issues were left unanswered or simply left out. as a member of the european parliament, i could not therefore support the vote on an incomplete report whose legal, social and economic implications for the member states had not been fully analysed.
in writing. ‒ the communication presented by the european commission and the report discussed focus on environmental and safety issues. these are undoubtedly important issues, which is why i voted in favour of the report. however, i felt that there was no reference in these documents to the impact of sustainable and well-organised public transport on improving the labour market. we must not forget that for many people, public transport is the only means of transport to get to work. the effectiveness of measures to combat poverty and social exclusion is therefore determined by the development of public transport in urban centres and suburban areas. very often, the cost of commuting to work or the time it takes to get there is a barrier to getting out of unemployment. the problem is that these links are often not seen, both at local and eu level. if we are to achieve the europe 2020 goals of increasing employment and reducing social exclusion, we need to focus more on the development of efficient and sustainable public transport. this is important because it is projected that in the near future more than 80% of europeans will live in urban areas, and that this will increase the problems already existing today.
in writing. ‒ more than four-fifths of europeans now live in urban areas, and this proportion is likely to increase in the coming years, contributing to new societal challenges related to quality of life and sustainability. unfortunately, urban mobility still relies heavily on the use of conventional vehicles, which account for around 25% of co2 emissions in the eu. to reverse this trend, both the european union and the member states should take action to increase the use of public transport, carpooling and cycling by urban dwellers. it's a great project, not just for infrastructure, but for society. transport costs must be reduced and the number of cycle paths increased. the commission should therefore seek to coordinate and consolidate eu initiatives in the field of mobility, and member states should encourage their cities to take more environmentally friendly but also economically sound actions.

in writing. the commission, council and european parliament reached a final agreement at second reading on the trade mark reform package, which was formally approved by the plenary assembly on 14 december 2015. not only have the rules changed, but also the name of the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim) has changed, which will now function as the european union intellectual property office (euipo). trade mark-based industries account for 21% of all jobs and 34% of the total gdp of the union, according to research carried out last year by ohim and the european patent office. consequently, trade marks are now one of the most important market instruments for determining the position of the goods they designate on the market. a trade mark confers on its proprietor an exclusive right enabling him to prohibit third parties from using it in the course of trade. the reform of the trademark system was aimed at modernising the current system to keep pace with a constantly evolving market for the benefit of all users, and to stimulate innovation and economic growth by increasing accessibility for businesses. in conclusion, trademarks in the 21st century should be registered quickly and without unnecessary administrative burdens, while ensuring a high quality of service and a level of legal certainty. those amendments are complementary to the efforts to ensure the coexistence and complementarity of the union and national trademark registration systems.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the ecr group generally supports the european commission's initiative on trademark reform, which does not propose a new system but a targeted modernisation of existing rules. the aim of these activities is, inter alia, to align the terminology of legal acts with the treaty of lisbon, to organise cooperation between the office for harmonization in the internal market and national offices, and to rationalise the procedures for filing and registering community trade marks. i would like to take this opportunity to draw your attention to a number of important issues identified by the member states which have not been fully addressed in these reports. excessive fees for appeals and for an application for revocation may be a serious obstacle to eu citizens exercising their rights in the context of trade marks. in addition, the proposal to have the procedure for challenging the non-use of an earlier trade mark before a court may be a complication for some member states, resulting in a duplication of powers with the national patent office. as regards the budget surplus of the office for harmonization in the internal market, the ecr group considers that it would be more appropriate to transfer the surplus to the national ip offices for the purposes of promoting and developing the trade mark system. the proposals i have outlined would be very helpful to businesses, especially smes, as they can improve their competitiveness and market position.

madam president! although solidarity is one of the pillars of the energy union, projects such as nord stream continue to undermine this solidarity in the european union. we have repeatedly stressed that the nord stream project is a project that affects europe's energy security. today i would like to add that this project also poses a serious threat to the development of the ports of szczecin and świnoujście. the two existing nord stream pipelines are located at a depth of 16 metres, so larger vessels with a draught of more than 13,5 metres cannot enter the ports of świnoujście and szczecin. this prevents container ships and bulk carriers from being docked in świnoujście. moreover, the implementation of nord stream ii will perpetuate this situation and practically block further development of the port of szczecin and świnoujście. i therefore call on the european commission to assess the compliance of the nord stream gas pipeline with eu law, with the eu's energy objectives, including the principle of solidarity, and with the planned development of the baltic sea region's blue economy.
on behalf of the ppe group.– mr president, i welcome the communication by the commission on completing the european economic and monetary union. the document sets a very ambitious agenda for the future. it builds on the five presidents’ report and it proposes a set of measures that focus on four strategic fronts: building an economic union, a financial union, a fiscal union and a political union. i see this document as a proposal to fill the gaps that have been left in the european construction of economic governance and the gaps that have been made apparent by the recent crisis. these reforms are definitely necessary. the project is very ambitious, but it is necessary if the euro area is to survive and to flourish. it is necessary if integration and convergence are to continue to strengthen. we all know the status quo cannot continue because it is too prone to crisis. i think that the choice which is ahead of us is: either we go forward and build a genuine union, or we simply have to go back and return probably to national currencies. now, the key question here is: to what extent is this politically feasible? to what extent are all actors of this process – including this parliament and the commission, but above all the national governments – ready to go ahead under the current difficult political circumstances? this current political climate in europe is not very prone to far-reaching integration projects, but we are all convinced that this is absolutely necessary to move forward. in order to complete the emu, we all need more political ambition and more political determination. our political group is ready to cooperate on this front. blue-card question.– mr rosati, it seems that in view of the crisis – the creeping crisis – the resilience of countries which did not adopt the common currency is greater than that of other countries. it seems that only the most powerful countries of the eurozone are able to overcome the crisis successfully. the weaker ones have to share the asymmetric portion of their sovereignty. is it true?
blue-card answer.– the resilience of individual member states of the euro area has nothing to do with the common currency, but rather with the sort of macroeconomic policies they have pursued over the last several years. we see that within the euro area there are countries that fare perfectly well – these are mostly northern countries – yet there are other countries that, as a result of irresponsible policies in the past, have got into big trouble, so this is not a question of the common currency. the common currency gives quite a lot of advantages to those countries, but what we have to pay attention to is the pursuit of reasonable domestic policies.
of all the european union's projects, economic ones, such as the common market, are among the most successful. it is good that after years of misunderstanding, we are calling the single currency a political project. i leave it to the eurogroup to assess the merits of this project, its efficiency, especially in relation to cost. it is important that all member states of the european union, irrespective of the currency they have adopted, have equal access to the common market and its benefits. all the projects prepared by the presidents should be geared to this.
madam president, the eurozone’s challenges, both its architecture and its common governance, so far based on the intergovernmental approach, are often characterised by a too far-going respect for diversity of preferences and past—dependency thinking. rules in the institutions have been under improvement, but reforms have not yet reached a critical mass. we have to make further decisive steps on the institutions and rule reforms to make the governance system effective. but before this happens, sound fiscal positions in every jurisdiction and an unprecedented level of policy coordination at eurozone level are fundamental. in 2016 we will have to prepare for the ecb’s shift towards normal monetary policy in a way that will not lead to further contraction. to make it possible for the ecb to handle the transition to higher interest rates in a successful way, there is a need to have – on the fiscal and structural policies side of the eurozone – right, timely and well-coordinated reaction. it is worth recalling that over the last years we have had a bad experience of mr draghi’s calls for action by member states not resulting in support for his efforts. we cannot afford it this time around. let us use the opportunity created by the fact that the commission has presented eurozone recommendations six months before country—specific recommendations and that there is a eurozone working programme for the first half of 2016. full use of these two vehicles can give us an effective policy coordination.
madam president! in taking part in the debate on economic and monetary union, as a non-euro country, i would like to express my doubts as to whether the ambitious intentions of the so-called five presidents' report can be implemented in a time of serious economic problems in several euro area countries. i would like to point out that the countries of the union that have used their national currencies for several years have had both higher economic growth and, consequently, lower unemployment rates than most of the countries that use the euro. it is sufficient that these countries meet the two main fiscal criteria of maastricht i.e. a public sector deficit of no more than 3% and a public debt of no more than 60% which means the stability of their public finances and, consequently, stable economic growth and declining unemployment. i am of course in favour of closer cooperation within the euro area, i.e. the creation of further financial, fiscal and political unions, but i do not think that these will solve the main problems facing a growing number of euro area countries.
madam president! it must be welcomed that further steps are being taken to stabilise and develop the situation, but, with all the positive attitude towards the document we are talking about, we must also speak out about the issues that are questionable. first, i would include among them this unfounded belief in institutional solutions: if there is a problem, you have to create an institution, if there is an institution, you have to create another. here too, we have the proposal to set up new institutions, such as the european budgetary council, but above all, i have my doubts about the proposal to set up national competitiveness councils. i'm absolutely convinced that these bodies will be completely fictitious. the second thing is the pace of change. seven years after the crisis, the proposal is for a ten-year perspective in three stages. today, it is difficult to plan for even a short period of time, let alone a long one. ten years to make a decision is, in my opinion, a long time. third, the biggest, best guarantee of economic growth and protection against crises is a healthy and fair market. we have a problem with the single market, which is infected with the virus of over-regulation and protectionism. we must fight against this, and then it will be easier for us to create an economic and monetary union too.

in writing. ‒ a vote was held today on the report on the memorandum of understanding between the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim) and eurojust. the purpose of the protocol is to strengthen cooperation between the two institutions. the arrangements contained in the minutes are intended to contribute to the better performance of the tasks entrusted to them. one important provision is article 3, which states that the exchange of information or experience provided for in the protocol does not include the transmission of operational information containing data relating to a specific or an unspecified person. i welcome this provision, but i urge caution when implementing the data protection guarantee provided for in this article. the form of dispute settlement is also an important issue. the text of article 6 provides that disputes concerning the interpretation or application of the protocol are to be settled by consultation and negotiation between the representatives. this rules out third-party arbitration. this is consistent with most of these types of agreements. in the event of a serious breach of the provisions of the protocol or if it is considered that such a breach may occur, either body may temporarily suspend the application of the memorandum of understanding pending consultations and negotiations. the memorandum of understanding aims to develop strategic cooperation to help eurojust and ohim achieve their respective objectives. the minutes of the meetings in this form are in their mutual interest. as of today, it can be said that they are ready for this cooperation.
in writing. ‒ one of the key issues that the eu fisheries sector must focus on is ensuring the protection and optimal use of the environmental resources of the north-east atlantic. to this end, it was proposed to introduce the changes recommended by the north-east atlantic fisheries commission (neafc) into european legislation. the proposed amendments relate to two main issues: the alignment of the port state's measures to prevent illegal fishing with the provisions of the agreement concluded with the food and agriculture organisation of the united nations (fao) and the obligation to inform the port of destination of each vessel, even if it is outside the convention area. these actions aim to adapt eu law to the current challenges facing european fisheries, namely the need to maintain the biological balance in marine areas and to protect endangered organisms, including the highly popular atlantic cod, its close relative, the baltic cod (which is also endangered). these are necessary actions, but the question is, why is it only when we are threatened that we do so? should we not prevent the destruction of natural ecosystems rather than repair them? we must bear this in mind not only for the present state of affairs but also for future generations who may pay a heavy price for our laziness.

in writing. ‒ according to eurostat, electricity consumption per capita in kwh varies widely across the eu. commissioner cañete's statement that europe is overproducing energy is statistically correct. however, the problem is that it is not evenly distributed, and this is not only due to the lack of interconnections. cross-border connectors are not able to solve this problem completely. only future trans-european networks linking east and west will improve peak energy efficiency, and those linking north and south will make the use of res (wind in the north and solar in the south) relevant in europe. the lack of holistic grid designs pushes the vision of a real, long-term electricity market in europe ad calendas graecas. by designing reliable interconnections within the eu itself, we cannot cut ourselves off from our neighbours' energy systems. given that the interconnection of national systems is only the first, if not the most optimal, step towards eu energy solidarity, i voted in favour of this report.

ladies and gentlemen! i am very pleased that we are unanimous in opposing the patenting of plant and animal varieties. the european parliament already made a clear statement on this issue in 2012. however, recent decisions to patent plants have raised the question of whose interest it is to patent plant and animal varieties. who bends the law to make a profit? i think that the european parliament and the commission should defend the rights of farmers and livestock farmers. article 4 of the directive clearly states that the granting of patents on plant and animal varieties is excluded, and i therefore call on the commission to react quickly and effectively to this matter, because that is what we are called upon to do to defend the rights of farmers and breeders.
mr. chairman, please! ibrahim halawa was 17 years old when he was convicted, along with 494 others, of attacking national security forces during protests in cairo. he's facing the death penalty. in recent years, the number of death sentences in egypt has increased significantly. twelve people have been executed this year. halawa has exercised his democratic right to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly. his trial was postponed several times. after the last such ruling, this young man went on a hunger strike. he and the other defendants are entitled to a fair, open and impartial trial in accordance with international standards. he was also restricted from receiving correspondence in english. there are suspicions that he may have been tortured. i call on the egyptian authorities to stop the widespread violation of human rights, to acquit ibrahim halawa, a citizen of the european union. egypt must also ratify the 1986 convention against torture and abolish the death penalty.
mr. chairman, please! the human rights situation in egypt is a matter of great concern to the international community. egyptian authorities ignore basic civil liberties, including the right to assembly, protest, and freedom of speech. irish teenager ibrahim halawa has been held in a cairo prison for more than two years, and is one of 500 other prisoners of conscience. he's facing the death penalty. officially, the process cannot begin for organizational and logistical reasons. no courtroom in egypt can accommodate the record number of defendants. on the day of his arrest in august 2013, the military and police stormed the mosque in ramesses square where several hundred protesters had taken refuge, killing 97 people and arresting the rest. condemning the restriction on the right to freedom of association and expression, we call on the egyptian authorities to release immediately all prisoners convicted for fighting for civil and political freedoms. according to article 10 of the universal declaration of human rights, everyone is entitled to a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal. in egypt, there is still a lack of respect for this principle.
in writing.– the case of mr ibrahim halawa is considered to be in breach of both international law and human rights. mr halawa is potentially facing the death penalty. according to the egyptian authorities mr ibrahim halawa, who is an irish and egyptian citizen, is guilty of exercising violence and direct involvement in killing several civilians, and therefore is tried in accordance with the egyptian law. moreover, the egyptian authorities claim that all of the accusations directed at their legal system and the fact that they are breaching international law are invalid and that the egyptian judiciary is considered to be an independent and just unit. however, i find this to be not exactly true. apparently, the defendant is being kept in a court in a soundproof cell, which means that he is denied his right to follow the allegations. moreover, the potential death penalty is a breach of the right to life and the situation should be handled by people who have respect for human rights. mr halawa, even if guilty, should be given a just, unbiased trial by the independent judiciary without a threat of facing the loss of his life.

mr. chairman, please! the monetary unification of europe has caused a very serious economic crisis. it has hit some countries hard, but it has also led to the political disintegration of our cooperation. political reason would have us back off from such a policy, but the european union authorities only want to use this crisis to push even harder, even harder, to confiscate the sovereign competences of the nation states. this will only cause a greater political crisis, as the british position shows. this is not only in the interests of our peoples, but unfortunately it is a sign of serious political irresponsibility. but it's your choice. we choose to be sovereign.
in writing. ‒ the package of proposals adopted by the european commission on 21 october this year marks the beginning of the first stage in a series of actions to complete the construction of economic and monetary union. the commission is certainly to be commended for its efforts to develop the eu economy and to improve public finances. the document included many important demands, such as a change in approach to the european semester, the creation of a banking union and a more coherent representation of the euro area in international institutions. unfortunately, in addition to the important solutions, the document contains many proposals that may raise doubts. one of these issues is the misplaced belief in the miraculous power of institutional solutions. it is proposed to add to the existing bodies at european and national level, such as the national competitiveness councils. the european parliament resolution rightly highlights the commission's positive actions to strengthen economic and monetary union, while highlighting the problems with the implementation at national level of certain budgetary and fiscal reforms and the lack of proper coordination between the commission and parliament. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the theses set out in the report by christian preda on human rights and democracy in the world in 2014 and the eu's policy in this area. i agree that fundamental freedoms and human rights, such as freedom of speech, freedom of assembly, freedom of association and the principle of non-discrimination are constantly threatened and violated, and human rights defenders often pay a high price for their activism, in extreme cases, the price of their lives. i particularly strongly support the comments in the femm opinion attached to the report, which recalls women's rights as an important area of human rights and the need to mainstream women's rights in politics and the economy. i agree with the report's assertion that respect for human rights is an attribute of mature democracies and that fundamental freedoms and democratic values are at the heart of the european union's identity and underpin all its policies. these values are not given once and for all, they are constantly challenged and violated, which is why it is so important to take the right steps and create a legal framework for them, such as the strategic framework and the new european agenda for human rights and democracy, launched in 2012, which talks about integrating human rights issues into the eu's external policy and its relations with the entire external world.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report on the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world 2014 and the european union’s policy on the matter. the report states the importance for the european union to make the most out of the policy tools that are at our disposal in order to promote and protect human rights and democratic principles not only within the eu, but worldwide. moreover, the text considers the necessity for effective implementation of the new eu action plan on human rights and democracy 2015-2019. this is particularly important, because if we manage to do so, it will create the channels for joint global human rights actions and therefore enhanced respect for human rights. i believe that the report highlights the crucial role of international cooperation in the field of human rights and democracy. furthermore, it fully supports eu engagement in organisations such as the un or oecd, and that support is exactly what we need in order to promote human rights.
in writing. ‒ the dayton peace agreement obliged the parties to the conflict, namely the bosniaks, serbs and croats, to immediately cease hostilities and withdraw their armed forces from the designated demilitarised zone. this agreement brought to an end the bloodiest armed conflict in europe's postwar history. it should be noted, however, that the dayton agreement became the foundation on which the entirely new and extremely complex institutional structure of bosnia and herzegovina was built. within a single state, there are two autonomous units, ten cantons and 147 municipal councils, which means four levels of government. this is of course compounded by the country's ethnic division into three ethnic groups: bosniaks, serbs, and croats. each of these groups has numerous opportunities to block the decision-making system, which de facto leads to the paralysis of the state. this is why it is so important to support local political leaders in the difficult process of modernising the inefficient, inefficient and inconsistent institutions in bosnia and herzegovina. without a stable political system and an efficient and competent public administration, it is difficult to imagine the gradual integration of the country into the european union.
in writing. ‒ i am very pleased with the report presented. the eu's arms exports are worth €40 billion a year, including €28 billion to third countries. if you look at the global arms trade, 36 percent of that trade is in the eu. it is therefore entirely appropriate to assess each year whether the member states of the european union apply strict criteria to the arms trade. unfortunately, as the report indicates, this is not the case, and weapons exported from the eu also end up in the wrong hands. this requires not only tougher criteria for arms exports, but above all, close monitoring of who is the end user of arms. the primary purchasers are basically buying guns legally. the problem is that later, these weapons are often resold and end up in the hands of the wrong people. this is the weakest point in the implementation of the eu arms export policy.
